title: Program Manager, GRC
description:
About the role

Riot Platforms is building its Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) function across three pillars: Risk Management, Governance, and Compliance. The team supports contractual commitments for ISO 27001:2022 certification and SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II attestations, as well as Riot’s SOX obligations.

The GRC Program Manager will partner with GRC leaders to build the processes, plans, and reporting needed to coordinate this work across business units and sites. Assigned to the Senior Director or a GRC Director, you will manage initiatives against established deadlines and help maintain audit readiness.

This individual contributor role relies on collaboration and follow-through. You will work across Finance, Legal, IT and Security Engineering, HR, Procurement, and Operations to drive progress and accountability without direct authority.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on program manager who can build processes, navigate GRC requirements, and deliver in a fast-moving environment.


What you'll do

  • Build and improve GRC processes. Partner with GRC leaders to establish the program charter, roles and responsibilities, intake and prioritization processes, meeting cadences, escalation paths, and standards needed to turn GRC strategy into repeatable execution.
  • Drive cross-functional engagement. Lead working groups and coordinate with Finance, Legal, IT and Security Engineering, HR, Procurement, and Operations to integrate GRC requirements into day-to-day work.
  • Manage plans and deadlines. Own the roadmap and schedule for assigned initiatives and help maintain a coordinated enterprise GRC schedule across ISO 27001:2022, SOC 1, SOC 2 Type II, and SOX IT general controls (ITGC).
  • Coordinate certification and audit activities. Work with GRC leaders, control owners, and auditors to track gap remediation, control implementation, evidence readiness, and audit schedules as sites and business units come into scope.
  • Support year-round audit readiness. Help establish and operate consistent processes for evidence ownership, collection, naming, quality review, and retention.
  • Track and report progress. Develop and maintain dashboards and metrics for control-owner timeliness, evidence readiness, remediation aging, policy attestation, and other program priorities. Prepare updates for GRC leadership and the Audit Committee.
  • Deliver assigned GRC initiatives. Work alongside GRC leaders to build and operate processes such as policy review and attestation, remediation and finding tracking, risk management workflows, and control testing schedules.
  • Identify and resolve obstacles. Surface schedule, resource, and control risks early; coordinate follow-up; and escalate issues with options and recommended next steps.
  • Measure program maturity: define and report compliance KPIs such as control-owner timeliness, evidence freshness, remediation aging, and policy attestation rates, and build the executive and Audit Committee dashboards that show progress against target.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years of program or project management experience, including at least 3 years managing GRC, IT audit, security compliance, or risk initiatives.
  • Experience supporting GRC, compliance, or related programs in a data center, colocation, or critical infrastructure environment, such as energy, utilities, or digital asset mining.
  • Hands-on ownership of the program plan and timeline for at least one ISO 27001 certification or SOC 1 or SOC 2 Type II audit cycle—not solely evidence collection.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, SOX IT general controls (ITGC), and NIST CSF, with the ability to translate control requirements into actionable plans.
  • A track record of delivering complex, cross-functional programs against certification, regulatory, or contractual deadlines, with measurable results.
  • Experience preparing clear, accurate reporting for executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to coordinate work and drive accountability across teams without direct authority.
  • Experience building or establishing processes in a fast-moving environment.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including status reporting that distinguishes planned, in progress, complete, and verified work.
  • Experience using GRC platforms, such as Vanta, Drata, Hyperproof, ServiceNow GRC/IRM, or OneTrust, and work management tools, such as Asana, Jira, or Smartsheet.

Preferred:

  • Relevant certifications: PMP, PgMP, or equivalent project management credential. GRC-specific credentials—such as ISO 27001 Lead Implementer, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, CISA, or CRISC—are strongly valued.
  • Public company audit coordination: Proven experience operating in a publicly traded company, collaborating directly with Internal Audit and independent external audit firms.
  • Greenfield program build: Demonstrated experience standing up a GRC PMO, operating model, or cross-functional delivery cadences from scratch.
  • Executive and committee reporting: Familiarity with preparing status reports, risk summaries, or presentation materials for executive leadership and the Audit Committee.


Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: $115,000 - $145,000 (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant.
  • Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans.
  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.


Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Technisch Facilitair Medewerker
description:
In deze hands-on functie ondersteun je zowel het dagelijkse onderhoud van onze faciliteiten als de technische gereedheid van onze maritieme trainingsomgeving. Je werkt met trainingsapparatuur, praktische trainingsinstallaties, gereedschappen en andere technische middelen. Je voert inspecties en kleine reparaties uit, biedt eerstelijnsondersteuning bij technische problemen en helpt ervoor te zorgen dat onze trainingsfaciliteiten veilig, functioneel en klaar voor gebruik zijn.

Jouw verantwoordelijkheden

  • Uitvoeren van algemeen gebouwonderhoud, kleine reparaties en preventief onderhoud.
  • Inspecteren, testen en ondersteunen bij het onderhoud van technische trainingsapparatuur, praktische trainingsinstallaties en andere technische middelen.
  • Bieden van eerstelijnsondersteuning bij technische storingen en complexere reparaties afstemmen met interne teams of externe specialisten.
  • Voorbereiden van leslokalen en technische trainingsruimtes en ervoor zorgen dat apparatuur gereed is voor trainingen.
  • Ondersteunen bij de installatie, vervanging en het onderhoud van facilitaire voorzieningen en trainingsapparatuur.
  • Beheren en onderhouden van gereedschappen, persoonlijke beschermingsmiddelen (PBM), reserveonderdelen en technische verbruiksmaterialen.
  • Signaleren van technische gebreken en opvolgen van benodigde reparaties en onderhoudswerkzaamheden.
  • Coördineren en begeleiden van externe leveranciers en monteurs die werkzaamheden op locatie uitvoeren.
  • Bijhouden van controlelijsten, storingsregistraties en eenvoudige onderhoudsadministratie.
  • Bijdragen aan een veilige en betrouwbare werk\- en trainingsomgeving.

Ervaring & profiel

Wij zoeken iemand met:

  • Minimaal 3 jaar relevante werkervaring in facilitair onderhoud, technisch onderhoud of een vergelijkbare praktische functie.
  • Brede technische kennis en kennis van gebouwonderhoud, waarbij je in staat bent kleine reparaties zelfstandig uit te voeren.
  • Ervaring met technische apparatuur, gereedschappen en installaties en het vermogen om technische problemen te signaleren en op te lossen.
  • Een praktische, proactieve en oplossingsgerichte instelling.
  • Goede organisatorische vaardigheden en het vermogen om zowel gepland onderhoud als onverwachte technische problemen te prioriteren.
  • Goede computervaardigheden, waaronder Microsoft Office.
  • Je spreekt uitstekend Nederlands en kunt je goed redden in het Engels.
  • Bij voorkeur een geldig rijbewijs.
  • Een BHV\-certificaat, VOP (NEN 3140) en VCA\-certificaat, of de bereidheid deze certificaten te behalen.

Wat bieden wij?

Werken bij CSMART betekent werken in een unieke, internationale maritieme omgeving in Almere. Naast je salaris bieden wij een uitgebreid pakket aan arbeidsvoorwaarden, waaronder:

  • Een salaris tussen €3.000,- en €3.500,- exclusief vakantiegeld op basis van een fulltime dienstverband.
  • 8% vakantiegeld.
  • tot 25 vakantiedagen per jaar op basis van een fulltime dienstverband.
  • Een volledig door de werkgever betaalde pensioenregeling van 11%.
  • Een reiskostenvergoeding van € 0,25 per kilometer voor woon\-werkverkeer van en naar CSMART.
  • Toegang tot mogelijkheden voor professionele ontwikkeling en LinkedIn Learning.
  • Toegang tot de fitnessruimte van het CSMART Hotel.
  • Korting op ontbijt, lunch en diner in het CSMART Hotel.
  • Toegang tot Carnival cruise benefits na één jaar dienstverband.
  • De mogelijkheid om bepaalde Nederlandse feestdagen om te wisselen voor een Custom Leave Day die voor jou persoonlijk betekenisvol is.

Selectieprocedure
Solliciteren kan tot 24 november 2026 om 18:00 uur, of totdat we voldoende sollicitaties hebben ontvangen.
Na het sluiten van de vacature worden alle sollicitaties beoordeeld. Alleen kandidaten die aan de voorwaarden voor de functie voldoen, worden geïnformeerd over de uitkomst van hun sollicitatie.
De selectieprocedure bestaat uit:
  • Een eerste gesprek op locatie
  • Een tweede gesprek op locatie
  • Een voorwaardelijk arbeidsvoorstel
  • Een arbeidsovereenkomst
Let op: sollicitaties van kandidaten die niet aan de essentiële voorwaarden voor deze functie voldoen, waaronder het recht om in Nederland te wonen en werken, worden niet in behandeling genomen.

title: Full-Stack Engineer — Real-Time Recommendation Engine
description:

You will collaborate with data, algorithm, and business teams to shape personalized content strategies, design experiments, and ensure robust, scalable, secure systems. Remote-friendly with strong growth opportunities.

title: Quality Assurance  Coordinator- Education Services
description:
Who We Are

For over 60 years, Abilities First, Inc. has been empowering individuals with developmental disabilities to live their most vibrant, independent lives. From early education to adulthood, our wide range of services—including preschool and school programs, day and residential habilitation, community connections, and employment services—are designed to uplift every individual’s unique strengths and dreams.


We believe in the power of people—of every background, identity, and ability—to create change and build a more inclusive world. Abilities First is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is welcoming and supportive of people of varying abilities, races, ethnicities, religions, socio-economic status, gender and gender identities. At Abilities First, you’ll join a mission-driven team that values collaboration, celebrates individuality, and is dedicated to meaningful work. If you're ready to turn your passion into purpose, we’d love to welcome you aboard


Who We Need

Abilities First is seeking a Quality Assurance Coordinator for Educational Programs. The QA Coordinator is responsible for monitoring overall service provision throughout Abilities First’s educational programs in accordance with agency philosophy and policy, Corporate Compliance Plan, and various state oversight agencies that monitor Abilities First. The primary focus of the Quality Assurance Coordinator for Educational programs is the creation and implementation of our auditing procedures in compliance with OCFS and NYSED requirements, with secondary responsibilities related to quality improvement throughout the school/preschool programs. The Quality Assurance Coordinator is responsible for assisting school administrators in developing quality on-site orientation programs and profession


Schedule: Monday through Friday, 40 hours per week based in offices located in Orange County with ability to travel to Dutchess County sites for training and as needed.


Pay Range: $26.25 - $28.25 per hour.


Responsibilities include:

  • Develop an understanding and maintain up to date knowledge of regulatory requirements of all agency State Oversight Agencies, including but not limited to OPWDD, NYSED, OCFS and OMH. Provide information and support to programs as needed to achieve compliance when there are changes.
  • Creates and implements an Educational Services audit protocol and compliance program that aligns with regulatory requirements as outlined by the appropriate state oversight agencies. Conducts internal audits of all designated programs as outlined Internal Audit Policy, monitoring program areas to ensure the needs of students are being met through meaningful activities and interactions as well as comply with State and Federal regulations and agency policy and procedure.
  • Provide verbal and written feedback to appropriate parties, completing written reports on findings.
  • Provide recommendations to programs based on outcomes, requests responses and plan of corrective actions when needed.
  • Works collaboratively with Quality Assurance team to triage any reports received and make recommendations, where applicable.
  • Assist in the review, documentation, and investigation of all allegations of abuse and neglect, reportable incidents, notable occurrences, Part 625 events and situations, and non- reportable incidents, adhering to all required timelines. For OPWDD events, this includes the use Incident Report and Management Application (“IRMA”) and the NYS Justice Center’s Web Submission of Investigation Reports (“WSIR”) application.
  • Will actively participate and present in committees including but not limited to local incident review for designated program(s) and incident review committee for the overall agency.
  • Takes an active role participating and presenting to the Corporate Compliance Committee.
  • Offer technical assistance and guidance to staff as well as follow-up monitoring activities at the location if indicated in order to improve quality of education and/or compliance issues.
  • Responds to reports of compliance concerns, referring to other responsible parties when necessary.
  • Assist with agency training by teaching designated curriculum topics to new and/or existing employees, either during orientation or during required refreshers.
  • Provide training to appropriate staff as identified in routine monitoring of program sites.
  • Communicate effectively with various team members to foster teamwork and a positive environment that meets the needs of the people we support.
  • Communicates effectively with individuals and their families to enhance relationships and ensure satisfaction with the services provided by the agency.
  • Maintains strict confidentiality of sensitive data and information obtained.
  • Adhere to agency Code of Legal and Ethical Behavior, which require all employees, consultants, board members, volunteers, and affiliates to perform their responsibilities according to ethical and legal standards with honesty, integrity, fairness, good faith and respect for others and the law.
  • Ensures all required trainings and certifications required are current, and seeks further support and training where needed.
  • Follows all agency policy and procedures and demonstrates continuous regard to personal safety and the safety of others.
  • Will incorporate core competency concepts of person-centered excellence by respecting people’s concerns and responding accordingly and will use “teachable moments” to assist people in understanding and exercising their rights.
  • Performs other appropriate job-related activities as requested by supervisor or as circumstances warrant.

Perks & Benefits:

  • Time to Recharge – Paid vacation, personal, sick, and holidays
  • Health & Wellness – Medical, dental, and vision plans to keep you covered
  • Plan for The Future – 401(k) with employer match and employer-paid life insurance
  • Level Up Your Skills– Tuition reimbursement and online training through the College of Direct Support (and to boost your earning potential)
  • Get Paid When You Need It – On Demand Pay gives you access to earnings as early as the next day
  • Exclusive Extras – Employee discounts with Verizon, AT&T, Royal Carting, and more

title: Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform - Go/Python
description:
Senior Consultant, Tax Content Architect - LATAM (ARG, CL, CRI, MX)

Cargill is committed to providing food and agricultural solutions to nourish the world in a safe, responsible, and sustainable way. Sitting at the heart of the supply chain, we partner with farmers and customers to source, make and deliver products that are vital for living. Our 155,000 team members innovate with purpose, providing customers with life's essentials so businesses can grow, communities prosper, and consumers live well. With over 160 years of experience as a family company, we look ahead while remaining true to our values. We put people first. We reach higher. We do the right thing-today and for generations to come.

JOB PURPOSE AND IMPACT

The Senior Consultant, Tax Content Architect will focus on technology implementations, governance and enhancements of tax elements in enterprise resource planning (ERP) and improvements of tax processes within the LATAM region. With limited supervision, this job develops tax solutions and advice on tax requirements in ERP systems. In this role you will work in close liaison with the wider tax team and connect with the technology deployment, sustain & optimize teams, collaborate with DT&D to contribute to efficient tax determination and resulting reporting processes.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • TAX SOLUTIONS: Support the tax technology implementations (ERP and applications), including the gathering of local tax requirements with country or regional tax experts, assisting on the initial design process, performing analysis, testing and assisting on the creation of trainings following a go live.
  • TAX ERP ANALYSIS: Support with building and the maintenance of tax requirements in ERP systems and tax dedicated applications, following a standard tax methodology to gather and meet tax requirements.
  • TAX ARCHITECTURE: Assure that the tax requirements are designed, documented and implemented in a consistent manner across all areas within tax using the Tax Methodology, including assisting with the controls in the ERP space, such as the monitoring of tax logic in ERP.
  • TAX LIASON: Collaborate with other tax content architects and tax managers to come to a joined solution.

QUALIFICATIONS

MINIMUM

  • Minimum requirement of 5 years of relevant work experience.
  • Fluent English language skills - written and verbal

PREFERRED

  • Strong analytical skills to embed tax requirements in ERP systems or applications.
  • Good understanding of tax reporting requirements as well as the basic understanding of statutory requirements and configuration in current technologies.
  • Basic understanding of tax functionality in enterprise resource planning systems
  • Experience within or good understanding of an international tax/finance environment.

Important: The candidate must be based in Rosario (Argentina), Coronel (Chile), San José (Costa Rica) or Mexico City (Mexico).

title: Supervisor, Comprehensive Care Advocacy
description:
HealthPartners is hiring a Supervisor, Comprehensive Care Advocacy (CCA). This position exists to provide leadership and supervision for a team of Case Managers/Care Coordinators, including hiring, orientation, performance monitoring and staff development in order to effectively meet the goals of the program. Provide day-to-day consultation and support to staff with questions, issues, and challenging cases. Monitor the work and workload of all team members, including case audits and reports to identify opportunities for coaching and/or quality improvement. Lead Quality Improvement and process improvement activities at the individual team level and across teams.

ACCOUNTABILITIES:

Leadership:

  • Responsible for the supervision of staff, including having the authority to hire, transfer, lay off, promote, discipline and discharge, train, reward and review performance of employees. Ensures compliance to organizational and departmental policies and procedures.

  • Build effective relationships throughout the department and with other partners in care, and inspire staff to achieve excellence in the daily operations of Case Management.

  • Embrace change. Create an environment that encourages creativity, independence, and willingness to change in Case Management team members.

  • Consistently apply HealthPartners organizational and department values (missions / vision / initiatives) and continuous quality improvement principles in relationships, daily work, and program supervision.

Member Focus:

  • Ensure all staff, processes and programs are member-focused, resulting in high levels of member/patient/family, colleague and team member satisfaction.

  • Thorough knowledge of how to access and understand member benefits / coverage / payor information.

Relationship and Team Building:

  • Establish and maintain good working relationships within Case Management Department, with other HealthPartners departments, to facilitate excellence in Case Management processes and outcomes.

  • Create and maintain a cohesive Case Management team by facilitating a collaborative, respectful, diverse environment.

Program Supervision and Evaluation:

  • Become an expert on all program workflows and regulatory elements, seeking additional education as needed.

  • Evaluate current processes to identify needs and opportunities to improve the Case Management program.

  • Work with Program Manager, Case Management, to ensure implementation of new department programs and initiatives in a timely and effective manner.

  • Work with Program Manager to ensure compliance with Medicare / Medicaid contract requirements and regulations.

  • Monitor for education/training needs. Once identified, facilitate implementation of training for appropriate staff.

  • Review and consult on complex cases as identified by program criteria.

Staff Selection and Development:

  • Provide supervision, guidance, coaching, and development of staff.

  • Provide ongoing performance feedback to staff members, and complete annual reviews on a timely basis.

  • Complete one on one meeting and site visits with staff to evaluate performance to ensure compliance with Case Management policies and procedures promoting consistency with care coordination activities.

  • Recruit and select new staff in coordination with Program Manager, Case Management.

  • Orient new staff with ongoing evaluation of orientation process.

  • Monitor staffing and recommend adjustments to Program Manager as needed.

  • Promote staff development in assignment of special projects, ongoing independent study, education-related professional activities, and professional affiliations to maintain and increase knowledge in the areas of Case Management.

  • Review feedback from Patient Satisfaction Surveys and Service Recovery logs and share this with staff including coaching as appropriate.

Communication:

  • Communicate with members, families, physicians and staff to facilitate successful daily operations of the Case Management Program.

  • Maintain confidentiality of information in accordance with department and corporate policies.

  • Collaborate with internal departments, according to co-management principles for patient-centered care.

Technology:

  • Maintain knowledge of and effectively use automated applications and systems.

  • Understand the data and reports available to maximize their use and value.

  • Implement strategies to ensure efficiency and productivity through proficient use of automated systems by Case Management staff

Personal Development:

  • Participate in ongoing independent study, education-related professional activities, and professional affiliations to maintain and increase knowledge in the areas of Case Management.

Other Duties:

  • Participate in various committees, task forces, projects, and quality improvement teams, as needed and assigned.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Current Dimension:

  • Reports to Program Manager, Case Management.

  • Directly supervises Case Management team consisting of professional case managers.

  • Interacts with medical, administrative, and front line staff within the organization.

  • Supervises daily operations of program serving HealthPartners members.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Registered Nurse with current license in the State of Minnesota (BSN preferred) OR LSW Social Worker for MSHO or MSC+ (LISW preferred).

  • Certification as a CCM, CMC or equivalent certification, with achievement of certification within 18 months of employment.

  • Minimum of 3 years clinical practice experience.

  • Minimum of 3 years experience in case management.

  • Demonstrated effective leadership and supervisory skills.

  • High level of expertise in written, oral, and interpersonal communication.

  • Demonstrated skill in effective use and management of automated medical management systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to function independently and cooperatively.

  • Understanding of healthcare and/or HMO industry.

  • Demonstrated experience in hiring, orientation, coaching, and team building of professional staff.

  • Demonstrated flexibility and organization.

  • Demonstrated appropriate decision making under challenging situations.

CHALLENGES:

  • Maintaining focus on the desired mission and vision while effectively responding to a rapidly evolving environment.

  • Influencing team members and colleagues to work collaboratively in achieving the goals and objectives of the Case Management program.

  • Facilitation and implementation of interdependent, cross-divisional processes and strategies for successful change, with compliance to regulatory, accreditation, and customer requirements.

  • Supervising staff during significant change and rapid implementation.

DECISION-MAKING:

  • Make independent decisions within the scope of this position’s accountabilities and determine the need for and the timing of consultation with leadership and/or Medical Director.

  • Use professional clinical judgement, organizational knowledge, industry knowledge, and common sense in determining appropriate alternatives for members/patients/families, consulting with senior leadership and/or Medical Director, when indicated.

  • Assist with the development and implementation of the Case Management/MSHO/MSC+ programs. Make recommendations to leadership regarding policy development and/or changes.

  • Identify and communicate variances from customer, regulatory, and accreditation requirements, and ensures action is expediently taken to achieve necessary level of organizational competence.

title: Lähihoitaja Ihotautien vastaanotto
description:
Haluaisitko tehdä hoitotyötä ihotauteja sairastavien potilaiden parissa sekä olla osana tiimiä, jolla on tärkeä rooli potilaslähtöisen hoidon toteutumisessa? Olet tervetullut ja toivottu jäsen työyhteisöömme, jossa työskentelet tasavertaisena ja osaamistasi arvostetaan. Toivomme tehtävän aloitusta viimeistään 11.1.2027 tai sopimuksen mukaan.

Yksiköstämme

Haemme lähihoitajaa vakituiseen tehtävään Tulehduskeskuksen Ihotautien vastaanotolle. Aloitat työskentelyn valohoitotiimissä. Valohoitotiimissä annetaan erilaisia valohoitoja, kuten UVA, UVB ja PUVA. Lisäksi työtehtäviin kuuluu ihon paikallishoidon ohjausta ja tarvittaessa siinä avustamista. Työhön kuuluu myös ajanvaraus- ja puhelintyötä. Osaamisen karttuessa työtehtäviä laajennetaan myös muuhun yksikön toimintaan, esimerkiksi vastaanottotyöhön. Työskentely Ihotautien vastaanotolla tarjoaa hyvän oppimisalustan ihotauteja sairastavien potilaiden hoitotyöhön. Työ on päivätyötä, arkipäivisin klo 7.30–15.30 välillä. Potilaat tulevat hoitoon ajanvarauksella. Työpaikka sijaitsee Iho- ja allergiasairaalassa Helsingissä.

HUSin arvot kohtaaminen, edelläkävijyys ja yhdenvertaisuus toteutuvat toiminnassamme. Kohtaamme potilaat ja työyhteisömme jäsenet kunnioittavasti hyvässä keskinäisessä vuorovaikutuksessa. Olemme saaneet kiitosta osaamisestamme kohdata potilaat sekä hyvästä ilmapiiristä työyhteisöissämme. Potilaat hoidamme yhdenvertaisesti, heidän tarpeisiinsa vastaten. Työyhteisöissä meillä on yhdenvertaiset oikeudet ja velvollisuudet.

Tarjoamme sinulle

Uusien työntekijöiden tueksi olemme laatineet kattavan perehdytysohjelman. Sinulla on tukenasi kollegoiden, kokeneiden asiantuntijoiden sekä esihenkilöiden tuki. HUS tarjoaa työntekijöille monipuolisia etuja esim. alennuksia hyvinvointipalveluihin ja liikuntakeskuksiin. Lisäksi käytössämme on ePassi-etu, jota voit hyödyntää työmatka-, liikunta-, hieronta- ja kulttuuripalveluihin. Lisäksi HUS tarjoaa henkilöstölleen vuokrattavia työsuhdeasuntoja.

Tehtäväkohtainen palkka on 2777,91€/kk ja mahdolliset kokemus- ja muut lisät.

Toivomme sinulta

Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

Overview

We have an opportunity for a C1 to join the Critical Energy Resilience Unit to lead the Scottish Government’s response to challenges associated with downstream oil resilience, and ad hoc business continuity issues in the oil and gas sector. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who has extensive experience in cross government engagement in the pursuit of securing alignment between UK Government and Scottish Government priorities for transitioning industries. This role is also suited to someone who has a proven track record of working with external commercial advisers to devise and implement a response to businesses in distress, ideally in the energy sector. Lastly, this role is suited to someone who thrives when engaging with SCS and senior Ministerial level to secure outcomes that deliver on the priorities of the Scottish Government and represent value for the taxpayer.

The Critical Energy Resilience Unit is one of four units within the Energy Industries Division and leads the Scottish Government’s approach to securing Scotland’s energy security and resilience. Through often high pressure, high profile and time sensitive activities, the Unit develops policy and through partnership working seeks to meet the needs of Scotland in relation to energy security.

Scotland remains reliant on a range of energy sources to ensure functioning of society, public services and the economy. The Critical Energy Resilience Unit works across a range of external partners, extensively with the UK Government, other Scottish Government departments and external agencies to develop and implement plans in relation to energy security. The Unit also has responsibility for leading the Scottish Government’s approach to distressed energy intensive businesses across Scotland including spearheading engagement with business leaders, commercial advisers and enterprise agencies.

The work of the unit is high profile, with significant levels of political, stakeholder and media attention, and are cross-cutting in nature as they interact with wider energy strategy, climate change and economic objectives across Directorates. There is therefore an expectation of regular and extensive out of hours working including in response to crisis situations. There is likely to be some expectations of travel.

This role is central to providing Ministers with assurance and support on the full range of energy resilience issues with particular lead on gas, road fuels and leading inter-governmental and cross governmental planning and assurance activity.

Responsibilities
  • Lead Scotland’s approach to ensuring security of supply of road fuels and the development of contingency plans in the event of shortages and catastrophic events
  • Lead Scotland’s approach to ensuring security of supply of gas and the development of contingency plans in the event of shortages and catastrophic events
  • Provide leadership to supporting Ministers across all energy resilience issues including leading the unit’s work of briefing, product development and planning.
  • Lead cross government engagement on issues of energy resilience

title: Production Coordinator

title: AMR Regional Crisis Manager
description:
Do you instinctively know when to take action? Do you excel in high-pressure situations? Then a career at Apple might be for you. As part of Apple’s Global Security team, you’ll safeguard our most valuable assets—our people and innovations. Working alongside a dedicated team, you’ll develop and implement crisis management strategies to protect Apple’s operations, employees, and assets across its facilities and global supply chain, ensuring resilience against emerging threats and disruptions.

You’ll play a key role in Apple’s Crisis Management team, which follows a Prepare, Coordinate, and Respond approach to support colleagues and business operations during critical situations. Success in this role requires expertise in crisis management, tactical problem-solving, and strong stakeholder engagement.

Prepare: • Apply deep knowledge of security risks—geopolitical, operational, and natural disasters—across the AMR region (North, South and Central America) to design, implement, and test crisis response procedures and protocols. • Maintain established relationships with law enforcement, government agencies, and security professionals across the region. • Deliver executive-level presentations and public speaking engagements. • Support the development of the Crisis Management Training Program and delivers crisis preparedness training—both in-person and virtually—to Crisis Response Teams (CRTs) across AMR.

Coordinate: • Partner with Apple business units to enhance Crisis Management (CM) programs and support growth initiatives. • Build relationships with senior stakeholders to integrate CM into business operations. • Develop a comprehensive understanding of Apple’s assets across business units.

Respond: • Lead crisis response efforts in AMR and globally when needed. • Provide clear, well-informed assessments and maintain composure under pressure. • Make critical decisions in high-ambiguity situations. • Lead Apple’s crisis response to various incidents, deliver situation reports, and guide teams through crisis response plans. • Work with key stakeholders to drive effective resolutions. • Quickly identify and assess risks to Apple during incidents. • Brief cross-functional response teams and executives on unfolding situations and response actions. • Communicate with Apple employees through appropriate channels during crisis events. • Conduct post-incident reviews, assess decision-making effectiveness, and implement improvements.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in crisis management or a related field
  • Extensive experience working with law enforcement or security vendors
  • Global perspective in addressing crisis challenges
  • Experience developing and implementing proactive crisis response plans
  • Experience creating high-quality presentations and delivering impactful training to support crisis management initiatives
  • Ability to distill complex information into clear, concise communication
  • Able to travel domestically and internationally up to 50% of the time

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree preferred or equivalent experience in a related field
  • Strong understanding of the full spectrum of security risks in AMR, with specific experience in film/television production security and crisis management within production environments
  • Strong track record of delivering on commitments and acknowledging mistakes when necessary
  • Exceptional attention to detail and standards
  • Ability to assess and test local response capabilities and CRT readiness

description:
Olisitko sinä meidän osastomme uusi sydän Diagnostiikkakeskuksessa, Jorvin kliinisen neurofysiologian yksikössä (KNF)?

HUS Diagnostiikkakeskus on Suomen johtava kliinisten laboratorio- ja kuvantamispalvelujen tuottaja. Pääasiallinen toiminta-alueemme on HUS-yhtymän erikoissairaanhoito ja HUSiin kuuluvien hyvinvointialueiden perusterveydenhuolto. Vastaamme myös Kymenlaakson hyvinvointialueen ja Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialueen laboratorio- ja kuvantamistoiminnasta.

Toimimme kahdeksalla lääketieteen erikoisalalla. Vastaamme valtakunnallisesti useista erityisosaamista vaativista tutkimuksista sekä yliopistolliselle sairaalalle kuuluvasta tutkimuksesta ja opetuksesta. Diagnostiset tutkimukset ovat keskeisessä roolissa sairauksien varmistamisessa, poissulkemisessa, osana hoitoa sekä hoidon seurannassa ja seulonnassa. HUS Diagnostiikkakeskuksessa työskentelee noin 3500 laboratorio- ja kuvantamisalan asiantuntijaa yli 170 toimipisteessä.

Tiimimme Jorvin sairaalassa tarvitsee vahvuuteensa lähihoitajaa osastonsihteeri-lähihoitajan vakituiseen tehtävään. Lähihoitaja toimii pääasiassa asiakaspalvelutehtävissä, aikojen varauksessa ja muissa tutkimuksiin liittyvissä tehtävissä, mutta myös tarvittaessa kliinisessä työssä erilaisissa avustavissa tehtävissä. Mahdollisesti tulevaisuudessa näytteenottotehtävät tulevat osaksi päivittäistä rutiinia.

Meillä Jorvissa tehdään laajasti erilaisia tutkimuksia, kuten EEG, ENMG, unitutkimuksia sekä erilaisia polygrafioita. Kehitämme toimintaamme jatkuvasti sekä laatutyön osalta että LEAN:in näkökulmasta. Meillä on käytössä päivittäisen resurssoinnin malli, jossa on osa yhteinen KNF-toimintaa. Meillä pääset osaksi osaavaa moniammatillista tiimiä ja pääset näköalapaikalle kliinisen neurologian toimintaan. Saamme joka kerta myös opiskelijoiden palautteissa kiitosta.

Mitä toivomme sinulta?

Olet koulutukseltasi nimikesuojattu lähihoitaja, sinulla on jo kokemusta työelämästä sekä sihteerin töitä ja Apotti-järjestelmästä, näytteenotosta, pidät ihmisten kanssa työskentelystä ja potilaiden ohjaamisesta ja olet omatoiminen tiimipelaaja, joka oppii nopeasti uutta! Toivomme, että olet Office-paketin ohjelmistojen ja muiden tietojärjestelmien kokenut käyttäjä. Tehtävässä edellytetään hyvää suomen kielen suullista ja kirjallista taitoa, ruotsin kielen osaaminen luetaan eduksi.

About the Project

We are partnering with an innovative cybersecurity company building a next-generation Identity Security and Identity Observability platform .

The product helps enterprise security teams understand how human users, service accounts, workloads, applications, and AI-driven identities access systems across cloud, SaaS, network, endpoint, and on-premise environments .

At the core of the platform is a highly data-intensive architecture that collects and analyzes large volumes of events, logs, network telemetry, identity activity, and security signals . title: Remote Senior Data Engineer - Ingest, Integrate & Scale
description:
Coderio designs and delivers scalable digital solutions for global companies. We combine strong technical expertise with a product mindset to lead complex software initiatives end-to-end. We work with international clients, value autonomy and clear communication, and build long-term partnerships through technical excellence.

More information:

We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to design, build, and optimize scalable, high-performance data platforms supporting large volumes of financial and transactional data. The ideal candidate has strong expertise in Python, SQL, Apache Spark, AWS, and modern data engineering architectures, with proven experience working with production-grade systems in fast-paced environments.

Candidates must reside exclusively in Argentina, Brazil, or Uruguay.

What You Can Expect (Responsibilities)

  • Design, build, and maintain high-throughput, low-latency batch and streaming data pipelines to ingest and process financial transactions from diverse global sources.

  • Design, scale, and optimize cloud data warehouse and lakehouse architectures capable of handling massive volumes of structured and unstructured data.

  • Collaborate with Data Scientists, Software Engineers, and Product Managers to understand business needs and translate them into scalable, reliable data solutions.

  • Implement and enforce data quality frameworks, automated testing, monitoring, and alerting to ensure data integrity, reliability, high availability, and compliance with SLAs.

  • Drive the adoption of DataOps practices, including CI/CD, workflow automation, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for data systems.

  • Champion data governance, privacy, and security standards across data storage and compute layers, including GDPR/LGPD compliance.

  • Mentor and guide junior and mid-level Data Engineers, promoting engineering excellence, best practices, and modern architectural patterns.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in Data Engineering, Big Data, or related Software Engineering roles, with a proven track record managing high-volume, production-grade data systems in fast-paced environments.

  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL for complex data processing, optimization, and software development; Scala or Java experience is a plus.

  • Hands‑on experience with Apache Spark/PySpark, Delta Lake, and modern lakehouse architectures, including Data Mesh principles.

  • Strong expertise in AWS data services, particularly S3, Glue, Athena, EventBridge, Firehose, and Lambda.

  • Solid experience with data orchestration and warehousing technologies, including Apache Airflow or similar DAG-based tools and platforms such as Snowflake, AWS Redshift, or Google BigQuery.

  • Experience designing real‑time streaming architectures using technologies such as Apache Kafka or AWS Kinesis, as well as familiarity with modern data transformation and modeling tools such as dbt.

  • Strong knowledge of DevOps/DataOps practices, including Git, Docker, CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar), Infrastructure as Code, and cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP.

  • Advanced English proficiency is required, with the ability to communicate effectively in English in both technical and non‑technical contexts.

Nice to Have

  • Previous experience in Fintech, Payments, E‑commerce, or other high‑growth technology environments, particularly working with financial transactions or highly regulated data.

  • Experience with Databricks and advanced cloud lakehouse architectures.

  • Knowledge of data privacy, governance, and security frameworks, including GDPR/LGPD, as well as experience implementing secure data platforms.

  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform, advanced DataOps automation, and mentoring Data Engineers or contributing to technical architecture decisions.

Benefits

  • 100% remote
  • Long-term commitment, with autonomy and meaningful impact
  • Strategic, high‑visibility role within a modern engineering culture
  • Collaborative international team with strong technical leadership
  • Career development and growth opportunities within Coderio

Why join Coderio?

At Coderio, we value talent and excellence. While we are primarily a remote‑first company, this specific strategic role offers the opportunity to work directly on‑site to drive high‑stakes initiatives. We are passionate about technology, collaboration, and fair compensation. We offer an inclusive and challenging environment with real growth opportunities. If you are motivated to design solutions that make a difference, we are waiting for you.

title: Intern. Media Analytics & AI Innovation Intern
description:
The Media Analytics & AI Innovation Intern will contribute to a portfolio of projects designed to strengthen media intelligence, reporting, creative evaluation, and operational efficiency. Working alongside Media team members and cross-functional partners, the intern will help develop recurring insights, research marketplace and creative trends, analyze campaign performance, and recommend opportunities for future testing and improvement.

In addition to project ownership, the intern will participate in team meetings, collaborate with internal stakeholders and agency partners, and contribute to ongoing media planning, measurement, and process-improvement initiatives. The intern will also gain practical exposure to AI-powered agents and workflows by helping the team evaluate use cases, test outputs, document processes, and refine solutions for different marketing needs.

By the end of the internship, the student will deliver a collection of media insights, recommendations, documentation, and project outputs, along with a final presentation summarizing key findings and learnings.

Essential Functions:

  • Develop recurring media insights and executive-ready summaries.
  • Analyze campaign performance and identify key trends and opportunities.
  • Conduct competitive, consumer, creative, and industry research.
  • Develop reports, presentations, documentation, and recommendations for stakeholders.
  • Support media planning, measurement, and optimization initiatives.
  • Assist with the evaluation, testing, building, and refinement of AI-powered agents and workflows.
  • Document processes, use cases, findings, and recommended improvements.
  • Collaborate with internal teams, agency partners, and technology partners.
  • Present project updates, findings, and recommendations to department leadership.
  • Support additional media and marketing projects as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Current undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in Marketing, Business, Analytics, Communications, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Previous internship, leadership, campus organization, or project experience.
  • Experience working with data, reporting, research, or presentations.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Interest in media, marketing, analytics, or emerging technology.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Familiarity with generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, or similar platforms.
  • Basic understanding of digital marketing, advertising, or analytics.
  • Demonstrated interest in testing new tools and solving business problems.

Summer 2027 Internship Program

Are you ready to set sail on an exceptional career journey? Carnival Corporation’s North America Internship Program offers students the opportunity to contribute to meaningful work, build professional skills, and gain firsthand exposure to the cruise and travel industry.

Each intern is hired into and works directly with one brand, department, and team while participating in a shared, location-based internship experience with interns from across Carnival Corporation’s North America brands.

Program Details

  • Program Length: 10 weeks
  • Schedule: Full-time, 40 hours per week
  • Work Arrangement: In-office
  • Compensation: Competitive hourly wage provided
  • East Coast Cohort: June 1–August 5, 2027, based in Doral or Fort Lauderdale, Florida
  • West Coast Cohort: June 14–August 20, 2027, based in Seattle, Washington

Candidates must be available for the full dates of the cohort associated with their internship location. Limited time away may be accommodated, but candidates should not anticipate missing more than two to three workdays. Any extended vacation or significant scheduling conflict should be discussed during the recruitment process.

Your Internship Experience

  • Meaningful Work: Contribute to real projects and business priorities while gaining exposure to the day-to-day work of the assigned team.
  • Professional Development: Participate in structured learning opportunities designed to strengthen workplace, career, and leadership skills.
  • Mentorship and Support: Receive guidance, feedback, and support from leaders and professionals throughout the experience.
  • Networking: Build relationships with fellow interns, employees, and leaders across participating brands and functions.
  • Cohort Experience: Participate in location-based programming and activities with interns from across Carnival Corporation.
  • Project Showcase: Present internship work, outcomes, and key learnings as part of a location-based showcase at the conclusion of the program.

The internship program is designed to develop future talent and provide students with meaningful exposure to the organization. Strong performance may lead to consideration for future full-time, rotational, or other Emerging Talent opportunities based on business needs and available positions; however, participation does not guarantee future employment.

title: TRANSPLANT MGR 1
description:
Job Function Summary:

Involves the development and implementation of policies, procedures, standards and protocols for lung transplant. Includes the establishment of mechanisms to monitor the quality of transplant care in conjunction with the hospital wide plan and ensures compliance with applicable accrediting agencies and regulatory standards. Involves interdisciplinary patient care from a team of experts who represent medical disciplines as well as support services.

Generic Scope

Spends the majority of time (50% or more) achieving organizational objectives through the coordinated achievements of subordinate staff. Establishes departmental goals and objectives, functions with autonomy. Manages the accountability and stewardship of human, financial, and often physical resources in compliance with departmental and organizational goals and objectives. Ensures subordinate supervisors and professionals adhere to defined internal controls. Manages systems and procedures to protect departmental assets.

Custom Scope

Manages the clinical and business operations of lung transplant . Manages resources, oversees compliance with internal policy and external regulatory agencies. Implements quality and performance improvement plans, and contributes to strategic plans and policies.

The lung transplant manager is responsible for clinical, human resource and quality outcomes for the Adult Lung Transplant program. This includes actively managing all clinical operations including evaluation of potential lung recipients, management of all patients on the lung transplant waitlist, and clinical oversight of lung recipients’ post-transplant. The manager will monitor, analyze, and reconcile operations metrics including referral, waitlist, and transplant volumes. Working closely with Medical & Surgical Directors and transplant service line directors, the manager will develop standards of care to ensure high-quality, cost-effective delivery of care and spearhead innovative projects for program improvements.

The manager will be responsible for obtaining approval for hiring, onboarding, and staff retention. The manager identifies and develops organizational talent and embraces continuous learning for themselves and their staff. This position is responsible for ensuring a positive professional work environment,

The manager will respond to all patient satisfaction and patient safety concerns and evaluate means for programmatic improvement. This includes responsibility for program development, management and overall day-to-day operations for the Lung Transplant Program. The manager collaborates with transplant leaders to advance quality strategies, facilitate timeliness of services, and enhance patient and staff satisfaction.

The manager will provide advice and support to the Director of Clinical Operations, Executive Director, physicians and staff on administrative policies and procedures, and has responsibility for ensuring compliance. The incumbent will identify educational needs of departments supporting the transplant programs and recommend, provide, and/or facilitate in-service programs to increase awareness of policies, procedures and other pertinent information and ensure effective interdepartmental relationships. The lung transplant manager will report directly to the Director of Clinical Operations, Transplant Services.

UCSF Transplant Services provides care to kidney, liver, lung and pancreas patients with end stage organ failure requiring transplantation. Each year we evaluate over 3,000 potential recipients and living donors and perform over 750 transplants. UCSF is one of the busiest transplant programs in the country with excellent post-transplant outcomes. Our multidisciplinary team of experienced clinicians provides cutting edge care to our patients and their families.

title: Inventory Control Lead (Vaughan, ON)
description:
Inventory Control Lead – Supply Chain | Automotive Manufacturing

Location: Woodbridge, ON (fully on site) | Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Compensation: $90,000 to $120,000+, based on experience, plus quarterly profit sharing and benefits


About the Opportunity

An established Tier 1 automotive manufacturer that supplies major North American OEMs. The company is modernizing its operations: it is building out MES now and will move to SAP. They need a seasoned supply chain professional who can step in, make business decisions and help take the materials function to the next level.


This is not a role for someone who wants to “grow into” supply chain. It suits someone who already understands how materials move from the supplier to the production line. You should know the logic behind the system and be ready to make an impact from day one.


How You’ll Start

For your first three months, you’ll work as a Material Analyst on some of the most challenging accounts. That’s how you learn the product, the supply base and the team from the inside. After that, you’ll take on leadership of a team of 5 Material Analysts and the cycle counter.


What You’ll Do


  • Own the day-to-day materials flow so the production lines never go down, working through supplier delivery gaps, quality issues and runouts
  • Lead and support a team of Material Analysts who manage the supply base, bring in material for the production floor and work daily with suppliers and production
  • Drive master planning, level loading and production scheduling
  • Lead inventory reduction work and improve inventory turns using JIT principles
  • Review current systems and processes, find what is outdated and put better ways of working in place
  • Play a key role in the MES rollout and the future SAP changeover, including helping the team adopt the new systems
  • Take part in IATF 16949 and customer audits
  • Attend supplier meetings and be available for after-hours calls from production when issues come up (no regular weekend work)


What You Bring


  • Several years of hands-on supply chain or materials experience in automotive manufacturing (strongly preferred). Aerospace or similar complex manufacturing will also be considered.
  • A deep grasp of supply chain fundamentals: MRP logic, ABC analysis, master planning, level loading, scheduling and inventory turns
  • Experience with ERP or MRP systems. SAP is an asset, but a strong grasp of the logic matters more than any one platform.
  • Experience going through a system implementation (ERP, MES or scheduling software) is a strong asset
  • Experience with IATF 16949 audits, including customer audits
  • Advanced Excel skills. Power BI or other analytics tools are an asset.
  • A business decision-maker who works independently and makes things better
  • A university degree is not required. Proven experience and know-how matter most.
  • APICS or CPIM certification is a bonus


Who You Are


  • Calm under pressure in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same
  • High emotional intelligence: compassionate, approachable and good at building trust with a capable, engaged team
  • Someone who leads by example and coaches people rather than micromanaging them
  • Self-motivated, energetic and eager to modernize how things are done


What’s Offered


  • $90,000 to $120,000+ base, based on experience
  • Quarterly in-house profit sharing after 3 months, with additional company profit sharing after 2 years
  • Comprehensive benefits
  • The chance to shape the systems and future direction of a growing materials team


If you have a solid supply chain background and want to lead real change, send me a message at (ja@toptiertalentgroup.com) or apply directly. All inquiries are kept confidential.

title: Gambling Harms Strategy Delivery Officer

Help to implement Brent’s first Gambling Harms Strategy

Brent is one of the most diverse boroughs in the country, with communities, ideas and experiences from across the world helping to shape who we are. Working here means joining a council that is focused on fairness, open to new thinking and committed to improving life for local people.

Our values shape how we work and what people can expect from us. We collaborate proactively, lead inclusively, embrace change, are bold and curious, and celebrate and share our success. For people who care about public service and want their work to matter, Brent offers the chance to make a meaningful difference.

About the role

Brent Council is at an exciting point in its work to tackle gambling-related harms. As we develop and implement the borough's first dedicated Gambling Harms Strategy, we are looking for an ambitious and motivated individual to lead and coordinate its delivery. This is a unique opportunity to shape a key public health priority that has strong support from elected Members and senior leaders. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in influencing how gambling harms are understood, prevented and addressed across Brent, helping to further establish Brent as a leader in tackling gambling-related harm.

The postholder will coordinate the delivery of the Strategy's four key priorities:

  1. Raise awareness and understanding of gambling-related harms among residents, communities and professionals.
  2. Strengthen data, screening and referral processes to enable earlier identification of gambling-related harm.
  3. Improve pathways to support for individuals at risk of, or experiencing, gambling-related harm.
  4. Maximise the use of planning, regulatory and enforcement powers to reduce gambling-related harms and promote healthier communities.

In this role, you will:

  • Coordinate the delivery and implementation of Brent’s new Gambling Harms Strategy
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with partners across the council, voluntary sector and community organisations
  • Establish a Gambling Harms Partnership and take a lead role in the steering group
  • Champion the recognition of gambling harms as a public health issue
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen Brent’s response to tackling gambling harms

About you

This role offers an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about influencing strategic change, reducing health inequalities and delivering meaningful impact for residents.

We are looking for someone who:

  • Can influence, engage and build consensus across a diverse range of stakeholders
  • Can communicate persuasively to different audiences and navigate challenging discussions with confidence
  • Understands the complexity of gambling-related harms and the significant impact they can have on individuals, families and communities
  • Brings creative thinking and innovation to problem solving
  • Is committed to improving the lives of our resident

Why join us?

We know people do their best work when they feel valued, supported and able to grow. At Brent, you will benefit from:

  • 27 days’ annual leave, rising with length of service, plus bank holidays
  • Local Government Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions
  • hybrid and flexible working options for most roles
  • supportive family-friendly policies
  • health and wellbeing support, including eye test support and a 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme
  • financial wellbeing support, including education sessions, childcare deposit loans, and season ticket loans
  • travel support, including affordable parking nearby, a Cycle to Work scheme, and onsite facilities
  • learning and development opportunities to support your career
  • access to My Brent Rewards with exclusive discounts on shopping, travel, leisure and entertainment


To learn more about our staff benefits, visit Our offer to you.

How to apply

Interested in applying? Click "Apply Now" to begin your application.

You will need to submit a supporting statement demonstrating how you meet the application criteria outlined below.

• Knowledge of public health and of using a balanced evidence base to inform and support programmes that improve the health of the population
• Experience of implementing and delivering public health interventions
• Experience of influencing and achieving outcomes through partnership working without direct managerial authority
• Experience of facilitating discussions and building consensus amongst stakeholders with differing priorities, interests and perspectives
• Experience working on gambling harms
• Ability to communicate complex evidence, research findings and policy issues clearly to a range of audiences, including senior leaders, elected members, partners and residents
• Ability to rapidly acquire and apply specialist knowledge in emerging subject areas, translating complex evidence and policy into practical actions and recommendations

This is a key part of the selection process, and applications without a supporting statement may not be considered. You may also upload a CV to support your application, but it cannot replace the supporting statement.

The position provides direct services to families and providers as needed and works collaboratively with internal departments and external community partners. This position does not directly supervise staff but may provide day-to-day workflow coordination, training, technical assistance, and lead support to R&R team members as assigned by the R&R Manager. This position works across multiple Wu Yee service locations throughout San Francisco, with primary assignments in the Bayview and Chinatown neighborhoods and periodic assignments in the Mission and Downtown areas, based on program and coverage needs.

Program Operations & Team Support

title: Sr Director, Retention
description:
The Senior Director, Retention is a high-impact, high-visibility role at Learning Care Group, a $1.5B PE-backed early childhood education operator serving families across 11 brands and 1,100+ centers nationwide. LCG is evolving from a pure digital media buy model toward a 'win local' acquisition approach, and once a family is enrolled the relationship is managed through a deeply human, field-led motion: the Director of the center, the enrollment and call center teams, and the brand-level service experience. Lifecycle marketing is one lever in that motion, not the whole motion. This role sits inside the Chief Digital Office and owns enterprise retention as a commercial outcome: defining and sizing the retention use cases, developing the enterprise retention playbook, and partnering with Field, Call Center, Enrollment, and Lifecycle leaders to implement that playbook across the 11-brand, 1,100+ center portfolio. The role translates propensity-to-churn signals from the Palantir platform and Tertein data science into orchestrated interventions that span digital channels AND the human touchpoints the family actually experiences at the center. The role owns the retention P&L narrative, the intervention program roadmap, and the measurement operating system that proves dollars delivered, and presents that narrative directly to the Executive Leadership Team on a defined cadence. The role does NOT own the underlying data platform (owned by IT), the churn model build (owned by Finance Data Science with Tertein), or the field operations that execute at the center (owned by COO). The role owns the commercial outcome and the cross-functional orchestration that delivers it.

Key Responsibilities:

  1. Define and size the enterprise retention commercial use cases, including the specific family cohorts, churn drivers, and intervention opportunities that represent the material dollars the function will deliver.
  2. Develop the enterprise retention playbook and partner with Field Operations, Center Directors, the Call Center, Enrollment, and Lifecycle Marketing to implement it across 11 brands and 1,100+ centers.
  3. Translate propensity-to-churn signals from Palantir and modeling output from Tertein and Finance Data Science into orchestrated intervention programs that span digital channels AND the human touchpoints the family experiences at the center.
  4. Partner with the Senior Director, Enterprise Analytics & BI to establish and own the enterprise leading indicator framework for family churn, including the early-warning signals that identify at-risk families before they make the decision to disenroll, the thresholds that trigger intervention, and the operating cadence that keeps the framework current.
  5. Stand up and own the system that captures, reports, and acts on Voice of the Customer and broader customer insights across the post-enrollment domain, including structured surveys, passive signal capture from SproutAbout and Procare, service and incident intake, Director-level qualitative feedback, and call recording analysis, with a closed loop from insight to intervention.
  6. Build and manage the retention intervention portfolio across the full omnichannel surface, including center-level service recovery, Director-led family conversations, Call Center save programs, lifecycle email and SMS journeys, save offers, win-back programs, and in-center experience moments.
  7. Own the retention P&L narrative, including size of the opportunity, dollars delivered, flow-through to EBITDA, and the executive reporting that tracks performance against commitment.

  9. Experience hiring, developing, and scaling retention or lifecycle teams is required.
  10. Experience presenting retention performance and strategy to C-suite or board audiences is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  1. 12+ years of retention or lifecycle experience is preferred.

  5. Experience with Palantir Foundry or a comparable operational analytics platform is preferred.

  9. Experience partnering with embedded data science teams and external data science vendors is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  10. Working knowledge of CRM platforms, data science outputs, and modern measurement frameworks.

title: Family Services Specialist I-II

description:
Family Services Specialist I-II CPS
Title Description

Family Services Specialist I represents the entry level employees working under close supervision while being trained in their program area. Employees perform routine- to journey-level casework activities and the casework usually is reviewed by the supervisor prior to implementing a case action. Upon completion of the training program and attainment of necessary approvals, the employee shall be redefined to a full-performance Family Services Specialist II and becomes eligible for a pay increase as defined by the local agency compensation plan.

The Family Services Specialist I is distinguished from the Family Services Specialist II by the latter’s functioning more independently as a full performance Family Services Specialist.

Family Services Specialist II is the full performance level in the occupational group for Family Services. Employees are responsible for developing and implementing individualized service plans involving the application of casework methods in Employment Services and Child Care, and basic service level caseloads of Adult/Adult Protective Services, Child Protective Services, Foster Care, Adoptions. Employees may provide services in all program areas or specialize in one or several program areas. Typically employees perform all tasks independently and only seek supervisory advice on unusual situations or when policies and procedures require supervisory review or involvement.

  • Interprets laws, policies and regulations as applied to specific area of responsibility;
  • Monitors, coordinates and administers specific programs as assigned;
  • Coordinates services within specific area of responsibility;
  • Interviews and assesses customer needs and other relevant factors – such as education/skill levels, abilities, interests, and support systems.
  • Informs clients of related service programs rules/regulations, and right to participate;
  • Presents cases to determine appropriate services and writes/implements service plans;

title: ESIS ProClaim Representative, A&H
description:
The Accident and Health Adjuster is responsible for the day-to-day management of an inventory of hospital indemnity, hospital accident, and accidental death and dismemberment claims. This role involves reviewing medical documentation, investigating losses, interpreting policy language to support coverage and payment determinations, setting and evaluating reserves, preparing coverage letters and reports, and delivering high-quality customer service.

The position reports directly to the Team Leader. The selected candidate should be able to prioritize work effectively, manage multiple tasks, adapt to changing priorities, and support claim handling requirements in a fast-paced environment.

This role requires working in the office a minimum of three days per week.

Duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Under limited supervision, receive assignments and review claim and policy information to support investigations and determine coverage obligations, as applicable to the line of business.
  • Contact, interview, and obtain statements, recorded or in person, from insureds, claimants, witnesses, physicians, attorneys, police officers, and others as needed to gather relevant claim information.
  • Depending on the line of business, inspect and appraise damage for property losses or coordinate appraisal services as needed.
  • Evaluate facts gathered during the investigation to determine liability, if any, and the company’s obligations under the policy contract.
  • Prepare reports related to investigations, settlements, claim denials, and evaluations of involved parties, as appropriate.
  • Set reserves within authority limits and recommend reserve changes to the Team Leader.
  • Review claim progress and status with the Team Leader and discuss issues and recommended next steps.
  • Prepare and submit unusual or potentially adverse exposures to the Team Leader.
  • Assist the Team Leader in identifying opportunities to improve claims handling methods and processes.
  • Resolve claims in a timely and equitable manner.
  • Obtain releases, proofs of loss, or settlement agreements and issue company drafts for claim payments.
  • Communicate claim denials to claimants, insureds/customers, or attorneys when applicable.
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to work independently.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Strong written communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear policy interpretation documentation.
  • Strong customer service skills.
  • Experience with claims handling systems.
  • Adjuster licensing preferred.
  • Claims handling experience preferred.
  • Positive, collaborative, and adaptable approach to working in a changing environment.

An applicable resident or designated home state adjuster’s license is required for ESIS Field Claims Adjusters. Adjusters that do not fulfill the license requirements will not meet ESIS’s employment requirements for handling claims. ESIS supports independent self-study time and will allow up to 4 months to pass the adjuster licensing exam.

ESIS, a Chubb company, provides claim and risk management services to a wide variety of commercial clients. ESIS’ innovative best-in-class approach to program design, integration, and achievement of results aligns with the needs and expectations of our clients’ unique risk management needs. With more than 70 years of experience, and offerings in both the U.S. and globally, ESIS provides one of the industry’s broadest selections of risk management solutions covering both pre- and post-loss services.

ESIS Specialty continually monitors, measures, and analyzes trends while working closely with clients to identify opportunities to positively impact their program costs. ESIS Specialty applies a balanced approach to claims handling and management and continually refines approach to be sure services are customized, complementary and complete.

The pay range for the role is $57,000 to $83,000. The specific offer will depend on an applicant’s skills and other factors. title: AIML - Senior Machine Learning Platform Engineer, Responsible AI and Safety
description:
Join us in shaping the future of Generative AI at Apple! Are you passionate about making AI systems safer, more inclusive, and globally representative? Apple is seeking a Machine Learning Platform Engineer to build the tooling and infrastructure behind our Responsible AI mitigations, from on-device foundation models running on Apple Silicon to server-side inference on Private Cloud Compute (PCC). In this role, you will build the Python platform our ML and safety engineers rely on to train, evaluate, deploy, and configure safety classifiers, guardrail models, and model behavior overrides. You will turn manual, one-off workflows into automated, scalable, and reproducible systems, so that every evaluation runs the same way, every deployment is validated, and every configuration change is safe to ship

Our team leads Responsible AI initiatives for global generative AI products, operating at the intersection of policy, product, and GenAI. We build the safety guardrails, and policy enforcement layers that protect users from unintended model behavior. This role builds the platform underneath that work. You will build the systems that enable consistent training and evaluation at scale: an training/evaluation platform that runs any benchmark the same way every time, deployment pipelines that package and release models and mitigation assets to devices and the cloud, and tooling that lets engineers across many languages and modalities author and validate configuration changes with confidence. You will also dig into the failures and regressions the platform surfaces, and turn them into concrete fixes. ML engineers, client engineers, policy, and release teams are your customers, and you will need enough understanding of how models are evaluated and served to build infrastructure whose results they can trust.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional engineering experience, with Python as a primary development language
  • BS in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience
  • Experience building infrastructure or tooling for ML inference, evaluation, or deployment that is used by engineers outside your direct team
  • Experience building or operating infrastructure that deploys ML models to production and maintains them across versions
  • Working knowledge of how ML models are evaluated (metrics, held-out test sets, error analysis, sources of non-reproducibility), enough to build evaluation infrastructure whose results ML engineers can trust
  • Experience designing configuration-driven systems, including schemas, validation, versioning, and safe rollout of config changes
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: testing, CI/CD, code review, and writing maintainable code that others build on
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to cross-functional partners
  • Must be comfortable working with sensitive or potentially offensive content

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with LLM inference, including tokenization, batching, streaming, and serving frameworks
  • Working knowledge of on-device ML runtimes (Core ML, MLX, or equivalent) and the model-export lifecycle: converting trained models into shippable assets and loading them at runtime
  • Experience running distributed evaluation or workflow orchestration at scale (Kubernetes, Ray, Spark, or equivalent)
  • Experience with text normalization, pattern-based filtering, or multilingual NLP
  • Experience with Responsible AI, trust and safety, or content moderation systems
  • Experience building LLM-based or agentic developer tooling
  • Familiarity with Swift
