title: System QA Engineer
description:
About GSM Outdoors

At GSM Outdoors, we design, develop, and deliver innovative products that enhance outdoor experiences. Our portfolio includes some of the industry's most recognized brands in hunting, shooting, fishing, and outdoor recreation. Through technology and product innovation, we continue to create solutions that connect people with the outdoors.


Position Summary

GSM Outdoors is seeking a Systems QA Engineer to take ownership of quality across our connected cellular camera ecosystem, including mobile applications, web platforms, APIs, and camera hardware.


This role is responsible for validating the complete user experience and ensuring every feature works as intended—from initial requirements and development through application functionality, API integrations, hardware performance, and the data generated by our devices. The Systems QA Engineer will partner closely with software, mobile, hardware, and product teams to identify potential issues early, develop comprehensive test strategies, and ensure quality is integrated throughout the development lifecycle.


The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, technically curious, collaborative, and passionate about delivering reliable products and seamless user experiences.


Essential Job Functions


Requirements & Test Planning

  • Review user stories, requirements, and acceptance criteria to identify gaps, ambiguities, and potential testability risks before development begins.
  • Collaborate with Product Management and Engineering teams to clarify requirements and establish clear, measurable testing expectations.
  • Develop and maintain test plans for features and product releases, along with detailed test cases for individual user stories.
  • Document and maintain test plans, test cases, and testing progress within JIRA.

End-to-End Systems Testing

  • Execute testing throughout the development sprint across iOS and Android mobile applications, web platforms, and cellular camera hardware.
  • Validate features and user workflows across the entire connected product ecosystem, ensuring applications, APIs, devices, and data function together as expected.
  • Perform functional, integration, regression, and exploratory testing to identify defects and potential product issues.
  • Verify camera functionality, device behavior, connectivity, and the accuracy and consistency of data generated by the hardware.
  • Document, track, prioritize, and communicate defects while partnering with Engineering to support timely resolution and retesting.

API & Database Validation

  • Perform API testing using Postman and available API documentation.
  • Develop and maintain Postman collections to support repeatable API testing.
  • Validate API responses, integrations, and expected system behavior.
  • Use SQL queries and database management tools to verify that information is stored, updated, and retrieved accurately.
  • Investigate discrepancies between application behavior, API responses, camera-generated data, and database records.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Quality Improvement

  • Work closely with software, mobile, hardware, and product development teams to integrate testing into the software development lifecycle.
  • Participate in sprint planning, requirements reviews, development discussions, and release readiness activities.
  • Communicate testing progress, risks, and defects clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Identify opportunities to improve testing coverage, documentation, and quality assurance processes.
  • Help ensure releases meet established quality expectations before deployment.

title: Breakthrough Teaching and Learning Manager
description:
Breakthrough San Francisco at SF Day School

Teaching and Learning Manager

Position: Breakthrough Teaching and Learning Manager

Position Status: Active

Agreement Dates: Spring 2026 - June 30, 2027

Report to: Breakthrough Director of Middle School Programs

Department: Staff

Supervisory Responsibilities: Yes

Pay Category: Non-Exempt

Pay Rate: $30 - $45 per hour, depending on experience

Pay Schedule: Semi-monthly


Breakthrough Overview


Breakthrough San Francisco supports young people on the path to college and trains the next generation of educators. In 2026-27, we’re serving 304 students from across San Francisco. They make an eight-year commitment - from the summer after fourth grade until their high school graduation - with ongoing support available during their college years. In addition, through our summer teacher residency, we train outstanding college students for education careers. Founded in 1993, we are a community involvement initiative of San Francisco Day School and one of two dozen affiliates of the national non-profit organization Breakthrough Collaborative. For more information, please visit.


Position Summary


The Teaching and Learning Manager oversees Breakthrough’s summer teacher residency – an opportunity for outstanding college students from across the country to gain valuable training and experience as classroom teachers. They select, train, and supervise our summer Teaching Fellows, as well as our Instructional Coaches - experienced professional educators who train and support them. In addition, the Teaching and Learning Manager oversees workshop and elective class instruction in our Saturday program during the school year. Whatever the time of year, they ensure that instruction at Breakthrough is engaging and impactful and fosters a culture of inclusivity and growth for all participants in our program. The Teaching and Learning Manager collaborates closely with other Breakthrough staff members and reports to Breakthrough San Francisco’s Director of Middle School Programs.


Essential Functions

School Year Program

  • Oversee grade-level workshops and elective classes, as part of Breakthrough’s impactful Saturday program for fifth - eighth graders. Select, train, and coach volunteer teachers, ensuring high-quality instruction. Prepare workshop and elective class supplies.
  • Develop rigorous and engaging academic enrichment materials for fifth - eighth graders to complete with support from volunteers.
  • Possibly, provide high school guidance support to Breakthrough eighth graders and families.
  • Support school-year program planning and operations, including Back to Breakthrough Bash, Celebration, student selection, and emergency preparedness.

Summer Program

  • Oversee Teaching Fellow selection process, yielding a committed, reflective, and diverse group of aspiring educators.
  • Oversee Teaching Fellow training and professional development. Develop pre-summer assignments. Plan and lead two-week Teacher Orientation, focused on essential building blocks for classroom success. Collaborate with Breakthrough’s High School and Postsecondary team on shared training sessions. Oversee professional development during the summer.
  • Supervise Teaching Fellows, creating a culture of inclusivity, high expectations, and shared growth. Lead pre-summer conversations and 1:1 check-ins, Faculty Meetings, and community building. Oversee Teaching Fellow evaluation.
  • Hire, train, and manage Instructional Coaches: experienced professional educators who support Teaching Fellows’ success. Lead pre-summer IC training sessions and weekly IC meetings during the summer. Create a culture of inclusivity, high expectations, and shared growth.
  • Oversee student assessment and analyze results, determining implications for supporting students and improving teaching and learning.
  • Lead career exploration programming for Teaching Fellows, facilitating their awareness of a wide range of pathways into the teaching profession. Provide ongoing career guidance post-summer.
  • Lead community-wide special events, possibly including Career Day.
  • Support summer program planning and operations, including Pre-Summer Orientation, Celebration, Morning Meeting, All-School Meeting, hallway and recess duty, and emergency preparedness.

Other Expectations

  • Build positive relationships with students. Hold them accountable for high standards of behavior and performance.
  • Collaborate effectively with other Breakthrough San Francisco staff members, as well as staff at SF Day School and other Breakthrough sites nationally.
  • Complete other projects as needed.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree (master’s degree a plus)
  • At least 3-5 years of professional teaching experience, ideally at the middle school level
  • Experience with teacher training, coaching, and instructional leadership
  • Familiarity with Next Generation Science Standards and Common Core State Standards
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with first-generation college students and their families
  • Demonstrated ability to hold students to high standards and achieve meaningful results
  • Demonstrated cultural competence and commitment to anti-racist and social justice education
  • Demonstrated history of reflecting on own performance and striving for professional growth
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills
  • Experience with curriculum development a plus
  • Supervisory/managerial experience a plus
  • Prior experience with Summerbridge/Breakthrough a plus
  • Familiarity with San Francisco public and/or private schools a plus
  • Familiarity with Amharic, Cantonese, Spanish, and/or Tigrinya a plus

Commitment and Compensation

  • Year-round, full-time, hourly position
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package, commensurate with education and experience and consistent with SF Day School personnel policies.

EEO

San Francisco Day School is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment including the decision to hire will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. San Francisco Day School does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition or history, pregnancy, expression, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under any federal, state, or local law. San Francisco Day School will provide reasonable accommodation(s) to all qualified candidates and all employees with disabilities, where their disability affects the performance of their essential job functions, except when doing so would create undue hardship. If you need assistance or need to request accommodations, please contact hr@sfday.org.


SF Day Community Expectations

In following these community expectations, we strive to create:

  • A working environment for employees to feel grounded in purpose, seen, and respected at school.
  • A learning environment for students to gain the skills and knowledge to grow into global citizens who care for themselves, each other, and our world.

Employees:

  1. Are compassionate and kind to ourselves and others. We work together as active contributors in a connected community and focus on balance and wellness so we can show up fully for students.
  2. Are prepared. We have the appropriate training, knowledge, and skills regarding this age group's developmental characteristics and needs. We complete our responsibilities with professionalism and fidelity.
  3. Are reflective and accountable. We take time to consider the intent and impact of our actions and repair the harm done for the betterment of the community.
  4. Are lifelong learners. We are committed to continuous professional growth and lifelong learning.
  5. Put the children first. We are child-centered, both in and out of the classroom. We treat each child as an individual with respect and dignity. We create a safe environment where students grow in autonomy and the ability to work and play together.
  6. Partner with families. We believe in the importance of the home-school partnership and partner with families proactively and positively.
  7. Communicate with professionalism and care. We communicate with professionalism and care to each other and our students.
  8. Uphold high expectations for ourselves and our students. It is all of our work to create an environment that fosters personal integrity and social responsibility.

Teachers:

  1. Are skilled at teaching their subject area and grade level(s). We are constantly deepening and evolving our craft to ensure best practices. We know how we teach is as important as what we teach, and growth requires feedback, reflection, and change.
  2. Understand the arc of child development. We align our pedagogy and content to this developmental arc.
  3. Create an engaging, culturally responsive classroom. We recognize and value the importance of actively engaging students’ learning. We honor students’ cultural displays of learning and respond positively and constructively.
  4. Plan for predictable variability in the learning profiles of students. We provide multiple means of representation and engagement, as well as support and extension in what we teach and assess.
  5. Provide clear, consistent classroom norms and logical consequences. We provide feedback to students with clarity and care and guide them through the reflective and restorative process. Students know what routines to expect and what’s expected of them to support them in becoming empowered learners and responsible school community members.
  6. Provide clear learning goals and objectives. We align to content area scope and sequence. We ensure that students know what they are learning when they are learning it, and why they are learning it.

This job description supersedes all prior job descriptions and is intended to describe the general content and essential requirements for the position listed above. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of requirements, duties, and responsibilities. Management reserves the right to add or change the duties of this position as required at any time.

All employment with San Francisco Day School is at will and shall continue only upon the mutual consent of the School and the employee. This means that an employee may terminate their employment with the School at any time with or without cause or prior notice and that the School may terminate an employee’s employment at any time with or without cause or prior notice.

# Job Summary:
Manage the obtaining, maintenance and monitoring of environmental and sectoral permits that enable the execution of the project in Argentina, ensuring that the engineering design, constructive planning and field activities comply with the applicable national and provincial regulations, with the commitments assumed before the authority and with the environmental standards of the client.
The position acts as a bridge between engineering and the regulatory authority: it translates the legal requirements into verifiable design criteria, anticipates the environmental restrictions that condition the layout and the construction sequence, and maintains a critical permit route aligned with the project schedule. Its performance is measured by the absence of regulatory detentions and by the technical quality of the information presented to the competent bodies.
# Major Responsibilities:
Permission management
• Preparing and keeping updated the project permits matrix, identifying competent body, submission requirements, legal deadlines and actual processing deadlines.
• Prepare, review and submit the Environmental Impact Report and its biennial updates, along with the supporting technical documentation required by the provincial mining authority.
• Managing the associated sectoral permits: water use and concession, effluent dumping, emissions into the atmosphere, hazardous waste management, soil movement, intervention of native vegetation and transport of hazardous substances.
• Maintaining technical dialogue with provincial and national enforcement authorities, responding to observations, requests for additional information and audits.
• Timely alert the permits that constitute a critical route and propose sequencing alternatives when a regulatory deadline compromises the schedule.
# Environmental studies and assessment
• Defining the scope of the environmental baselines - air quality, noise, surface and groundwater, soils, flora, fauna, glaciers and periglacial environment, archaeology and socio-economic environment - and technically supervise the consulting firms that execute them.
• Reviewing consultant deliverables verifying methodological sufficiency, representativeness of sampling and traceability of data before its incorporation into the file.
• Evaluating environmental impacts of the project, propose mitigation and compensation measures, and verify that they are reflected in the design criteria and technical specifications.
• Estimating hours, costs and deadlines of environmental studies for their incorporation into the project budget and program.
# Compliance, monitoring and interface with the project
• Keeping track of environmental commitments derived from the Environmental Impact Statement and the permits granted, and periodically verify their compliance on the ground.
• Providing the engineering disciplines with the environmental constraints applicable to the design - layout restrictions, exclusion areas, discharge limits and water management criteria - and verify their incorporation.
• Preparing progress reports on the status of permits for the client and for the project management, with status, regulatory risks and mitigation actions.
• Supporting the processes of citizen participation and relations with communities and local authorities, in coordination with the social area of the project and the client.
• Issuing the environmental deliverables under the project's documentary control system, respecting the review scheme and the preparation, review and approval signatures.
# Regulatory framework of reference
• Dominating the Argentine environmental regime and its federal articulation: the Nation sets the minimum protection budgets and the provinces, as holders of the original domain of natural resources, are the enforcement authority that grants the permits. The following list is the minimum core required: Law 25.675, Law 24.585; Law 26.639; Law 24.051, Law 25.688, Law 26.331, Law 25.743, Law 25.831, Law 27.520, ILO Convention 169 (Law 24.071).
# Education and Experience Requirements:
Level 1:
• Requires a university degree in Environmental Sciences, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Natural Resources, Geological Sciences or Biological Sciences, with professional registration in the corresponding jurisdiction, between 5 and 8 years of professional practice in environmental management and permits, with at least 3 years in mining, energy or infrastructure projects in Argentina.
• A graduate degree, major or diploma in environmental management, environmental impact assessment or environmental law is desirable.
Level 2:
• Requires a university degree in Environmental Sciences, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Natural Resources, Geological Sciences or Biological Sciences, with professional registration in the corresponding jurisdiction, between 8 and 10 years of professional practice in environmental management and permits, with at least 5 years in mining, energy or infrastructure projects in Argentina.
• A graduate degree, major or diploma in environmental management, environmental impact assessment or environmental law is desirable.
# Required Knowledge and Skills:
• Verifiable participation in at least one complete cycle of environmental processing: preparation of the study, submission to the authority, response to observations and obtaining the approving resolution.
• Experience in direct interaction with provincial and national public agencies, and in technical supervision of environmental consultancies.
• Previous experience in EPC or EPCM environments is desirable, with exposure to document control, change control and management of interfaces between disciplines. Mastery of the Argentine environmental regime described in the previous section and ability to track its provincial regulations.
• Environmental impact assessment methodologies, design of monitoring plans and environmental management programs; notions of modeling of air quality, noise and dispersion of pollutants.
• Management of geographic information systems, advanced spreadsheets and project scheduling tools.
• Native Spanish and intermediate or higher technical English, sufficient to read international standards and participate in meetings with multinational teams.
• The Documentary Organization: Maintains complete, versioned and auditable files at all times.
• Integrity: Does not sign or endorse information that it cannot endorse, even under deadline pressure.
• The technical rigor: Supports each statement of the file in verifiable data and detects methodological weaknesses in third-party studies.
• Regulatory anticipation: Identifies the permit that will become a critical route before it becomes one and activates management well in advance.
• The institutional communication: Maintains a professional and traceable relationship with the authority; writes with legal and technical precision.
• The transversal work: Translates environmental requirements into the language of engineering and negotiates solutions with the disciplines without compromising compliance.
• Experience in metallic and/or non-metallic mining.

About the Role

We're hiring a Software Engineer to help build Velora's AI-native software platform, giving nonprofit teams more time for their mission and less time spent on administration. You'll join the team that builds the CRM, data and integrations at the core of the platform, supporting donor management, communications, automation and reporting as a mature product moves into newer services.

This is a full-stack role where you'll own well-scoped features end to end, from a Product prototype through build, release and verification in production. You'll work across frontend, backend, infrastructure and data, own the testing and quality of your own work, and keep an eye on what you ship after it goes live. You'll grow your design and scoping skills with guidance from senior engineers and partner closely with Product along the way.

AI is central to how we work. You'll direct coding agents on your own features, review every output critically and stay accountable for what ships. You'll also take part in code reviews, giving thoughtful feedback and using what you learn to raise the quality of your own work.

What will you be doing?

  • Own well-scoped features end to end, from a PM's prototype through build and release, engaging Product early and growing with guidance on scope and trade-offs.
  • Work across the full stack -frontend, backend, infrastructure and data-on your own features, rather than a single layer.
  • Work AI-native by default: direct approved agents in Cursor on your own work, review every output critically, and stay accountable for everything you ship.
  • Own quality for your features with no QA handoff: write unit, integration and end-to-end (E2E) tests that prove the work, and flag higher-risk work so the team can decide whether to pull in central QA.
  • Ship small changes to production continuously, often behind feature flags. Work is done when it's verified in production, not when it's merged.
  • Own what you ship after release: monitoring, triage and fixes.
  • Build securely from design onward, with particular care for donor data, and review for security in code review.
  • Contribute to design on your features, learning how a mature core application is moving into newer services, and making code improvements with guidance.
  • Participate in code reviews, giving timely, constructive feedback and using feedback to raise the quality of your own work.

How we build:

  • We deploy to production many times a day; feature flags separate deploying from releasing.
  • AI increases individual leverage; it doesn't replace pairing or peer judgment.
  • Meeting-light: short daily standups, retros every two weeks and meeting-free Fridays.

What we're looking for:

  • 2-3 years as a software engineer; SaaS product experience preferred.

description:
Tarjoamme mielenkiintoisen työn lasten ja perheiden parissa monipuolisessa työympäristössä.

Erikoistuvan lääkärin viran toimenkuvaan kuuluvat lasten hematologia-onkologiaan erikoistuvan lääkärin monipuoliset tehtävät koulutuksen vaatimaksi ajaksi. Kyseessä on määräaikainen tehtävä asianomaisen koulutustarpeen mukaan, kuitenkin maksimissaan 2 vuotta. Koulutus on lasten hematologia-onkologian lisäkoulutusohjelman mukainen koulutus.

Viran menestyksellinen hoitaminen edellyttää hyviä vuorovaikutustaitoja ja kykyä toimia moniammatillisissa työryhmissä. Sijoituspaikka on virkasuhteen alussa Uusi lastensairaala, mutta virantoimitukseen kuuluu, että työtä tehdään tarvittaessa muissakin HUSin toimipaikoissa. Virkaan liittyy päivystysvelvollisuus.

Hae meille hakuajan loppuun mennessä. HUSissa olet osa vaikuttavinta hoitoa.

Tehtävän kelpoisuusehdot

Erikoislääkärin pätevyys soveltuvalla erikoisalalla ja lisäksi laillistettu lääkäri tai lupa toimia lääkärin tehtävissä.

Haettavana olevan viran kohdalla soveltuva erikoisala on lastentaudit.

Tehtävään valitun tulee esittää rikosrekisterilain (770/1993) 6 §:n 2 mom. mukainen lasten kanssa työskenteleviltä vaadittava rekisteriote.

Kielitaitovaatimuksena on suomen kielen hyvä suullinen ja kirjallinen taito ja ruotsin kielen tyydyttävä suullinen ja kirjallinen taito taikka ruotsin kielen hyvä suullinen ja kirjallinen taito ja suomen kielen tyydyttävä suullinen ja kirjallinen taito.

Edellytämme asiakas- ja potilastiloissa työskentelevältä tartuntatautilain mukaista rokotussuojaa, ja terveydenhuollon toimintayksiköissä työskentelevältä terveydentilan selvitystä keuhkotuberkuloosista.

Yhteystiedot

Osastonylilääkäri Samppa Ryhänen p. 050 427 0942 tai erityispediatrian linjajohtaja Antti Kyrönlahti p. 050 427 2395

title: Advanced Semiconductor Engineer
description:
Join a team that designs, verifies, integrates and tests complex microfabricated products within Honeywell Aerospace. Develop cutting-edge technologies in the field of micro-electrical and micro-optical mechanical systems (MEMS and MOEMs) fabrication for

Honeywell Aerospace's Advanced Technology division. Work with highly skilled engineers and technicians in a state-of-the-art process lab developing and characterizing new sensors for aerospace applications. Contribute to business growth by proposing new research ideas and exploring innovative process techniques. The ideal candidate will have a broad understanding of materials and fabrication on silicon wafers, will effectively be able to lead a team of process lab engineers and technicians, and will have intimate knowledge of the workings of the machinery which comprise a process lab.

You will develop new products and processes in support of the organization's business strategies in cutting-edge technology development. Use wafer fabrication experience and skills for new business opportunities, products and processes in an R&D environment.

Areas of concentration will include process integration and metrology techniques specific to microfabrication such as photolithography, DRIE, ICP etching, PECVD, LPCVD, wafer bonding, CVD & PVD techniques, profilometry, ellipsometry, SEM, e-beam lithography, and others.

In this role you will:

Design and execute microfabrication experiments to improve processes and to support new technology development

Collaborate with technicians, design, manufacturing and budgeting teams to provide creative solutions to meet product requirements and enhance technology readiness of an ever-evolving advanced technology portfolio

Monitor and analyze data to fix yield, performance and reliability issues.

Propose novel products, devices, and solutions to meet R&D customers’ requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Document, analyze and interpret complex microfabrication problems, provide solutions, and oversee execution.
  • Design and interpret high quality experiments to improve micro-fabrication processes and capability.
  • Monitor and analyze metrology and parametric and probe data to fix yield, performance, and reliability issues.
  • Collaborate with technicians, design, manufacturing, and budgeting teams to provide creative solutions to meet product requirements and enhance technology readiness of an ever-evolving advanced technology portfolio.
  • Propose novel products, devices, and solutions to meet R&D customer’s requirements.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in technical disciplines such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics.
  • 5 years industry experience in wafer micro-fabrication techniques (PhD inclusive)

WE VALUE

  • PhD. or Masters in electrical engineering, microelectronics, electronics, material science, physics, mechanical engineering or chemistry engineering
  • MEMS and/or CMOS fabrication experience
  • Proficiency with data analysis and statistical techniques
  • Experience in leading a team of skilled process lab technicians
  • Experience with e-beam lithography, photolithography, DRIE, ICP etching, PECVD, wafer bonding, lithography, ALD, electroplating, CVD & PVD techniques, profilometry, ellipsometry, SEM, and others.
  • Experience with 2.5/3-D heterogenous integration
  • Knowledge of photolithography layout tools such as L-edit

title: Re-advertisement_ One National Consultants for the Situation Analysis of Midwifery in Jordan
description:
[This is a re-advertisement for Consultant 1. Candidates who previously submitted an application for this position under Job ID 37872 do not need to reapply, as their previous applications will remain on file].

Purpose of the Consultancy

Strengthening midwifery is a priority for UNFPA, given its importance for maternal and newborn health and for universal access to sexual and reproductive health services. UNFPA supports countries in aligning midwifery with the global standards of the International Confederation of Midwives (ICM) and in translating assessment findings into practical change. In Jordan, midwifery involves several interlinked issues, including education and training, professional regulation and standards, workforce and service delivery, and working relationships between health professions. UNFPA is carrying out a national assessment of midwifery, combining in-depth analysis with structured consultation of stakeholders, to identify gaps and blind spots and to produce a roadmap of agreed priority actions. UNFPA therefore requires two national consultants to support stakeholder consultation, information collection and analysis.

Scope of Work / Key Tasks

The consultants will work as a team and will divide the tasks below in coordination with UNFPA

  • Conduct a situation analysis using the UNFPA data collection tools
  • Review national documents in relevance to the national standards (if any) and to ICM global standards (professional framework, regulation, essential competencies, pre-service education).
  • Lead the design and facilitation of three focus group discussions with stakeholders selected in coordination with JNC.
  • Conduct at least 5 key informant interviews with policymakers and other decision-makers.
  • Collect and consolidate information from the discussions and interviews, including gaps and blind spots.
  • Contribute to drafting the national analysis, the assessment plan and the roadmap.
  • Co-lead the collective validation workshop with the second national consultant.
  • Support the presentation of findings and the roadmap to the Jordanian Nursing Council (JNC), in support of its annual work.

Duration and Working Schedule

23 November-31 December 2026

Place of Work

Consultant should be based in Amman and work on-site for the focus group discussions, the validation workshop and key meetings with UNFPA and the JNC.

Deliverables and Work Modalities

The assignment will be undertaken on a lump-sum basis, with payment made in two instalments upon completion and UNFPA’s acceptance of the deliverables below. All written deliverables will be submitted electronically.

Deliverable Timeline Payment
Completion of data collection through focus group discussions (FGDs) and key informant interviews (KIIs), including submission of three focus group reports and a summary of interviews. By 30 November 2026; FGDs scheduled for 24–26 November 2026. 50%
Completion and submission of the consultant’s contributions to the final assessment and roadmap, incorporating feedback from the validation workshop and JNC Board presentation, and approval by UNFPA. By 31 December 2026. 50%

Monitoring and Reporting

Deliverables are submitted electronically to the UNFPA Jordan Country Office. Progress is reviewed through regular check-in meetings.

Supervision

The consultant works under the supervision of the Health Policy Specialist at UNFPA in Jordan.

Expected Travel

If travel is required, UNFPA in Jordan will cover all related costs, according to its Duty Travel Policies.

Required Qualifications and Competencies

  • An advanced degree in Social and Health Sciences, Nursing, Midwifery, or a related field, with a minimum of 5 years of professional experience in midwifery, strategic planning, education, evaluation, or research; or a Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience.
  • Fluent in Arabic and English (required),
  • Strong leadership skills,
  • Inspiring facilitation and communication skills.

Inputs / Support Provided by UNFPA

  • The consultants will be responsible for arranging their own workspace, equipment, supplies, and any other resources required to carry out the assignment. UNFPA will not provide office space or equipment.

Other relevant information or special conditions, if any:

The consultant will work in close coordination with another consultant, with each accountable to UNFPA for the deliverables specified in their respective Terms of Reference; neither consultant will supervise the other. They will exchange relevant data, tools and findings, subject to applicable confidentiality requirements, and jointly ensure consistency between the assessment and roadmap. Consultant 1 will lead the FGDs and KIIs and prepare the corresponding reports. Consultant 2 will contribute to the analysis and synthesis of findings, co-facilitate the validation workshop, document and incorporate stakeholder feedback into the assessment and roadmap, and jointly prepare the workshop report with Consultant 1.

If you're ready to turn your passion into purpose, we’d love to welcome you aboard.



Who We Need

Abilities First is seeking a Supportive Residential Coach. The Supportive Residential Coach will be responsible for the provision of individual services as identified in the Individual Service Plan and by the treatment team for individuals who need specific assistance and supports. He/she will be responsible for maintaining current medical services and following up on the medical needs of the individuals within the program. The Supportive Residential Coach will be responsible for the supervision of the daily activities/responsibilities of the residents. The Supportive Residential Coach helps the resident achieve valued outcomes and promotes individualization (self-determination & choice), independence (self-reliance to the extent possible), integration (involvement with relatives and friends and belonging to a neighborhood community) and productivity (accomplishments that contribute to the person’s own life and the lives of those around them).


The Supportive Residential Coach is required to provide assistance to individuals with that reside in an independent placement in the apartment settings throughout the community. The staff assigned to this program must have excellent time management skills, problem solving, flexibilities with their work schedules, work independently and efficiently to able to provide supports and oversight for multi individuals on their caseload. This position also requires staff to provide 24hrs oversight on an on-call basis at designated times throughout the calendar year by providing support for the individuals with the Direct Care Cell-phone.


Full-Time Non-Exempt

Standard Schedule: Sunday 9:00am-5:00pm, Monday -Thursday 10:00am-6:pm with flexibility and ability to provide on call coverage on a rotating basis

Salary Range: $18.89 - $20.89 per hour

**Weekend Shift Differential of $1.00 per hour for hours worked Friday 11pm- Monday 7am **


Depending on the needs of the program, additional certifications (training provided) for med administration $1.00, insulin $.50, G-Tube $1.00 and ostomy care $.50!


Responsibilities:


  • Establishes a working relationship with all residents and supervises their participation in daily activities as needed.
  • Ensures the safety and well-being of the residents.
  • Required to participate in the on-call rotation and provide 24hrs oversight with the use of the Direct Care Cell-phone for an entire week multiple times throughout the year- please see Direct Care On-call Policy-Procedure
  • Provides training and assistance to the residents in developing basic skills in appropriate social behaviors and communication, safety, housekeeping, personal care, health care, medication administration, using public transportation, menu & meal preparation, grocery purchasing, and planning recreational activities.
  • Assists the resident in achieving progress toward their individualized-based outcomes.
  • Assist the individuals with financial training to maintain adequate amounts of fund to pay monthly bills. – this includes maintaining accurate updated documentation in the individual’s checkbook registry as well as completing financial ledgers (savings, checking, burial, etc. accounts).
  • Is an active participant in the service planning process by attending ISP/Res. Hab. – Case Review meetings.
  • Documents attendance, completes weekly billing for individuals and Monthly Summaries for the individual with the use of the Therap system.
  • Performs responsibilities that demonstrate the ability to work cooperatively and establish professional relationships with all persons involved with the resident.
  • Assist individuals with scheduling and maintaining medical appointments (includes completing medical consultation forms for doctor’s appointments.)
  • Assist with ensuring the individuals have an adequate supply of medications by completing weekly medication counts and supervision of the individuals with filling their weekly pill box and assistance/supervision of ordering refill of medications and obtaining new prescriptions as needed.
  • Assist the Program RN with updating the site specific medication formularies for the individuals.
  • Updating the Emergency Information Sheets for the individuals bi-yearly (every six-months) or as necessary.

title: IT Architect
description:
DESCRIPTION:

The Information Technology Division (ITD) of the State Court Administrator’s Office (SCAO) is seeking an IT Architect. This role is critical to the design, development, maintenance, and support of internally developed web-based applications at the MN Judicial Branch. This work provides senior-level vision and a technical road map and architecture, and includes requirements gathering, designing, coding, testing, documenting, and implementing software at an expert and high level of complexity. These applications range from internal applications to externally facing, enterprise-level software applications requiring 24x7 availability. The person in this role is expected to be able to work at an expert level on both the front-end and the back end of application development (full-stack development).

This role works independently and with a team (including collaborations with other senior-level staff and leadership within IT), providing technical direction, leading developers in design, development, and support, and handling architectural responsibilities like defining architecture, setting security standards, and ensuring scalability and maintainability.

EXAMPLES OF JOB DUTIES:

The following are examples of major job duties expected for this position to perform:

  • Provides leadership and guidance by participating in architectural design discussions, advancing established architectural visions, and reviewing and approving functional, technical, and deployment specifications to ensure alignment with enterprise standards and business requirements.
  • Develops, maintains, and manages the application portfolio inventory in collaboration with technical and business partners to ensure accurate documentation of applications, technologies, and related information.
  • Leads planning, coordination, and dependency management across products, projects, and strategic initiatives by collaborating with product owners to identify and resolve technical, business, application, and resource dependencies and ensure alignment of priorities and delivery schedules.
  • Provides technical oversight for large, complex projects and programs by directing project execution, identifying and mitigating risks and issues, monitoring progress, and communicating project status, outcomes, and recommendations to management and key stakeholders.
  • Evaluates, troubleshoots, and supports existing applications, including database, security, web services, and third-party integrations, while identifying and promoting emerging technologies, tools, and methodologies to advance the organization's technology capabilities.
  • Communicates complex technical concepts, architectural recommendations, and technology solutions effectively to technology and business partners through written communications, presentations, and collaborative discussions.

TYPICAL QUALIFICATIONS:

Below are the past experiences that will enable success in the role. For education requirements listed, the equivalent number of years of related experience may serve as a substitute.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree, or a degree or certificate in the computer field from a technical college or trade school, or equivalent work experience in software programming and development.
  • Minimum of 8 years’ experience in software development.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Degree in computer science or management information systems or included coursework in these areas.
  • 10-15 years of significant experience in software development. 2-3 years’ experience leading other developers.
  • Work experience related to the courts and/or criminal justice.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Thorough knowledge of information technology principles, practices, standards, and emerging trends, including data analytics, software development, systems architecture and design, network infrastructure, integrations, database management, and multi-platform computing environments.
  • Thorough knowledge of systems analysis and design, business process reengineering, application development, programming languages, database structures, data architecture, APIs, web services, network operating systems, and hardware and software technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to design, develop, test, document, maintain, and troubleshoot complex applications and web services using technologies such as Angular, C#, .NET, MVC, and SQL Server, including database, security, integration, and third-party components.
  • Skill in leading cross-functional teams of technical and professional staff in the planning, development, implementation, and support of complex technology, database, and analytics solutions.
  • Thorough knowledge of project, program, and portfolio management principles, with the ability to plan, coordinate, and manage multiple large-scale, complex IT projects in alignment with organizational strategies and priorities.
  • Skill in identifying, prioritizing, coordinating, and managing project resources, as well as planning and conducting hardware, software, network, and systems testing and evaluation.
  • Ability to provide advanced technical troubleshooting and support, develop technology solution roadmaps, oversee system upgrades and patching, and provide technical and policy recommendations to management.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, explain complex technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences, and establish effective working relationships with stakeholders, project teams, IT divisions, and developers.

SALARY: The expected starting salary range for external candidates is $46.73 - $59.59 per hour ($97,572 - $124,424 annually). The full salary range for this position is $46.73 - $72.45 per hour ($97,572 - $151,276 annually). This position is exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act and is eligible for State of MN employee benefits.

SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION

Position Logistics:

This full-time position is classified as an IT Architect. The position will work normal business hours, Monday-Friday. Work will be conducted in a hybrid environment, with in-person work required approximately 1 time per month at the Minnesota Judicial Center, in St. Paul, Minnesota.

APPLY: Complete and submit your online application with cover letter and resume attached by 11/30/2026, at 11:59 p.m. All employment offers are contingent upon satisfactory results of our background check processes.

description:
BigQuery

Data Engineer (Marketing-oriented) | Remote for Marketing Agency for Education

Our client is a fast-growing performance marketing agency specializing in mission-driven organizations across higher education and nonprofit sectors. Since launching in 2020, the agency has built a strong reputation for combining strategic thinking, creative execution, and data-driven marketing to help universities and organizations achieve measurable growth.

Company Overview:

Our client is a fast-growing performance marketing agency specializing in mission-driven organizations across higher education and nonprofit sectors. Since launching in 2020, the agency has built a strong reputation for combining strategic thinking, creative execution, and data-driven marketing to help universities and organizations achieve measurable growth.

Your Role:

The Senior Data Engineer sits at the center of the agency's Data and Analytics function, connecting every paid media platform and CRM the agency touches into a single, reliable source of truth. You'll own the full path data takes: from a client's ad accounts and CRM, through Adverity, into a BigQuery warehouse, through modular dbt/Dataform transformations, and out to the Looker Studio dashboards and automated Google Sheets reports the team and its partners rely on daily. Reporting to the Data and Analytics Manager, you're joining at a pivotal moment — the agency is scaling its roster of education and nonprofit partners, and this role is instrumental in evolving the automated reporting suite that makes that growth possible without sacrificing data quality or client trust.

You'll:

  • Own data ingestion & pipeline architecture — connect and maintain API pipelines from paid media platforms (Meta, Google Ads, LinkedIn, TikTok, programmatic) into Adverity, build custom Python connectors for anything not natively supported, and architect scalable pipelines from source system through to dashboard

  • Own CRM integration — build and maintain reliable CRM data connections (Slate, Salesforce, HubSpot) so lead and enrollment data flows cleanly into the warehouse

  • Own the data warehouse — route, optimize, and store raw and processed data in Google BigQuery; design efficient schemas for complex, multi-source marketing data (granularity, normalization, slowly changing dimensions); manage partitioning, clustering, and storage strategy to control query cost and performance

  • Own transformation & mapping — build SQL schemas that map, blend, and organize multi-channel data accurately for each client, in modular, version-controlled, documented dbt or Dataform pipelines, with standardized naming conventions and metric definitions across platforms and clients

  • Own CI/CD & data segregation — maintain CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, automated testing) for robust, version-controlled releases, and enforce strict data segregation across multi-client environments

  • Enable the reporting layer — create clean, performant data views built specifically for fast Looker Studio dashboards and automated Google Sheets reports, and partner with the Data and Analytics Manager and client teams to translate reporting requirements into warehouse models

  • Drive data quality — monitor pipeline health, resolve API breaks, minimize latency, implement validation frameworks and automated testing, troubleshoot discrepancies to root cause across source/warehouse/BI layers, and proactively flag data quality risks to leadership

You Bring:

  • 5+ years of hands-on data engineering experience, ideally in a marketing or agency environment

  • Strong experience configuring datastreams, transformations, and destinations in Adverity or a comparable ETL platform (Fivetran, Supermetrics, Funnel)

  • Intermediate to advanced SQL, with proven BigQuery experience in transformation, partitioning, and modeling

  • Expertise in dbt or Dataform, managing modular, version-controlled, documented SQL transformation pipelines

  • Python proficiency for custom API connections and pipeline automation

  • Experience with CRM data flows and integrations (Slate, Salesforce, and/or HubSpot)

  • A deep understanding of marketing metrics (ROAS, CPA, CAC) and paid platform schemas, with a proven track record of structuring data to optimize Looker Studio performance

  • Proficiency with Git and collaborative development workflows, and proven ability to manage multi-client data environments with strict data segregation

  • An analytical, solution-driven mindset with a growth orientation, and strong communication skills that turn complex data workflows into clear narratives for non-technical audiences — education marketing experience (traditional or online) is especially valued

  • 10+ years of professional Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Platform Engineering, or related experience.

  • Strong software development experience with:

    • Python

    • Go

  • Strong experience designing and consuming REST APIs.

  • Hands‑on experience building data ingestion pipelines, connector frameworks, integration platforms, or similar systems.

  • Experience integrating complex enterprise systems and third‑party platforms.

  • Solid understanding of both SQL and NoSQL databases.

  • Production experience with at least one major cloud platform:

    • AWS

    • Azure

    • GCP

  • Experience working with Docker and Kubernetes.

  • Strong understanding of Git-based development workflows and CI/CD practices.

  • Experience designing reliable, scalable, and production-ready distributed systems.

  • Strong debugging skills across APIs, infrastructure, networking, application services, and data pipelines.

  • Experience working directly with customers, stakeholders, or technical partners.

  • Ability to translate complex customer requirements into pragmatic technical solutions.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to operate effectively in customer-facing technical conversations.

  • High degree of autonomy and ownership when solving ambiguous technical problems.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience integrating AI-driven insights or machine learning models into marketing data pipelines to sharpen predictive analytics and data utility

  • Familiarity using AI or LLM tools to optimize performance forecasting, automated audience segmentation, or marketing workflows

  • Experience connecting, managing, and maintaining APIs for generative AI platforms within a marketing data architecture

  • Experience using AI/ML-driven anomaly detection to monitor pipelines and proactively flag data quality issues

What’s Offered:

  • Remote role with the flexibility that comes with a distributed, async-friendly team

  • Competitive compensation based on experience and location

  • A pivotal, high-visibility seat on a scaling Data & Analytics team, with real ownership over the agency's reporting infrastructure

  • The chance to build the data backbone for an agency whose partners are education and nonprofit organizations working to build a better world

  • A culture built around finding a better way, playing as a team of A-players, and treating results as the engine rather than the goal

  • Direct impact: the pipelines and models you build directly shape how partners see (and trust) their own performance data

Interview Process:

  • Screening Call with Atomic HR
  • Hiring Team Interview (walkthrough of a pipeline or data model you've built)
  • Technical Assessment (a real-world data engineering case study)

title: Senior Product Manager, Environmental Systems
description:
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Environmental Systems team. You will be responsible for the product strategy, roadmap, and execution to streamline, analyze, and drive decisions. This means creating intuitive experiences for extremely complex and nuanced data sets, collaborating with internal clients and engineering - and heavily leveraging AI tools and frontier LLMs - to bring an early-stage product to a larger market.

We work cross-functionally and you will partner daily with our engineers (AI and traditional software), designers, environmental experts, Apple system owners, and stakeholders to build impactful software products, specifically unlocking new product experiences. We believe in going deep on user research and data analysis to decide where we should go next with our products, we believe in delivering iterative features quickly and continuously improving our products and processes, and we are a strong design and product-led organization. We love talking to and working with our users every day to enable them to do their best work.

We want someone who has experience taking an idea from the whiteboard to production and then scaling it. You are going to get to do that again here.

The applications we build are used daily by people across Apple who drive our supply chain and environmental initiatives, as well as those who scale them globally. Our partners include environmental and supply chain experts, carbon modeling specialists, product designers, supply chain managers, and our global suppliers. We work closely with these groups to build software platforms that turn complex, high-stakes environmental data into clear operational decisions. In this role, you will:

Lead Product Strategy & Roadmap: Define and drive the multi-year vision, strategy, and execution roadmap for our environmental platforms, balancing immediate operational needs with long-term strategic commitments. Shape Supplier & Enterprise Systems: Lead the definition and scaling of supplier-facing data intake platforms, auditable environmental reporting tools, and internal analytical systems used across Apple. Drive Generative AI & Agentic Capabilities: Identify high-leverage opportunities to integrate LLMs, agentic workflows (including MCP), and automated tools into daily workflows—defining clear use cases, human-in-the-loop guardrails, and success criteria. Deep Discovery & Problem Definition: Spend time with end users—from hardware engineers and carbon modelers to suppliers—to synthesize complex, ambiguous problems into clear, actionable product requirements and specifications. Cross-Functional Orchestration: Partner daily with engineering, product design, environmental domain experts, and Apple business owners to establish sprint priorities, unblock technical constraints, and make principled trade-offs. Define Metrics & Measure Impact: Establish quantitative and qualitative success metrics for feature adoption, data fidelity, and decision velocity; use telemetry and user feedback to continuously iterate post-launch. Executive Communication: Clearly articulate product rationale, trade-offs, and progress to cross-functional partners, working groups, and executive leadership.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related technical or scientific field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 5+ years of product management experience, preferably building complex tools and systems
  • 8+ years of experience working with software product teams, either in a product role, or design or engineering
  • Professional experience building AI products using MCP and Agents
  • Product-first mindset, and the demonstrated ability to define and build intentional product processes that are shared cross-functionally
  • Demonstrated ability to craft and effectively communicate a product vision, strategy, and roadmap, and the ability to inspire the product team to execute upon these artifacts
  • Demonstrated use of user research, usability studies, analytics and data to drive business decisions and prioritize, as well as the ability to distill this work quickly into impactful decisions that move the team and product forward

Preferred Qualifications

  • Craft and set the product vision & strategy
  • Create use cases and user stories and communicate them effectively to both design and software engineering
  • Build and prioritize an ambitious but iterative roadmap that balances user needs with business and stakeholder priorities, as well as team needs
  • Ship experiences that are delightful to our users
  • Deeply understand and empathize with our users’ needs and pain points
  • Present and communicate product decisions, roadmaps, and long-term goals to the product team, stakeholder groups, and organizational leadership

title: Director Partnerships
description:
The Director Partnerships at Hertz is accountable for owning and growing our ‘Non-Air’ partner segment. Using your significant network within the Financial (inclusive of challenger / legacy consumer finance, banking and credit cards), Loyalty (inc. affinity programmes & cashback), Auto Association, Insurance, Employee Benefits, Travel and Accommodation sectors, you will build and execute a pipeline of opportunities to meaningfully grow the portfolio to a leading position. You will own the lifecycle of our partnerships from identifying and planning the acquisition of new partners, to their implementation and year-on-year growth. Working with the wider EMEA Partnerships team, you will deliver executive reporting on progress, as well as act as the key point of contact with the partners you win, to ensure a robust roadmap of growth-driving activity is in-place and continuously fit-for-purpose.

A Day in the Life:

As our Director Partnerships, you’ll be continuously building and balancing priorities of a pipeline of new opportunities, accounting for changing market conditions and internal /partner resourcing, to ensure a rapid, steady pace of delivery, backed by robust back-fill. This role will focus heavily on business development activities – meeting new and advanced prospects regularly, in-person across the EMEA region. Building critical internal links to ensure buy-in and support for implementation of new opportunities will be equally critical, partnering daily with internal teams such as Revenue Management, Technology & Product, Operations, Fleet, Legal and Marketing.

Reporting to Senior Director Partnerships (Sales & Marketing EMEA), this role will be based in Uxbridge, UK, with daily interaction with stakeholders at all levels of seniority throughout Hertz’ global organisation.

What You’ll Do:

· Partner Prospecting & Outreach – identifies prospects, builds business plan / proposal, owns engagement plan

· Wins & Implements New Business – Owns and executes the plan, prioritising for longer vs. shorter-term Pipeline, Owns commercial negotiations, contracting and implementation of business to hand over to BAU Partnerships colleagues

· Leads & motivates a dedicated team

· Collaborates daily with Partnerships colleagues on handover of new business into BAU

· Utilises Tableau, Salesforce, MS365 suite (esp. Excel, PowerPoint), internal/ franchise/partner reporting and administration tools (e.g. Meili & CarTrawler dashboards / reports) to drive insight on new opportunities and early growth of recent wins

· Collaborates with Revenue Management, Technology & Product, Operations, Fleet Planning, Marketing and 3rd Party Technology providers

· Creates / Develops Pipeline, Account Planning / Roadmaps, Implementation Plans

· Contributes to department performance by meeting key metrics such as Revenue (via delivery of high-yield opportunities and timely implementation of new opportunities), Efficiency

What We’re Looking For:

· Bachelor’s Degree (e.g. Business Studies, Marketing) required, Master’s Degree (e.g. MSc/MBA) desired, 7-10+ years of experience

· Expert proficiency in creating compelling, visual and data-rich plans and stories – high degree of competence in Excel (including strong data manipulation skills), PowerPoint, and Power BI / Tableau or similar required

· Self-starter and strong finisher, with the ability to collaborate with internal and external stakeholders across multiple functions and locations, up to an executive level

· Flexible and adaptable; ability to work effectively in ambiguous situations

· Excellent verbal and written communication skills, particularly presentation production and delivery to an executive audience

· Results driven, ability to make decisions and help solve problems proactively

· Ability to influence stakeholders at all levels (from peers to executives) and keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced environment.

· Ability to see the big picture and drive process change according to the needs of the organisation

· Excellent organisation, time management, delegation, and prioritization skills.

What You’ll Strive For:

· Transformative growth

· Rapid conversion from prospect-to-partner, with a hunger to go beyond the Pipeline ‘as-is’

· Proactively owning the growth agenda by keeping in-tune with new trends and technology to identify emerging segments before our competitors

What You’ll Get:

· Bonus

· Company car or car allowance

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Ads
description:
Apple is where we use the power of technology to enrich people's lives. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other's ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It's the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you'll do more than join something — you'll add something.

Join the Apple Ads Engineering team and help build an advertising platform that benefits both customers and advertisers. Our technology makes advertising possible on the App Store, Apple News, Stocks, and Apple TV — helping people discover content, supporting creators and publishers, and connecting advertisers of all sizes with engaged audiences, all with the unwavering commitment to privacy you expect from Apple. In this role, you will design, develop, and launch the highly-performant, internet-scale backend systems that select and deliver the right ads in real time, collaborating across engineering, product, and infrastructure to bring elegant solutions into production at Apple scale.

At Apple Ads, we are building the next generation of privacy-focused advertising capabilities. Our team builds the data foundation for real-time retrieval systems. We generate and deliver data at scale, and we make sure it's correct, so these systems return the right results quickly and reliably. We work across real-time, near-real-time, and batch processing to give retrieval fresh, accurate, high-volume data. You will work cross-functionally to ensure that correct data is available for real-time selection, and that observability and flexibility are provided for stakeholders. While this role focuses on the candidate ingestion part of Apple Ads, we are not constrained by organization structure and offer the flexibility to contribute across a variety of backend systems, including opportunities to apply algorithmic search, machine learning, NLP, and AI to hard data ingestion problems. You will write clean, efficient, well-documented code, participate in code reviews, and mentor other engineers on the team. Collaboration with internal partners across indexing, search, serving, operations, and program management to define requirements and deliver high-quality solutions is essential. You should be passionate about building products that protect user privacy and thrive in a fast-paced environment with rapidly changing priorities — and have fun doing it.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 6+ years of industry experience building distributed, scalable data pipelines and data systems
  • Proven experience solving large-scale data problems: petabyte-scale datasets, high-throughput streaming, or complex batch processing
  • Hands-on experience building data pipelines and platformizing the repeated patterns
  • Deep expertise in distributed data processing technologies such as Spark, Flink, and Kafka
  • Strong programming skills in Scala, Java, Python, or Go, and the ability to pick up new technologies on your own
  • Strong computer science and distributed systems fundamentals, including partitioning, replication, fault tolerance, and consistency models
  • Experience building and running systems in the cloud (for example AWS S3, EC2, EKS/Kubernetes) and/or on premises
  • A track record of delivering complex software on time across many cross-team dependencies Productive use of AI coding tools in real delivery
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across large distributed systems
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to influence technical direction across teams
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience owning the architecture and long-term roadmap of a data platform or major platform component
  • Experience designing self-serve tools, such as declarative pipeline definitions, onboarding automation, or internal developer platforms for data
  • Experience with streaming and event-driven ingestion, deduplication, late-arriving data, parity and reconciliation, and stateful stream processing
  • Experience with metadata management, data catalogs, lineage, and data quality frameworks
  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration (for example Airflow) and infrastructure-as-code
  • A history of driving measurable improvements in reliability, efficiency, or cost at scale
  • Familiarity with privacy-preserving system design and data-handling practices
  • Contributions to open source distributed systems or data projects
  • Experience in advertising, recommendation, or large-scale retrieval systems is a big plus
  • Comfortable with ambiguous requirements

title: Procurement Data Analyst
description:
About the role

The Procurement Analyst is a foundational role within Prime's Global Supply Chain & Procurement function, designed for a motivated early-career professional who wants to build deep procurement expertise from day one. You will support the operational and analytical engine of our procurement team — processing requisitions, coordinating vendor onboarding, assisting with contract administration, and helping to maintain the data and reporting infrastructure that keeps our programs running.


You will work directly alongside experienced procurement managers and directors, gaining hands-on exposure to OFCI equipment sourcing, supplier relationship management, and large-scale capital program execution. You won't be filing paperwork in a back office — you'll be embedded in the work, learning by doing, and growing into broader responsibilities as you develop your skills and commercial instincts.


The Procurement Data Analyst function is young, growing fast, and deliberately built to operate above its weight class. This is a team where early-career professionals get real exposure to complex commercial programs — and where strong performers move quickly. If you're looking for a place to learn procurement the right way, from the ground up, this is it.


What you'll do

Requisition Intake & Purchase Order Support

• Receive, review, and process purchase requisitions, ensuring required information is complete and routed correctly for approval.

• Assist in drafting and issuing Purchase Orders under the guidance of senior procurement team members.

• Maintain accurate PO logs and open commitment trackers, flagging discrepancies or missing confirmations to the appropriate manager.

• Follow up with internal stakeholders and suppliers to confirm delivery schedules and resolve basic order status inquiries.

Contract Administration Support

• Assist in the administration of procurement contracts, including tracking key dates, milestones, and renewal windows.

• Help maintain the centralized contract repository, ensuring executed agreements are accurately filed and accessible.

• Support internal signature and approval workflows for contracts and amendments.

• Learn to work with standard contract templates and flag areas requiring legal or management review.

Vendor Onboarding & Supplier Data

• Coordinate the vendor onboarding process, collecting required documentation such as intake forms, insurance certificates, and compliance records.

• Enter and maintain accurate supplier information in procurement and ERP systems, ensuring records are complete and up to date.

• Communicate with vendors during the onboarding process to gather missing information and resolve setup issues.

• Partner with Accounts Payable to ensure new suppliers are correctly configured for payment processing.

Vendor Risk & Compliance Support

• Assist in maintaining vendor risk registers, tracking the status of supplier compliance documentation such as insurance, certifications, and safety records.

• Support baseline risk reviews by gathering publicly available supplier information and summarizing findings for manager review.

• Flag suppliers with lapsed documentation or identified compliance gaps to the relevant category manager.

• Help track contractual obligations and delivery commitments, escalating deviations as directed.

title: LNG Sr Engineer/LNG Sr Engineer II
description:
BHE GT&S has an exciting career opportunity for an LNG Sr Engineer/LNG Sr Engineer II at our Cove Point LNG facility located in Lusby, MD.

The LNG Sr Engineer/LNG Sr Engineer II reports to the Manager-LNG Operations (Maintenance) and is a member of multi-disciplined team responsible for the safe, compliant and reliable operation and maintenance of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) import/export and re-gasification terminal combustion turbines and steam turbines including LNG process system infrastructure, power/steam generation rotating machinery and auxiliary support systems.

The LNG Sr Engineer/LNG Sr Engineer II provides advanced turbine mechanical maintenance technical expertise, technical oversight, and hands-on leadership for all turbine maintenance activities performed at the facility. This role serves as the turbine subject matter expert (SME) for combustion turbines, steam turbines and associated turbine equipment typically found in large-scale industrial environments such as LNG terminals, power generation facilities, chemical and petrochemical plants, manufacturing operations, NGL processing facilities, cryogenic natural gas processing plants, and other hydrocarbon facilities.

The LNG Sr Engineer/LNG Sr Engineer II applies deep mechanical knowledge and significant, relevant turbine experience to independently execute and guide others through the most complex turbine maintenance, troubleshooting, inspections, and repairs. The position leads mechanical technical work in the field, ensuring safe execution, configuration‑compliant maintenance practices, and high‑reliability operation of turbine assets.

This position also supports turbine outage planning and execution by contributing to both planned and forced outages, turnarounds, and major overhauls in supporting outage scope development, work sequencing, and execution strategies, as well as developing detailed work plans, schedules, and resource requirements. It also includes reviewing outage work packages, contractor proposals, parts list and technical documentation to ensure work is technically sound, properly scoped, and executed to high maintenance and reliability standards.

The successful candidate must be willing to work in an industrial environment and will be responsible for the mechanical reliability of the facility’s turbines while ensuring the facility operates in full compliance with site, company, local, state, and federal policies, regulations, and procedures while also supporting continuous improvement, reliability initiatives, and cross-functional coordination. A strong commitment to safety and adherence to established protocols is essential to maintain the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of the terminal.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Perform all activities with emphasis on a proactive and preventative maintenance approach based on industry’s best practices, manufacturer recommendations, and regulatory requirements to include but not limited to: FERC, PHMSA, NFPA, USCG, DOT, MDOL, MDE and EPA.
  • Recognizes the safety, environmental and facility reliability consequences of actions taken maintaining the highest levels of safety and environmental compliance.
  • Provide technical guidance in the creation and implementation of turbine mechanical maintenance policies, procedures, condition-based assessments, maintenance plans, and work methods for multi-skilled maintenance teams.
  • Provide technical guidance and leadership to the operations and maintenance teams (internal and contractor) in the operation, maintenance, and repair of facility turbines.
  • Provide technical guidance in troubleshooting and repair activities of turbine and turbine auxiliary equipment including but not limited to fans, pumps and motors.
  • Provide technical input for turbine maintenance planning, prioritization, and execution, including review of parts lists, drawings, procedures, and technical documentation.
  • Provide technical guidance in the creation and implementation of turbine mechanical maintenance policies, procedures, condition-based assessments, maintenance plans, and work methods for multi-skilled maintenance teams.
  • Conduct turbine equipment failure investigations and root causes analysis (RCA) recommending and implementing corrective actions to improve equipment reliability.
  • Identify systemic turbine reliability issues and develop corrective and preventive actions to eliminate repeat failures and improve equipment availability.
  • Support turbine long‑term maintenance and asset lifecycle planning through condition assessments, remaining‑life evaluations, and failure analysis to drive continuous improvement and informed decision‑making.
  • Support planning major turbine outages, turnarounds, and overhauls, including scope development, work sequencing, execution strategies, and technical review of work packages and contractor proposals.
  • Physically lead and direct large‑scale turbine mechanical maintenance projects in the field, providing hands‑on technical oversight, work execution control, and real‑time troubleshooting during critical activities.
  • Utilize a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) (Maximo and Oracle) to manage assets, work orders, inventory, and scheduling to increase efficiency, reduce downtime, and streamline maintenance operations with a proactive approach.
  • Support cost forecasting of short-term and long‑term major turbine maintenance OPEX and CAPEX budgets.
  • Provide technical review and input to Management of Change (MOC) processes for turbine mechanical modifications.
  • May perform other duties as assigned.
  • Preferred: Extensive mechanical turbine experience in a similar type of role in LNG, power generation, petrochemical, cryogenic gas processing, or similar large-scale industrial facilities. Prior experience in outage management, project leadership, or supervision. GE Frame 7EA, GE Frame 5, and/or GE Frame 3 combustion turbine experience is a plus. Maximo and Oracle experience is a plus. Inventory Management experience is a plus.

****Relocation assistance for this position is available dependent upon meeting eligibility requirements.

****Please note that this position DOES NOT support any type of sponsorship.

title: Jr. Information Security Engineer| Information Security
description:
Job Overview

We are seeking a passionate and driven Junior Information Security Engineer to join our growing Information security team. In this role, your primary focus will be on Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT), with a heavy emphasis on Web Application Penetration Testing (WAPT).
You will work closely with senior engineers to identify, exploit, and help remediate security vulnerabilities across our digital assets.

Key Responsibilities

1. Security Testing & VAPT

  • Conduct regular Vulnerability Assessments and Penetration Testing (VAPT) on web applications, APIs, and network infrastructure.
  • Perform deep-dive Web Application Penetration Testing (WAPT) to identify flaws in logic, authentication, and session management.
  • Utilize Burp Suite Professional/Enterprise extensively for automated scanning, manual intercepting, fuzzing, and custom payload injection.

2. Analysis & Remediation

  • Analyze scan results and manual testing findings to eliminate false positives and document valid vulnerabilities.
  • Map findings against industry-standard frameworks like the OWASP Top 10.
  • Collaborate with development and engineering teams to provide clear, actionable remediation guidance for fixing discovered bugs.
3. Reporting & Documentation

  • Assist in drafting comprehensive technical security reports for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Keep security documentation, testing methodologies, and internal knowledge bases up to date.
Preferred Skills

  • Hands-on Experience: Strong foundational knowledge and practical experience using Burp Suite (Proxy, Repeater, Intruder, Collaborator).
  • Web Security Concepts: Deep understanding of web application architectures, HTTP protocols, and common vulnerabilities (e.g., SQLi, XSS, CSRF, IDOR, SSRF).
  • Tooling: Familiarity with other standard security tools such as Nmap, OWASP ZAP, Metasploit, Nikto, and Nessus.
  • OS Knowledge: Comfort working with both Linux and Windows environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 0-2 years of experience in Information Security
  • BSC/BE/B.Tech Computer Science/Information Technology or any similar degree
  • CISSP - Certified Information Systems Security Professional, CEH - Certified Ethical Hacker, ISO-27001 – Information Security Management Systems Lead Auditor, BSC (Burp Suite Certified Practitioner), OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional)
