As a Systems Engineer here at Honeywell, specializing in Gas Turbine Engines and Power Systems, you will play a pivotal role in leading specification development, process execution, and support System Architecture definition. You will provide high-level technical leadership across a diverse portfolio that spans both commercial and military aerospace programs. You will own System development scope, define complex propulsion and power generation requirements, and guide junior engineers. You will collaborate directly with Lead engineers to execute mission-critical programs, ensuring compliance with both civil aviation regulations and military defense standards.

Engine Architecture & Lifecycle Management

  • Own end-to-end lifecycle elements of gas turbine components or secondary power systems, including requirements derivation, allocation, tracking, and validation.

  • Lead System Integration and Verification (V&V) activities, defining engine test cell runs, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing, and flight test support plans.

Technical Execution & Compliance

  • Ensure System requirements are validated and decomposed to the subsystems and that verification plans are established by working with customers, stakeholders, and internal subject matter experts.
  • Incorporate Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) methodologies to model engine behaviors, logical architectures, and physical architectures.

Collaboration & Mentorship

  • Provide tactical guidance and engineering peer reviews for E1 and E2 systems engineers.
  • Interface directly with cross-functional teams (Aerothermal, Controls & Accessories, Turbomachinery, and Mechanical Design) to resolve engine-level technical bottlenecks.

MUST HAVE

  • Experience: Typically requires 4–8 years of progressive engineering experience, with a focus on gas turbine engines, auxiliary power units (APUs), or aerospace power systems.

WE VALUE

  • Technical Skills:
    o Proven experience with requirements management tools (DOORS, Jama, etc.) applied to propulsion systems.
    o Deep understanding of civil safety assessment processes (ARP4754A / ARP4761) or military safety/airworthiness standards.
    o Familiarity with the Systems Engineering "V" model as it applies to engine controls (FADEC), fuel systems, or thermal management
  • Direct experience with MBSE methodologies (SysML, Cameo) or transient engine performance simulation tools (NPSS, MATLAB/Simulink).

title: Temporary Researcher - Research Assistant, Zoology & Physiology (Bernard)
description:
Join Our Campus Community!

Thank you for your interest in joining the University of Wyoming. Our community thrives on the contributions of talented and driven individuals who share in our mission, vision, and values. If your expertise and experience align with the goals of our institution, we would be thrilled to hear from you. We encourage you to apply and become a valued member of our vibrant campus community today!

At the University of Wyoming, we are committed to creating a supportive and enriching workplace. To learn more about what we offer, please refer to UW’s Benefits Summary.

JOB TITLE:

Research Assistant

JOB PURPOSE:

Aid Bernard Lab with reviewing game camera footage taken in captivity at the Wyoming Game and Fish Department Tom Thorne / Beth Williams Wildlife Research Center at Sybille.

The purpose of this project is to evaluate pronghorn fawn behavior after being fitted with expandable GPS collars in a captive environment using camera trap technology. Specifically, we are interested in the following questions:

  1. Do GPS collars fit for larger ungulate species impede the natural behaviors of pronghorn fawns (i.e., minimize duration of movement, increased stress, etc.)?
  2. Do GPS collars intended for neonate ungulates expand appropriately on growing pronghorn fawns?

The chosen candidate will gain experience in game camera analysis, behavioral research, and engage with diverse stakeholders, including WGFD and University researchers. The chosen candidate will start at the beginning of the spring semester (January 2027) and work for approximately 12 – 16 weeks.

Candidate can be located in Laramie, WY, or Casper, WY.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Review footage taken in captivity at the Wyoming Game and Fish Department Tom Thorne / Beth Williams Wildlife Research Center at Sybille.
  • Conduct behavioral research.
  • Engage with diverse stakeholders, including WGFD and University researchers.

COMPETENCIES:

Safety Awareness

Consistency

Ability to Learn

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Undergraduate degree in biology, zoology, wildlife and fisheries science or related field

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

REQUIRED APPLICATION MATERIALS:

  1. Cover letter

  3. Contact information for four work-related references (references will only be contacted if you are selected as a finalist for the position).

On-Site: This position provides vital support to campus customers, and the successful candidate must be available to work and perform essential job functions on-site, understanding our location is at 7,220 feet above sea level (Laramie) or 5,150 feet above sea level (Casper).

HIRING STATEMENT/EEO:

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. In compliance with the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA), if you have a disability and would like to request an accommodation to apply for a position, please contact us at 307-766-2377 or email jobapps@uwyo.edu.

ABOUT LARAMIE:

The University of Wyoming is located in Laramie, a charming town of 30,000 residents nestled in the heart of the Rocky Mountain West. The state of Wyoming continues to invest in its only 4-year university, helping to make it a leader in academics, research, and outreach with state-of-the-art facilities and strong community ties. Located in a high mountain valley near the Colorado border, Laramie offers both outstanding recreational opportunities and close proximity to Colorado’s Front Range and the metropolitan Denver area. title: Logistics Cargo Tracking &  Dispatch Coordinator
description:
Logistics Cargo Tracking and Dispatch Coordinator


Location: Addison, TX

Pay: $22 - $23.31 per hour

Employment Type: Temp to Hire (90 day evaluation period)

Benefits: 401(k) , health insurance with company contribution, paid time off, and short-term disability and life insurance options

Shift Available: Weekdays and Weekends all shift available


We are committed to long-term growth and stability for our team members. All positions begin on a part-time basis with a clear path to full-time status, which is offered within the first 90 days based on individual performance and business needs.


Position Overview

First Responder Protective Services is hiring Flex and Part -Time Logistics Cargo Tracking & Dispatch Coordinators to support nationwide high-value cargo escort operations. In this fast-paced role, you'll monitor shipments from pickup through delivery, coordinate field personnel, communicate with clients, and maintain accurate operational updates. This position is ideal for candidates with experience in freight dispatch, transportation, fleet operations, track and trace, public safety communications, or other operations coordination environments. .

This is not a truck driving position, cybersecurity role, armed security officer assignment, or warehouse position. This is an office-based logistics operations and dispatch role supporting nationwide cargo escort operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Track high value cargo movements from departure through delivery using real-time GPS systems.
  • Monitor live camera feeds and other available security technology associated with active operations.
  • Conduct and document required check-ins with field escort personnel.
  • Communicate route progress, estimated arrival times, delays, stops, and delivery confirmations to clients.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to client phone calls, emails, and text messages.
  • Assign qualified field personnel to escort deployments based on availability, location, client requirements, and operational needs.
  • Confirm that assigned personnel understand pickup information, delivery information, reporting requirements, and client instructions.
  • Manage deployment schedules while helping control unnecessary overtime and travel expenses.
  • Arrange airfare, rental vehicles, hotels, and other necessary travel.
  • Track changes to flights, schedules, routes, pickup times, and delivery appointments.
  • Review GPS activity and field reports for route deviations, unexpected stops, missed check-ins, or conflicting information.
  • Maintain complete and accurate shipment monitoring logs.
  • Escalate communication failures, tracking interruptions, delays, incidents, and possible security concerns.
  • Support multiple active cargo movements while maintaining accurate records for each operation.
  • Handle confidential client, cargo, route, personnel, and shipment information with discretion.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify missing or conflicting information.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to remain organized while managing multiple active operations simultaneously.
  • Proficiency using multiple computer systems, browser tabs, email, GPS/tracking platforms, and messaging applications.
  • Ability to prioritize urgent situations while maintaining routine monitoring responsibilities.
  • Dependable attendance and the ability to work a full-time assigned schedule.
  • Ability to handle confidential cargo, client, route, and personnel information with discretion.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience in freight dispatch, track and trace, logistics, transportation, fleet monitoring, roadside assistance, emergency communications, public safety dispatch, or field service dispatch.
  • Experience working in a fast-paced operations, dispatch, transportation, or logistics environment.
  • Familiarity with GPS tracking systems, shipment monitoring platforms, or dispatch software.

Physical Requirements

  • Use multiple computer monitors simultaneously.
  • Frequently use a keyboard, mouse, and telephone.
  • Occasionally lift up to 20 pounds.
  • Ability to distinguish colors and read maps, GPS displays, and computer screens.

Essential Skills

  • Critical thinking
  • Problem solving

  • Multitasking

  • Decision-making
  • Customer service

Schedule and Work Environment

This is a Temp to Hire opportunity with an evaluation period of 90day. The dispatch coordinator will be supporting a 24/7 nationwide cargo operations center. Available schedules may include daytime, evening, overnight, weekend, and holiday shifts.

Some shifts may involve multiple active cargo movements, urgent client requests, travel changes, or operational issues. Other periods may be quieter and require consistent monitoring, accurate documentation, and sustained attention.

title: Individual Coach Analyst
description:
Position Summary

Bay FC is seeking an Individual Coach Analyst to join our team. Focusing on individual player development, the Individual Coach Analyst is an embedded, hands-on role connecting Bay FC's technical staff, performance analysis and data & analytics teams.

Working alongside other coaches, performance analysts, the Head of Data & Analytics and our youth coaches, this person is responsible for turning match and training footage into clear, individual development messaging for players. This role identifies each player's strengths and work-ons, supports the conversations that drive their on-pitch development, and makes sure every member of the coaching staff has fast, organized access to the right content.

The role leads Bay FC's positional profiles and player organizers, connecting individual development to the club's style of play and wider club identity. It will also support the player pathway, helping high-potential players make the transition into Bay FC's first team through open sharing of information with the youth coaches.


Responsibilities

Individual Video Analysis

  • Clip and review Bay FC matches and training sessions using Hudl Sportscode, with a focus on individual player actions, behaviors and decision-making
  • Organize individual player playlists to give all coaching staff quick, accessible access to each player's footage
  • Telestrate video to deliver strong, clear messaging to players that is consistent with the coaching staff's language and game model
  • Support the video capture of Bay FC first team training sessions
  • Support the live feedback processes in Bay FC first team training sessions
  • Support individual opposition preparation where appropriate, providing players with insight on the opponents they are likely to face


Player Development

  • Support the identification of each player's strengths and work-ons, in line with the club's positional profiles
  • Support player development conversations with the Head Coach and other members of the technical staff, preparing the video and data that underpin them
  • Support training sessions and the delivery of Individual Development Plan (IDP) work within sessions
  • Apply a strong tactical understanding and pattern recognition to identify recurring individual trends across matches and training
  • Support the youth coaches in transitioning high-potential players into Bay FC's first team through open sharing of information


Positional Profiles & Player Organizers

  • Develop and maintain the club's positional profiles, linked to Bay FC's style of play and wider club identity
  • Lead on the format and organization of all player organizers and visuals, ensuring a consistent Bay FC standard across the technical staff
  • Act as the main owner of best-practice organizers for each position, building a library of clips that shows what good looks like in every role


Data & Analytics

  • Work as part of the data & analytics team to create and use data profiles in individual player analysis
  • Translate & present individual data profiles to players in a clear and accessible way, connecting the data with the video context


Other Duties

  • Collaborate with the performance analysis team to develop and execute the goals of the department
  • Support the live in match analysis processes of the club
  • Communicate insights to players and staff with varying degrees of analytical knowledge
  • Show dedication to self-improvement and professional growth, taking on new responsibilities that enhance the capabilities of the department
  • Other duties as assigned.


THE BAY WAY

  • Team-first approach that prioritizes collective success and contributes to a high-performance culture
  • Leads with respect, fostering collaborative and inclusive environments
  • Demonstrates strong self-awareness, seeks feedback and adapts constructively
  • Builds trust and is sought out for credibility and reliability
  • Shows resilience and persistence in building strong networks and relationships


Qualifications

  • At least 2+ years of working in a video or performance analysis capacity within elite soccer (professional, collegiate, academy, etc.)
  • Advanced proficiency in Hudl Sportscode, including coding, clipping and playlist organization
  • Experience using telestration tools (e.g. Hudl Studio) to produce clear, player-facing video
  • Strong tactical background with the ability to recognize patterns of play at individual and team level
  • Strong talent identification and player development skillset
  • Strong data in soccer understanding. Ability to link metrics to player profiles
  • Experience creating and presenting data profiles for individual player analysis
  • Excellent communication skills, with confidence presenting to players and coaching staff
  • Experience supporting training sessions and Individual Development Plan (IDP) work, preferred
  • Excellent data analysis skills and understanding preferred
  • Coaching qualification (e.g. U.S. Soccer or UEFA license), preferred


Compensation:
The anticipated salary range for this role is between $80,000-$95,000, actual starting pay may vary based on a range of factors which can include experience, skills, and scope.

title: Software Engineer II - Machine Learning Engineer
description:

title: Planning & Scheduling Engineer
description:
About Us

At Technip Energies, we are more than just a leading engineering and technology company - we are pioneers committed to shaping a sustainable future. With thousands of talented professionals worldwide, we deliver innovative solutions to real-world energy challenges while fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment.
Join us on a one-of-a-kind journey where you can take pride in being part of the solution for the benefit of our planet, people, and communities.

Position Summary

The Planning and Scheduling Engineer defines project objectives in terms of duration and resources, develops and maintains an execution-aligned schedule, and monitors project status to support reliable forecasting. The role provides planning, monitoring, control, schedule analysis, and reporting support for projects and proposals, with a primary focus on home-office EPC activities and small engineering-services scopes.

The position works closely with the Head of Planning & Scheduling Department or the Project Planning and Scheduling lead, project and proposal teams, clients, partners, vendors, and subcontractors. The role may also supervise or train less-experienced colleagues, primarily on small and medium-size projects.

Key Responsibilities

Planning and Schedule Development

• Develop and maintain schedules that are compliant with the selected project execution strategy.

• Define and optimize the resources required across Engineering, Procurement, Construction, and Installation activities, as applicable.

• Develop the project summary timeline and support definition of the Project Breakdown Structure.

• Establish and maintain planning and scheduling methods, procedures, time schedules, physical-progress rules, dashboards, and reporting requirements.

• Coordinate with project stakeholders to integrate relevant planning inputs and maintain schedule consistency.

Monitoring, Control, and Forecasting

• Update schedules, monitor project status, and control progress against the approved baseline and contractual milestones.

• Assess schedule performance, identify deviations from standards or plans, and propose corrective actions.

• Prepare reliable forecasts for completion dates, durations, and resource requirements.

• Increase project-team awareness of key milestones, main durations, interfaces, and critical paths.

• Support client review and approval of the schedule baseline, reported progress, and milestone achievement.

Risk, Change, and Reporting

• Plan activities to mitigate schedule risks and support cost-efficient execution.

• Perform schedule risk analysis, where required, and communicate schedule exposure and mitigation actions.

• Estimate schedule impacts linked to changes and claims and contribute to Extension of Time analyses in the event of client-caused delay.

• Prepare clear, consistent schedule data, KPI reporting, dashboards, and management information.

• Provide project feedback and lessons learned to improve planning and scheduling methods and contribute to departmental statistics.

Team Support

• Provide planning and scheduling guidance to project and proposal teams.

• May supervise, coach, or train less-experienced colleagues on small and medium-size projects.

Role Dimensions and Key Interactions

Role Dimensions

• Works primarily on home-office activities for full EPC onshore or offshore contract scopes.

• Performs planning, monitoring, and control activities and may lead planning and scheduling for small engineering-services contracts, including conceptual and basic engineering scopes.

• Supports multiple stakeholders in a multidisciplinary, project-oriented environment.

Key Interactions

• Internal: Planning team and Project or Proposal team members.

• External: Clients, partners, vendors, and subcontractors.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

• Technical degree in Engineering or a related discipline.

• Moderate experience in project execution, planning, scheduling, or project controls (3 to 5 years)

• Good working knowledge of scheduling software, including Primavera P6 or an equivalent tool.

• Good knowledge of project controls requirements, procedures, and methods.

• Good knowledge of progress-measurement systems and Earned Value Analysis.

• Good knowledge of KPIs and project reporting systems.

• Fluency in English.

Role-Specific Knowledge and Skills

• Good knowledge of EPCI work processes and sequences.

• Ability to develop and communicate project summary timelines.

• Basic knowledge of schedule risk analysis and Extension of Time analysis.

• Basic knowledge of the Global Business Process Management System (GBPMS).

• Ability to identify deviations, analyze schedule information, and recommend practical actions.

• Solid analytical and problem-solving skills.

title: Technical Specialist - Lead (Turbine)
description:
BHE GT&S has an exciting career opportunity as a Technical Specialist Lead (Turbine) at our Cove Point facility located in Lusby, MD.

The Technical Specialist Lead (Turbine) reports to the Manager-LNG Operations (Maintenance) and is a member of multi-disciplined team responsible for the safe, compliant and reliable operation and maintenance of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) import/export and re-gasification terminal combustion turbines and steam turbines including LNG process system infrastructure, power/steam generation rotating machinery and auxiliary support systems.

The Technical Specialist Lead (Turbine) provides advanced turbine mechanical maintenance technical expertise, technical oversight, and hands-on leadership for all turbine maintenance activities performed at the facility. This role serves as the turbine subject matter expert (SME) for combustion turbines, steam turbines and associated turbine equipment typically found in large-scale industrial environments such as LNG terminals, power generation facilities, chemical and petrochemical plants, manufacturing operations, NGL processing facilities, cryogenic natural gas processing plants, and other hydrocarbon facilities.

The Technical Specialist Lead (Turbine) applies deep mechanical knowledge and significant, relevant turbine experience to independently execute and guide others through the most complex turbine maintenance, troubleshooting, inspections, and repairs. The position leads mechanical technical work in the field, ensuring safe execution, configuration‑compliant maintenance practices, and high‑reliability operation of turbine assets.

This position also supports turbine outage planning and execution by contributing to both planned and forced outages, turnarounds, and major overhauls in supporting outage scope development, work sequencing, and execution strategies, as well as developing detailed work plans, schedules, and resource requirements. It also includes reviewing outage work packages, contractor proposals, parts list and technical documentation to ensure work is technically sound, properly scoped, and executed to high maintenance and reliability standards.

The successful candidate must be willing to work in an industrial environment and will be responsible for the mechanical reliability of the facility’s turbines while ensuring the facility operates in full compliance with site, company, local, state, and federal policies, regulations, and procedures while also supporting continuous improvement, reliability initiatives, and cross-functional coordination. A strong commitment to safety and adherence to established protocols is essential to maintain the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of the terminal.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Perform all activities with emphasis on a proactive and preventative maintenance approach based on industry’s best practices, manufacturer recommendations, and regulatory requirements to include but not limited to: FERC, PHMSA, NFPA, USCG, DOT, MDOL, MDE and EPA.
  • Recognizes the safety, environmental and facility reliability consequences of actions taken maintaining the highest levels of safety and environmental compliance.
  • Provide technical guidance in the creation and implementation of turbine mechanical maintenance policies, procedures, condition-based assessments, maintenance plans, and work methods for multi-skilled maintenance teams.
  • Provide technical guidance and leadership to the operations and maintenance teams (internal and contractor) in the operation, maintenance, and repair of facility turbines.
  • Provide technical guidance in troubleshooting and repair activities of turbine and turbine auxiliary equipment including but not limited to fans, pumps and motors.
  • Provide technical input for turbine maintenance planning, prioritization, and execution, including review of parts lists, drawings, procedures, and technical documentation.
  • Provide technical guidance in the creation and implementation of turbine mechanical maintenance policies, procedures, condition-based assessments, maintenance plans, and work methods for multi-skilled maintenance teams.
  • Conduct turbine equipment failure investigations and root causes analysis (RCA) recommending and implementing corrective actions to improve equipment reliability.
  • Identify systemic turbine reliability issues and develop corrective and preventive actions to eliminate repeat failures and improve equipment availability.
  • Support turbine long‑term maintenance and asset lifecycle planning through condition assessments, remaining‑life evaluations, and failure analysis to drive continuous improvement and informed decision‑making.
  • Support planning major turbine outages, turnarounds, and overhauls, including scope development, work sequencing, execution strategies, and technical review of work packages and contractor proposals.
  • Physically lead and direct large‑scale turbine mechanical maintenance projects in the field, providing hands‑on technical oversight, work execution control, and real‑time troubleshooting during critical activities.
  • Utilize a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) (Maximo and Oracle) to manage assets, work orders, inventory, and scheduling to increase efficiency, reduce downtime, and streamline maintenance operations with a proactive approach.
  • Support cost forecasting of short-term and long‑term major turbine maintenance OPEX and CAPEX budgets.
  • Provide technical review and input to Management of Change (MOC) processes for turbine mechanical modifications.

  • Preferred: Extensive mechanical turbine experience in a similar type of role in LNG, power generation, petrochemical, cryogenic gas processing, or similar large-scale industrial facilities. Prior experience in outage management, project leadership, or supervision. GE Frame 7EA, GE Frame 5, and/or GE Frame 3 combustion turbine experience is a plus. Maximo and Oracle experience is a plus. title: Supervisor, Network Field Services
description:
The Network Field Services Supervisor will lead and enhance the capabilities of a team of Field Technicians who play a vital role in managing the logistics, installation, optimization, inventory management, and troubleshooting of network infrastructures across the university campus. This includes overseeing a wide range of network assets such as UPS devices, switches, routers, wireless access points, security appliances, and other network-related gear and spare allocation. In this strategic role, the Supervisor will collaborate extensively with customers, internal teams, vendors, and key stakeholders to evaluate, analyze, and resolve hardware and software network challenges. A critical component of this position is ensuring that the network field team consistently meets established service level agreements (SLAs) while building trust and upholding UCSF’s PRIDE values to maintain operational excellence.

During network crises, the Supervisor will act swiftly and decisively to mitigate disruptions and minimize downtime, safeguarding the continuity of campus operations. Additionally, the Supervisor will maintain effective communication channels with other IT divisions, providing detailed reports on network performance metrics and incident management. They will also oversee the development and delivery of cross-functional and customer training programs to promote user engagement, system proficiency, workflow efficiency, and maintain overall consistency.

The Network Field Services Supervisor will positively impact UCSF’s operations and culture by ensuring its IT infrastructure is reliable, secure, efficient, and effective in support of the university’s academic mission. This team member will advance UCSF’s mission by delivering exceptional IT services consistently across faculty, staff, and students while exemplifying UCSF’s vision, culture, and values.


The Supervisor receives assignments in the form of objectives with defined goals and expectations to achieve them. They provide directions to staff in alignment with established policies and management guidance. The Supervisor enforces UCSF standards and policies, building positive trust relationships with the team and conducting ongoing performance evaluations. They will address disciplinary actions as necessary.

This role involves recommending changes to enhance department policies and practices, identifying risks, and responding appropriately. The Supervisor is responsible for setting priorities, analyzing workflows, and ensuring the team operates efficiently and effectively.

Department Overview

University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is distinguished as a leading academic healthcare organization, home to groundbreaking discoveries, world-class education, and exceptional healthcare services. Beyond a focus on maintaining systems and resolving issues, we are committed to nurturing the potential of our team members and empowering them to excel. UCSF Infrastructure Services provides 24x7 support to the University community, upholding the highest level of responsiveness and reliability at all times for our customers. IS values innovation and excellence in ensuring secure and efficient IT services, regardless of the hour or complexity of the issue.

The Network Services team within Infrastructure Services holds a critical role in managing, maintaining, and developing the company's computer network infrastructure, particularly ensuring reliable technical accessibility for individuals engaged in vital medical and health research work. Their core responsibilities include providing secure internet and network services, managing IT services, and maintaining data systems. They support end-users, manage system updates, repairs, and connectivity issues, and play an essential role in troubleshooting network issues, optimizing performance, and implementing protocols. They also oversee software and hardware updates, and manage data storage, disaster recovery, and network resilience. Beyond this, Network Services provides specialized technical support to other employees in the organization, with a focus on those involved in medical and health research.

title: Lead LNG Technician (Plant Control Systems)
description:
BHE GT&S has an exciting career opportunity for a Lead LNG Technician (Plant Control Systems) located at our Cove Point facility in Lusby, MD.

The Lead LNG Lead Technician (Plant Control Systems) reports directly to the Supervisor-LNG Operations (Plant Controls System) and is a member of multi-disciplined team responsible for the safe, compliant and reliable operation and maintenance of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) import/export and re-gasification terminal Distributed Control System (DCS) including LNG process systems infrastructure, emergency response systems, power/steam generation rotating machinery and auxiliary control support systems.

The Lead LNG Technician (Plant Control Systems) is responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, repairing, and upgrading complex control systems that support LNG facility operations. This role provides technical leadership for the facility’s Distributed Control Systems (DCS) and associated process control and automation platforms.

Key responsibilities include the configuration, maintenance, optimization, and upgrade of DCS hardware and software, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs), Operator Training Simulator (OTS), alarm management systems, industrial networking infrastructure, system administration, and cybersecurity controls.

The position also supports the Operational Technology (OT) cybersecurity compliance systems, including asset inventory tools, application whitelisting, intrusion detection systems, password vault solutions, and disaster recovery platforms. The Lead LNG Technician (Plant Control Systems) ensures timely updates, compliance with cybersecurity standards, and the overall reliability, security, and availability of plant control systems.

The successful candidate must be willing to work in an industrial environment and will be responsible for the reliability of the facility’s Distributed Control Systems (DCS) while ensuring the facility operates in full compliance with site, company, local, state, and federal policies, regulations, and procedures while also supporting continuous improvement, reliability initiatives, and cross-functional coordination. A strong commitment to safety and adherence to established protocols is essential to maintain the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of the terminal.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Perform all activities with emphasis on a proactive and preventative maintenance approach based on industry’s best practices, manufacturer recommendations, and regulatory requirements to include but not limited to: FERC, PHMSA, NFPA, USCG, DOT, MDOL, MDE and EPA.
  • Recognizes the safety, environmental and facility reliability consequences of actions taken maintaining the highest levels of safety and environmental compliance.
  • Lead, coordinate, and execute DCS activities under the direction of the Supervisor-LNG Operations (Plant Controls System).
  • Work closely with and directly support the facility’s operations teams, providing control system technical expertise to ensure the plant control systems meet operational needs.
  • Respond to control system issues affecting facility operations, assisting with start-ups, shutdowns, and abnormal operating conditions, and implementing improvements that enhance operational reliability and performance.

title: Senior Architect - Routing Services
description:
Do you want to help design and implement the next generation of cloud networking?

Join our Routing Services team!

title: Knitwear Designer - Next Sourcing (Womenswear)
description:
Working Pattern: Typically 5 days in the office, with core hours flexible between 8am-6pm.

The Role
Next Sourcing is seeking a creative powerhouse to join our in-house global design hub. We are looking for a designer who lives at the intersection of high-fashion innovation and commercial viability. As our Womenswear Knitwear Designer, you will be the architect behind collections that are as wearable and profitable as they are trend setting.

We’re so much more than just a British retailer. From Istanbul to Shanghai, our Sourcing teams live and work in some of the most iconic cities in the world.

They're at the heart of finding, developing and delivering the products our customers love, wear and use every day. Located across the globe, our Next Sourcing teams specialise in all different parts of the sourcing operation, from design and technology to product development.

What You’ll Take On

  • Design the Full Womenswear Knitwear Range: Create everything from elevated, trend led basics to technical project based collections, ensuring a cohesive and modern aesthetic.
  • Translate Global Trends: Research and filter high level trends into "must-have" products that are relevant to the NEXT customer and commercially viable.
  • Inspirational & Development Travel: Embark on seasonal trips to key global cities for trend inspiration, as well as visiting our international factories and suppliers to oversee development and strengthen manufacturing relationships
  • Drive Rapid Design Cycles: Respond quickly to design briefs with high energy and precision, producing fast turnaround sketches and specs without sacrificing style.
  • Balance Cost and Quality: Design intelligently within strict price point guidelines, selecting the right yarns and stitches to maintain a premium feel at a competitive price.
  • Partner with Global Teams: Work daily with Buyers and Sourcing Specialists to align on range plans, and collaborate directly with Suppliers to ensure designs are executed to exact specifications.
  • Ensure Timely Delivery: Manage your workflow to meet tight production calendars, moving products from initial concept to "shelf-ready" samples on schedule.


What You’ll Bring

  • Knitwear Expertise: You have a solid background specifically in knitwear, with a deep understanding of yarns, gauges, and stitch constructions.
  • Design Software Mastery: Proficiency in Photoshop and Illustrator is essential; you’ll use these daily to create precise tech packs and high quality visual renders.
  • Industry Background: You have experience working within a large scale retailer or a high volume supplier, giving you a realistic understanding of the speed and scale at which we operate.
  • Supplier Savvy: Previous experience working directly with factories and various brands is a major plus, helping you navigate the transition from design to production smoothly.
  • Team First Mentality: You possess strong people skills and genuinely enjoy collaborating. You know how to build rapport with buyers, sourcing teams, and factory partners alike.
  • Resilience in Busy Moments: You stay organised and level headed when deadlines tighten, managing multiple projects without losing your creative spark or attention to detail.
  • Clear Communicator: You can articulate your design ideas effectively, whether you’re presenting a concept to a buyer or explaining a technical spec to a supplier.
  • Proactive Curiosity: You are genuinely passionate about fashion and always on the lookout for new opportunities, whether that’s a new sustainable yarn or a more efficient way to construct a garment.


Portfolio: We can’t wait to see your style!
Please ensure you attach your digital PDF portfolio to your application, as we won’t be able to consider your journey with us without it. We are looking for work that is trend-focused, demonstrating your ability to translate high-fashion concepts into commercially successful, elevated designs for the Womenswear Knitwear market! To help you put your best foot forward, we’ve put together a few top tips on what makes a portfolio stand out to our team.

Sponsorship
Candidates wishing to apply who would require sponsorship for this role will be required to meet the Home Office sponsorship requirements. For further information please see: https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa.

We encourage early applications for our roles, as our recruitment process begins as soon as the role is advertised. If we successfully fill the position, this advert may close earlier than planned.

At NEXT, we believe the best work happens when there are no barriers to collaboration. That’s why we are a Google-powered workspace. From your very first day, you’ll be using the full Google Workspace suite; Docs, Drive, and Meet, to stay connected and move fast. If your previous experience is rooted in other software suites, don’t worry! We’ll point you to a digital Google toolkit the moment you join, packed with handy guides and insider tips to help you transition smoothly and hit the ground running.

title: Senior Java Developer - Ai Focus (Spring Boot, Sql)
description:
Our client is a remote product studio that builds MVPs and custom software for startups and companies past the idea stage. Clients hire them for a fixed-scope MVP or for a product team billed by the two-week sprint, and the whole team uses AI coding tools every day.

They've been at it since 2020 and were profitable in 2025, with a 30% net margin. After building their own AI systems, they tripled monthly revenue with the same team size. Clients rate them 4.9 out of 5 in verified reviews, and the startups they build for have raised more than $25M in venture funding.

Your Role

You’ll join the team building workflow software for one of the studio’s clients: a live product that needs new workflow features while the existing ones keep running. The client's own engineers commit to the same repo, so every new table, permission and workflow goes in next to code someone else is changing. The weight is on the server side, from the SQL database on Azure up through the API, and you also build the React and TypeScript screens that sit on top.

AI coding tools draft most of the specs, tests and migrations. You direct them, read every diff line by line, and answer for what merges. If you'd rather write most of the code by hand, this probably isn't the right seat.

You report to the studio’s leadership and work day to day with the lead developer and the product manager, who sets the acceptance criteria for each sprint, success means delivering four to five features per two-week sprint, each verified before merge, and owning one area end to end (such as the task engine or the legacy migration) without breaking a live feature.

You Bring

  • 4+ years building full-stack web applications and releasing them to production
  • Experience working in a codebase you didn't write, learning its conventions before changing it
  • Hands-on work on workflow software where different user roles see different data, with approvals, task queues or state machines and an audit log or versioned history
  • React, TypeScript and SQL on Azure, including schema design and migrations
  • Daily use of Cursor, Claude Code or a similar AI coding tool on production work, with tests and CI behind it
  • Clear written and spoken English
  • Experience delivering in fixed-scope sprints with branches, code review and feature flags

Bonus Points

  • Work in a regulated setting such as finance, health or insurance
  • A migration from a legacy system, with reconciliation and duplicate review
  • Time as an outside vendor committing to a client's repo
  • Project rules, custom prompts or agent setups for AI coding tools that your team adopted
  • Spanish, since the platform is bilingual

What's Offered

  • Fully remote contractor role from LATAM, full time at about 40 hours a week
  • Core hours in US time zones, so your day overlaps with the lead developer and the product manager
  • An area of the product to own end to end, with your schema designs reviewed by the lead developer and the client's engineers
  • A team where AI-first delivery is already the daily routine, with tests, CI and feature flags as part of the normal process
  • A start in early November

Interview Process

  1. Intro Call: 30 minutes with atomic HR on your background and goals
  2. Leadership Screening: A short call, possibly with an async part first
  3. Product and Developer Conversation: How you take features from acceptance criteria to merge
  4. Take-Home Test: One feature like the real scope, built and checked

143L - Senior Data Engineer (Python/Go/Data Ingestion/Cloud) · Remote · LATAM

Get to Know Darwoft

At Darwoft, we build custom software solutions and partner with international companies to create high-impact digital products.

We are a Latin American technology company with a people-first culture, strong professional standards, and a long-term partnership mindset. We work with distributed teams, complex technical challenges, and clients whose technology has a direct impact on their businesses and users.

About the Project

We are partnering with an innovative cybersecurity company building a next-generation Identity Security and Identity Observability platform.

The product helps enterprise security teams understand how human users, service accounts, workloads, applications, and AI‑driven identities access systems across cloud, SaaS, network, endpoint, and on‑premise environments.

At the core of the platform is a highly data‑intensive architecture that collects and analyzes large volumes of events, logs, network telemetry, identity activity, and security signals. This information is processed to identify unusual access patterns, security risks, identity blind spots, infrastructure misconfigurations, and potential threats.

The platform integrates with complex enterprise ecosystems including identity providers, cloud platforms, SASE solutions, SIEMs, endpoint security tools, network infrastructure, and security services.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer focused on Data Ingestion, Integrations, and Collectors to become a key technical bridge between enterprise customers and the engineering organization.

This is not a traditional backend or internal data engineering position.

You'll work directly with customers to understand their infrastructure, data sources, security architecture, network topology, APIs, and workflows, then design and implement scalable mechanisms to ingest that information into the platform.

You'll combine data engineering, software engineering, solution architecture, cloud infrastructure, and technical consulting.

A major part of your mission will be building and evolving connectors and ingestion pipelines capable of integrating data from complex enterprise environments while maintaining reliability, scalability, security, and fast time-to-production.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design, develop, and maintain production-grade data collectors, connectors, and ingestion services.
  • Integrate enterprise data sources including identity providers, cloud platforms, SASE solutions, network infrastructure, endpoints, applications, security platforms, and SIEM systems.
  • Work directly with enterprise customers to understand their environments, data flows, APIs, security requirements, and integration constraints.
  • Participate in technical onboarding processes, from initial discovery and architecture design through production deployment.
  • Design scalable ingestion architectures for processing security events, logs, identity activity, network telemetry, and other high-volume data sources.
  • Build integrations using REST APIs, cloud-native services, event-driven architectures, and modern software engineering practices.
  • Develop backend services primarily using Python and/or Go.
  • Work with SQL and NoSQL databases to store, transform, query, and analyze high-volume data.
  • Build and operate containerized services using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Deploy and integrate solutions across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments.
  • Troubleshoot complex customer deployment and integration issues across application, infrastructure, networking, API, and data layers.
  • Optimize ingestion performance, reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency.
  • Collaborate with Solution Architects, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering teams.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor around customer data architecture, collection strategies, security integrations, and implementation best practices.
  • Identify recurring customer requirements and transform them into reusable connectors, platform capabilities, or improvements to the core product.
  • Contribute technical insights from real-world implementations to the product roadmap.
  • Support production adoption and continuously improve time-to-value for enterprise customers.
  • Participate in occasional customer‑facing technical sessions and, when necessary, onsite engagements.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of professional Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Platform Engineering, or related experience.
  • Strong software development experience with:
    • Python
    • Go
  • Strong experience designing and consuming REST APIs.
  • Hands‑on experience building data ingestion pipelines, connector frameworks, integration platforms, or similar systems.
  • Experience integrating complex enterprise systems and third‑party platforms.
  • Solid understanding of both SQL and NoSQL databases.
  • Production experience with at least one major cloud platform:
    • AWS
    • Azure
    • GCP
  • Experience working with Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Strong understanding of Git-based development workflows and CI/CD practices.
  • Experience designing reliable, scalable, and production‑ready distributed systems.
  • Strong debugging skills across APIs, infrastructure, networking, application services, and data pipelines.
  • Experience working directly with customers, stakeholders, or technical partners.
  • Ability to translate complex customer requirements into pragmatic technical solutions.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to operate effectively in customer‑facing technical conversations.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership when solving ambiguous technical problems.

Highly Relevant Experience

Experience with any of the following will be especially valuable:

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM)
  • Identity Providers (IdPs)
  • Identity Security
  • Cybersecurity platforms
  • SIEM systems
  • Security telemetry
  • Network security
  • Endpoint security
  • SASE / Zero Trust environments
  • Cloud security
  • Large‑scale event processing
  • Streaming architectures

Integration Experience

Previous experience integrating APIs or data from platforms such as the following is highly valuable:

  • AWS
  • Microsoft Azure
  • Google Cloud
  • Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory
  • Okta
  • Google Workspace
  • Duo
  • CrowdStrike
  • Zscaler
  • Palo Alto
  • Microsoft Defender
  • SIEM and security analytics platforms

Direct experience with every platform is not required. What matters is a strong track record of learning complex APIs and transforming heterogeneous enterprise data sources into reliable integrations.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with large-scale data processing or streaming platforms.
  • Experience designing reusable connector SDKs or integration frameworks.
  • Understanding of identity‑related security concepts such as authentication, authorization, credentials, service accounts, privileged access, and non‑human identities.
  • Experience with security events, audit logs, network telemetry, or cloud activity data.
  • Familiarity with event‑driven and distributed system architectures.
  • Experience deploying AI/ML‑enabled applications.
  • Exposure to LLMs, AI agents, or AI‑powered security applications.
  • Solution Architecture or Forward Deployed Engineering experience.
  • Previous experience in cybersecurity startups or high‑growth SaaS environments.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will be measured by your ability to:

  • Deliver successful enterprise integrations and deployments.
  • Reduce customer time-to-production.
  • Build reliable and scalable ingestion solutions.
  • Improve customer adoption and technical satisfaction.
  • Resolve complex integration challenges efficiently.

Job Summary:
Manage the obtaining, maintenance and monitoring of environmental and sectoral permits that enable the execution of the project in Argentina, ensuring that the engineering design, constructive planning and field activities comply with the applicable national and provincial regulations, with the commitments assumed before the authority and with the environmental standards of the client.
The position acts as a bridge between engineering and the regulatory authority: it translates the legal requirements into verifiable design criteria, anticipates the environmental restrictions that condition the layout and the construction sequence, and maintains a critical permit route aligned with the project schedule. Its performance is measured by the absence of regulatory detentions and by the technical quality of the information presented to the competent bodies.
Major Responsibilities:
Permission management
+ Preparing and keeping updated the project permits matrix, identifying competent body, submission requirements, legal deadlines and actual processing deadlines.
Prepare, review and submit the Environmental Impact Report and its biennial updates, along with the supporting technical documentation required by the provincial mining authority.
+ Managing the associated sectoral permits: water use and concession, effluent dumping, emissions into the atmosphere, hazardous waste management, soil movement, intervention of native vegetation and transport of hazardous substances.
+ Maintaining technical dialogue with provincial and national enforcement authorities, responding to observations, requests for additional information and audits.
+ Timely alert the permits that constitute a critical route and propose sequencing alternatives when a regulatory deadline compromises the schedule.
Environmental studies and assessment
+ Defining the scope of the environmental baselines - air quality, noise, surface and groundwater, soils, flora, fauna, glaciers and periglacial environment, archaeology and socio-economic environment - and technically supervise the consulting firms that execute them.
+ Reviewing consultant deliverables verifying methodological sufficiency, representativeness of sampling and traceability of data before its incorporation into the file.
+ Evaluating environmental impacts of the project, propose mitigation and compensation measures, and verify that they are reflected in the design criteria and technical specifications.
+ Estimating hours, costs and deadlines of environmental studies for their incorporation into the project budget and program.
Compliance, monitoring and interface with the project
+ Keeping track of environmental commitments derived from the Environmental Impact Statement and the permits granted, and periodically verify their compliance on the ground.
+ Providing the engineering disciplines with the environmental constraints applicable to the design - layout restrictions, exclusion areas, discharge limits and water management criteria - and verify their incorporation.
+ Preparing progress reports on the status of permits for the client and for the project management, with status, regulatory risks and mitigation actions.
+ Supporting the processes of citizen participation and relations with communities and local authorities, in coordination with the social area of the project and the client.
+ Issuing the environmental deliverables under the project's documentary control system, respecting the review scheme and the preparation, review and approval signatures.
Regulatory framework of reference
+ Dominating the Argentine environmental regime and its federal articulation: the Nation sets the minimum protection budgets and the provinces, as holders of the original domain of natural resources, are the enforcement authority that grants the permits. The following list is the minimum core required: Law 25.675, Law 24.585; Law 26.639; Law 24.051, Law 25.688, Law 26.331, Law 25.743, Law 25.831, Law 27.520, ILO Convention 169 (Law 24.071).
Education and Experience Requirements:
Level 1:
+ Requires a university degree in Environmental Sciences, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Natural Resources, Geological Sciences or Biological Sciences, with professional registration in the corresponding jurisdiction, between 5 and 8 years of professional practice in environmental management and permits, with at least 3 years in mining, energy or infrastructure projects in Argentina.
+ A graduate degree, major or diploma in environmental management, environmental impact assessment or environmental law is desirable.
Level 2:
+ Requires a university degree in Environmental Sciences, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Natural Resources, Geological Sciences or Biological Sciences, with professional registration in the corresponding jurisdiction, between 8 and 10 years of professional practice in environmental management and permits, with at least 5 years in mining, energy or infrastructure projects in Argentina.
+ A graduate degree, major or diploma in environmental management, environmental impact assessment or environmental law is desirable.
Required Knowledge and Skills:

+ Experience in direct interaction with provincial and national public agencies, and in technical supervision of environmental consultancies.

title: Senior Coordinating Event Producer
description:
Senior Coordinating Event Producer (Program Manager)

Los Angeles, California

Our Company
We’re more than just a workplace — we’re a community of people who care about doing meaningful work, supporting each other, and growing together. Whether you’re just starting out or looking to take the next step in your career, we believe in creating roles that energise, challenge, and inspire.


We’re committed to designing jobs that are sustainable, flexible, and aligned with your strengths — because we know that when work works for people, people do their best work.


Visit our Careers Portal to explore our culture, benefits, and current opportunities. You’ll find stories from our people and insights into how we work.


A Brief Summary

We are seeking an experienced, highly collaborative Senior Coordinating Event Producer with a strong background in program management, operations, and live event production to support global esports events.

This role sits at the intersection of event production, operations, and program management. The ideal candidate understands the fast-paced, often ambiguous nature of live events while bringing the structure, strategic thinking, and operational discipline needed to plan and execute complex productions consistently.

You'll partner with Event Producers, Production, Broadcast, Creative, Logistics, Product, and other cross-functional stakeholders to manage milestones, identify dependencies, track risks, facilitate decisions, and ensure teams have a clear understanding of priorities and deliverables.

Beyond managing existing workflows, you'll identify opportunities to improve them. This includes developing scalable processes, standardizing recurring activities, improving communication, and implementing systems that reduce reactive work and create greater visibility across events.

Success in this role requires more than strong organizational skills. We're looking for someone who can build relationships, navigate complex stakeholder dynamics, influence without formal authority, and introduce meaningful change while respecting the realities of live event production.


The position is based in Los Angeles, California, with domestic and international travel required to support global events. The role reports to Gravity Media's Service Delivery Manager, Studio Crewing Global Events.


What You'll Be Responsible For:

Program Management & Event Planning

  • Manage complex, cross-functional event programs from early planning and development through execution, delivery, and post-event evaluation.

  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve integrated workback schedules, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, and ownership structures.

  • Implement practical program management frameworks, including RAID, RACI, RAPID, decision logs, milestone tracking, and change control, adapting approaches to the needs of each event and team.

  • Identify risks and dependencies early, communicate potential impacts, and drive resolution before issues escalate.

  • Establish clear accountability, decision-making pathways, deliverable expectations, and definitions of done.

  • Monitor progress against milestones, flag schedule changes, and ensure teams understand critical deadlines and next steps.

  • Provide concise leadership reporting that clearly communicates progress, risks, decisions needed, and changes to plans.

  • Balance long-term planning with the flexibility required to respond to changing production needs.

Operational Strategy & Process Improvement

  • Evaluate existing workflows and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, accountability, and cross-functional alignment.

  • Design and implement repeatable and scalable systems, templates, processes, and best practices that support event planning and execution.

  • Use systems thinking and root-cause analysis to address recurring operational challenges rather than relying solely on short-term solutions.

  • Develop scalable processes that can be adapted and reused across events while accommodating unique production requirements.

  • Partner with program management and production counterparts across Riot Games esports properties to share learnings, align common workflows, and improve operational consistency.

  • Facilitate retrospectives, debriefs and post-event evaluations, consolidating feedback into actionable improvements for future events. Highlights and inclusion on event kickoffs from this intel gathered in an easily referenced and digestible way.

  • Help teams transition from reactive problem-solving toward more predictable, proactive event planning without compromising production agility.

  • Other job-related duties as assigned.


Cross-Functional Collaboration & Change Management

  • Build trusted working relationships with stakeholders across Event Production, Broadcast, Creative, Product, Logistics, and external production partners.

  • Drive alignment across teams with differing priorities, working styles, and levels of involvement.

  • Influence stakeholders without direct reporting authority, building buy-in and shared accountability for deliverables and decisions.

  • Lead change management efforts by introducing new workflows thoughtfully, communicating their value, and supporting adoption across teams.

  • Facilitate discussions, navigate competing perspectives, and resolve conflicts constructively.

  • Challenge existing processes diplomatically while maintaining strong relationships and respecting team expertise.

  • Establish clear communication practices that reduce ambiguity, unnecessary meetings, duplicated efforts, and disconnected decision-making.

  • Adapt communication style to different audiences, from individual contributors and external vendors to senior leadership.

  • Other job-related duties as assigned.


Event Production & Delivery Support

  • Support Event Producers in coordinating complex live esports productions, maintaining visibility across production milestones, deliverables, and operational needs.

  • Work closely with internal teams, production vendors, creative partners, and external stakeholders to ensure timely delivery of event requirements.

  • Coordinate cross-functional workflows related to ticketing, activations, co-streaming, partnerships, audience experience, and other event-specific initiatives.

  • Support creative and publishing deliverable tracking, including asset management, stakeholder reviews, feedback consolidation, and approval timelines.

  • Support as needed on communications and informational materials, including Know Before You Go messaging for attendees and invited guests.

  • Provide hands-on event producing and operational support when needed, particularly during critical planning periods and onsite execution.

  • Adapt quickly to evolving production circumstances while maintaining awareness of broader event priorities and dependencies.

  • Ensure short-term production demands are balanced with long-term program management and operational objectives.

  • Other job-related duties as assigned.


This Role Is for You If

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in program management, project management, operations, event production, or a combination of these disciplines.

  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional projects involving multiple teams, stakeholders, vendors, and competing deadlines.

  • Strong understanding of program and project management methodologies, including workback scheduling, dependency management, risk tracking, stakeholder alignment, and decision-making frameworks.

  • Experience designing, implementing, and improving operational processes, workflows, and systems, particularly in environments where established structures may be limited or evolving.

  • Familiarity with live event production environments and an understanding of the unique demands, urgency, and flexibility required to deliver large-scale events.

  • Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence, with a demonstrated ability to build trust, influence stakeholders, and navigate challenging team dynamics.

  • Experience driving change management initiatives, including securing stakeholder buy-in and successfully implementing new ways of working.

  • Ability to operate independently in ambiguous environments, identify gaps, take initiative, and move work forward without constant direction.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to escalate, and when additional alignment is necessary.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex information into concise, actionable updates for leadership.

  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities while remaining organized, adaptable, and solutions-oriented.

  • Experience facilitating discussions, managing disagreements, and driving cross-functional decisions.

  • Proficiency with collaborative project management tools and platforms such as Google Workspace, Airtable and Microsoft Office.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise sound judgment, and demonstrate professionalism in high-pressure environments.

  • Willingness to travel domestically and internationally and support the demands of live event production.


Preferred Qualifications

  • 2-5+ years Esports Production exposure across live broadcast, touring or other large scale global events/projects.

  • Familiarity with the unique production requirements of competitive esports, including broadcast operations, event production, and collaboration between game publishers and external production partners.

  • Experience supporting multiple concurrent events or programs across different regions, teams, or business units.

  • Proven success introducing operational structure and process improvements into fast-paced, creative, or production-focused organizations.

  • Experience partnering with senior leadership and navigating complex stakeholder relationships.

  • PMP certification or equivalent formal program management training.


What Success Looks Like

  • Event teams have clear visibility into milestones, responsibilities, dependencies, risks, and upcoming decisions.

  • Potential issues are identified and addressed earlier, reducing unnecessary last-minute escalations and reactive work.

  • Own agendas, recaps, and the weekly priorities update for recurring event meetings

  • Teams spend less time chasing information, duplicating efforts, or navigating unclear ownership.

  • Repeatable workflows and standardized planning practices improve efficiency and consistency across events.

  • Stakeholders trust the program management process because it supports their work rather than creating unnecessary overhead.

  • Cross-functional relationships strengthen, communication improves, and teams become more aligned in how they plan and execute events.

  • Each event contributes meaningful lessons and operational improvements to the next.

Ultimately, success means helping talented production teams work more effectively together, enabling them to focus on delivering exceptional live events while building the operational foundation needed to support continued growth.

Job Summary:
Manage the obtaining, maintenance and monitoring of environmental and sectoral permits that enable the execution of the project in Argentina, ensuring that the engineering design, constructive planning and field activities comply with the applicable national and provincial regulations, with the commitments assumed before the authority and with the environmental standards of the client.
The position acts as a bridge between engineering and the regulatory authority: it translates the legal requirements into verifiable design criteria, anticipates the environmental restrictions that condition the layout and the construction sequence, and maintains a critical permit route aligned with the project schedule. Its performance is measured by the absence of regulatory detentions and by the technical quality of the information presented to the competent bodies.
Major Responsibilities:
Permission management
+ Preparing and keeping updated the project permits matrix, identifying competent body, submission requirements, legal deadlines and actual processing deadlines.
Prepare, review and submit the Environmental Impact Report and its biennial updates, along with the supporting technical documentation required by the provincial mining authority.
+ Managing the associated sectoral permits: water use and concession, effluent dumping, emissions into the atmosphere, hazardous waste management, soil movement, intervention of native vegetation and transport of hazardous substances.
+ Maintaining technical dialogue with provincial and national enforcement authorities, responding to observations, requests for additional information and audits.
+ Timely alert the permits that constitute a critical route and propose sequencing alternatives when a regulatory deadline compromises the schedule.
Environmental studies and assessment
+ Defining the scope of the environmental baselines - air quality, noise, surface and groundwater, soils, flora, fauna, glaciers and periglacial environment, archaeology and socio-economic environment - and technically supervise the consulting firms that execute them.
+ Reviewing consultant deliverables verifying methodological sufficiency, representativeness of sampling and traceability of data before its incorporation into the file.
+ Evaluating environmental impacts of the project, propose mitigation and compensation measures, and verify that they are reflected in the design criteria and technical specifications.
+ Estimating hours, costs and deadlines of environmental studies for their incorporation into the project budget and program.
Compliance, monitoring and interface with the project
+ Keeping track of environmental commitments derived from the Environmental Impact Statement and the permits granted, and periodically verify their compliance on the ground.
+ Providing the engineering disciplines with the environmental constraints applicable to the design - layout restrictions, exclusion areas, discharge limits and water management criteria - and verify their incorporation.
+ Preparing progress reports on the status of permits for the client and for the project management, with status, regulatory risks and mitigation actions.
+ Supporting the processes of citizen participation and relations with communities and local authorities, in coordination with the social area of the project and the client.
+ Issuing the environmental deliverables under the project's documentary control system, respecting the review scheme and the preparation, review and approval signatures.
Regulatory framework of reference
+ Dominating the Argentine environmental regime and its federal articulation: the Nation sets the minimum protection budgets and the provinces, as holders of the original domain of natural resources, are the enforcement authority that grants the permits. The following list is the minimum core required: Law 25.675, Law 24.585; Law 26.639; Law 24.051, Law 25.688, Law 26.331, Law 25.743, Law 25.831, Law 27.520, ILO Convention 169 (Law 24.071).
Education and Experience Requirements:
Level 1:
+ Requires a university degree in Environmental Sciences, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Natural Resources, Geological Sciences or Biological Sciences, with professional registration in the corresponding jurisdiction, between 5 and 8 years of professional practice in environmental management and permits, with at least 3 years in mining, energy or infrastructure projects in Argentina.
+ A graduate degree, major or diploma in environmental management, environmental impact assessment or environmental law is desirable.
Level 2:
+ Requires a university degree in Environmental Sciences, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Natural Resources, Geological Sciences or Biological Sciences, with professional registration in the corresponding jurisdiction, between 8 and 10 years of professional practice in environmental management and permits, with at least 5 years in mining, energy or infrastructure projects in Argentina.
+ A graduate degree, major or diploma in environmental management, environmental impact assessment or environmental law is desirable.
Required Knowledge and Skills:
+ Verifiable participation in at least one complete cycle of environmental processing: preparation of the study, submission to the authority, response to observations and obtaining the approving resolution.
+ Experience in direct interaction with provincial and national public agencies, and in technical supervision of environmental consultancies.
+ Previous experience in EPC or EPCM environments is desirable, with exposure to document control, change control and management of interfaces between disciplines. Mastery of the Argentine environmental regime described in the previous section and ability to track its provincial regulations.
+ Environmental impact assessment methodologies, design of monitoring plans and environmental management

title: Senior Cloud Data Platform Engineer (Remote)
description:
AgileEngine is an Inc. 5000 company that creates award-winning software for Fortune 500 brands and trailblazing startups across 17+ industries. We rank among the leaders in areas like application development and AI/ML, and our people-first culture has earned us multiple Best Place to Work awards.

WHY JOIN US

If you're looking for a place to grow, make an impact, and work with people who care, we'd love to meet you!
