About Darwoft

Darwoft is a software factory that develops custom software solutions and provides IT staff augmentation services for international clients, primarily in the United States and Latin America. We partner with startups and high-growth companies to build high-impact digital products. Our culture is people-first, focused on technical quality, long-term relationships, and a collaborative mindset. We combine technical excellence with human proximity.

Senior Software Engineer — Observability Migration | Contractor Global

General Information

  • Location: Remote (Global)
  • Contract Type: Contractor
  • Industry / Project: Fintech / Conversational AI & Infrastructure
  • Time Zone: Coordination with US / LATAM / Global teams
  • English Level: Advanced (C1)

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to support and execute a critical observability migration. In this role, you will lead the transition of our application and infrastructure telemetry from New Relic to a modern, OpenTelemetry (OTel) Collector-based architecture. You will be responsible for re-instrumenting applications, updating infrastructure manifests, validating telemetry outputs, and ensuring seamless monitoring coverage across our high-scale ecosystem without compromising operational visibility.

Key Responsibilities

  • Migrate existing application instrumentation, tracing, and telemetry configurations from New Relic to OpenTelemetry.
  • Update YAML configuration files, environment variables, and deployment manifests according to established architecture standards.
  • Execute unit tests and validation suites to verify that telemetry is accurately generated, transformed, and exported to target backends.
  • Perform telemetry gap analysis, comparing existing New Relic data against OTel outputs to identify missing traces, metrics, logs, or resource attributes.
  • Assist in updating dashboards, monitoring documentation, and troubleshooting guides to reflect the OTel architecture.
  • Investigate telemetry collection and export errors, identifying root causes and collaborating with core platform engineers on complex edge cases.
  • Maintain clear tracking and reporting of implementation progress, edge cases, and potential migration risks.

Requirements

Must-Have:

  • Proven experience in software engineering with proficiency in at least one modern language (Java, Python, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript).
  • Hands-on experience with OpenTelemetry (OTel) concepts, including distributed tracing, metrics, logs, and OTel Collector configurations.
  • Deep experience with cloud observability paradigms and transitioning off legacy platforms like New Relic.
  • Solid understanding of HTTP, APIs, environment-based configurations, and reading/modifying complex YAML/JSON manifests.
  • Strong background in software testing, debugging log analysis, and validating high-cardinality telemetry data.
  • Familiarity with modern software delivery workflows (Git, PRs, CI/CD pipelines).

Nice-to-Have:

  • Experience operating or configuring OTel Collectors in Kubernetes or containerized environments.
  • Knowledge of FinOps and cost-optimization strategies related to telemetry ingestion rates.

Key Deliverables & Success Criteria

  • Execution: Successfully updated application instrumentation, validated OTel Collector configs, and verified end-to-end telemetry delivery to designated backends.
  • Documentation: Updated technical documentation, migration checklists, and runbooks.
  • Quality & Continuity: Zero removal of critical monitoring coverage during the migration window, with all pull requests passing automated tests and code reviews.

What We Offer (Contractor)

  • Contractor agreement with payment in USD.
  • 100% remote work in an international setting.
  • Access to Argentine public holidays.
  • Direct involvement in modernizing core platform observability for a high-growth fintech ecosystem.
  • Professional development, learning platforms, and referral programs.

title: Anti Social Behaviour Officer
description:
• Ipswich Borough Council
  • Address: Ipswich, Suffolk IP1 2DE
  • Salary: £34,237 - £36,581 per annum
  • Hours: 37 hours per week
  • Contract: Permanent, required as soon as possible

Ipswich Borough Council is looking for an Anti Social Behaviour Officer.

Ipswich Borough Council is committed to creating safe, thriving communities and improving the quality of life for our residents. Our organisation is constantly growing and developing our services to meet the needs of Ipswich and the people who live here.

To support our commitment to tackling and reducing the impact of Anti-Social Behaviour (ASB), Community Support is seeking to recruit a dedicated and motivated Housing ASB Officer to join our ASB Team. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a meaningful difference within our communities by investigating and resolving ASB, supporting victims and working collaboratively with tenants, residents and partner agencies to deliver effective and sustainable solutions.

This role will manage a challenging and complex caseload involving Council tenancies, delivering a high quality, proactive and effective ASB management service, responsible for taking prompt and proportionate action to investigate reports of ASB, assess risk and vulnerability, gather evidence and implement appropriate interventions to resolve cases successfully.

Working closely with tenants, internal departments and external partner agencies, including Police and support services, you will build and maintain strong professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes, safeguard vulnerable individuals and improve the quality of life for our communities. The role requires excellent communication, problem-solving and case management skills, alongside the ability to utilise a range of informal and formal enforcement tools where necessary.

You will be responsible for:

  • investigating reports of high-harm ASB and tenancy breaches

  • assessing risk and vulnerability, ensuring victims and perpetrators receive appropriate support

  • developing and implementing action plans to resolve cases effectively

  • gathering evidence, conducting interviews and maintaining accurate case records

  • preparing, and serving, legal documentation and supporting legal proceedings including attendance at Court, where required

  • working closely with Police, support agencies and community partners

  • attending and facilitating multi-agency meetings and representing the Council where required

  • ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, policies and procedure

  • contributing to the delivery of a high-quality housing and community service.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and proactive individual who:

  • has the knowledge and experience of tackling high level anti-social behaviour, housing management or community safety cases

  • has a good understanding of legislation and the use of the formal, and informal, tools and powers under the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014

  • has excellent communication skills working confidently with tenants, partners and stakeholders

  • demonstrates excellent investigative, problem-solving and decision-making skills

  • is resilient and able to manage challenging situations professionally

  • has proven experience of building strong working relationships with customers, colleagues and external partners

  • can maintain accurate records and produce high-quality reports and witness statements

  • is educated to ‘A’ level standard or equivalent and has 3 years’ experience working in a Tenancy Management or ASB role in social housing

  • holds a full driving licence and has the ability to climb stairs.

Hours of work are 37 per week, Monday to Friday.

DBS clearance is required for this role.

This is a hybrid working role (with a minimum of 2 days per week working in the office).

Why work for us?

As well as a competitive salary, the Council offers Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) membership, subsidised parking for work and leisure, public transport discounts, free swimming and gym membership, cycle purchase scheme, learning and development opportunities, flexible working opportunities, wellbeing support, lifestyle benefits and the opportunity to work with great colleagues.

For further information, please email Sally Tynan on sally.tynan@ipswich.gov.uk

Leadership
The CSX Leadership Model is the foundation of our Talent Strategy and is what drives CSX performance. CSX accordingly selects and develops talent based on each of the following: producing results, creating change, and inspiring excellence.

NOV delivers technology-driven equipment, systems, services and software solutions supporting energy production and industrial operations worldwide.   • Install, commission and test diesel generator sets at onshore and offshore locations.

Essential Qualifications

  • NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical Engineering or an equivalent recognised mechanical trade qualification or apprenticeship.

  • Practical knowledge of diesel engines, fuel systems and associated generator equipment.
  • Knowledge of generator control systems and electrical distribution sufficient to support effective fault diagnosis.
  • Strong mechanical troubleshooting and problem-solving capability.
  • Ability to read and interpret schematics, wiring diagrams and technical manuals.
  • Ability and willingness to travel and work offshore when required.
  • Ability to meet the applicable medical and safety requirements associated with offshore work.

title: Lead Engineering Test Technician
description:
As a Lead Engineering Test Technician here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will play a critical part in the development and certification of next-generation gas turbine engines.

Working alongside engineers and technicians, you will take ownership of testing activities across flow, spin pit, bearing, seals, and lubrication system test facilities. Your work will directly support our mission to deliver accurate, high-quality data to customers—right the first time.

You will also help maintain and improve test facilities and processes that enable product development, certification, and long-term support across the full Engines & Power Systems product line.

You will report to the Sr Test Engineering Manager, and you will work out of the Phoenix, AZ job site on an in-person work schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary test technician for the setup, execution, monitoring, and teardown of tests involving mechanical components, including bearings, seals, gears, lubrication pumps, gearboxes, and related hardware.
  • Install, configure, and prepare test articles within the test cell, including mounting to test stands, establishing mechanical drive connections, connecting data acquisition systems, and completing required oil, fuel, and air system plumbing.
  • Execute tests in accordance with approved test procedures, operating instructions, and safety requirements.
  • Troubleshoot test equipment, instrumentation, and facility hardware to identify and resolve issues. Collaborate with engineering teams to investigate and determine root causes for complex technical problems.
  • Maintain accurate, detailed, and organized test records, logs, and facility documentation to support test execution, traceability, and reporting requirements.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe test environment while adhering to all laboratory and facility safety procedures.
  • Provide constructive feedback on test plans, test methods, tooling, and facility improvements to enhance test quality, efficiency, and safety.
  • Perform assigned work using engineering drawings, CAD models, build instructions, checklists, test procedures, and verbal direction from the responsible test engineer.
  • Take ownership of test execution activities and support all aspects of successful test completion, ensuring the delivery of high-quality data that enables informed engineering and product decisions

Work Environment & Schedule

  • Hands-on work in a lab and industrial test environment
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs and work with large mechanical equipment and powered industrial vehicles
  • Occasional outdoor work
  • Overtime as needed (up to ~20%)
  • Occasional travel (<10%)
  • Shifts may change depending on the test under execution. This role is primarily a 1st shift role.

YOU MUST HAVE:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 4 years of directly related experience as a Test Technician or 6 years of experience in an aerospace or other complex mechanical system technician role
  • Hands-on experience building, assembling, repairing, maintaining, or fabricating hardware
  • The ability to work off-shift (2nd or 3rd shift) – Shifts may change depending on the test under execution. This role is primarily a 1st shift role.

WE VALUE

  • Strong mechanical aptitude and comfort working with hand tools
  • Practical problem-solving skills with demonstrated experience on complex mechanical or electro-mechanical systems
  • Experience with mechanical components (bearings, gears, seals and lube systems).
  • Direct experience executing complex and/or unique gas turbine engine or component tests independently
  • Individuals who are self-motivated and able to work independently (bias for action)
  • Demonstrated ability to make timely decisions in the face of ambiguous and complex situations
  • Relevant advanced education (or equivalent military experience) supporting work being done in at Engines & Power Systems (i.e. A&P school/license)

FAA Employment Requirements

All applicants for placement in DOT/FAA safety-sensitive positions will be required to submit to a pre-employment drug test, testing for Marijuana, Cocaine, Amphetamines (amphetamine, methamphetamine, MDMA, MDA), Phencyclidine (PCP), and Opioids (codeine, heroin, morphine, oxycodone, oxymorphone, hydrocodone, hydromorphone). The DOT/FAA regulations require all employees, regular and temporary, in safety-sensitive positions, to be included in the Honeywell Anti-drug and Alcohol Misuse Prevention Plan.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENTS

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

title: Health Technical Advisor
description:
TITLE: Health Technical Advisor
TEAM/PROGRAMME: PDQI LOCATION: Cairo
GRADE: 2 CONTRACT LENGTH: Calendar year, with possibility of renewal

CHILD SAFEGUARDING: (select only one)

Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g.

once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

ROLE PURPOSE:

The Health Technical Advisor is responsible for providing strategic and technical leadership with a primary focus on Child Health, Sexual Reproductive health (SRH/ASRH), Maternal Newborn Health (MNH), and Health Systems Strengthening (HSS). Under the general direction and guidance of the Director of Program Development and Quality, provides thematic leadership and ensures that all health programming in both development and humanitarian contexts is well monitored and is of excellent technical quality, attracts significant donor funding and contributes to national/global learning, advocacy, and programme development. S/he is expected to lead on developing a health sector strategy and thematic plan, aligned with the country strategic plan; sectoral assessment; program design, proposal writing and master budgeting support; and provide strategic and technical guidance and oversight to project managers and field teams implementing health programming and related initiatives; and, represent Save the Children (SC) in inter-agency fora.

In the event of a major humanitarian emergency, the role holder will be expected to work outside the normal role profile and be able to vary working hours accordingly.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: PDQI Director

Staff reporting to this post: Technical program staff (dotted line)

Budget Responsibilities: No

Field Travel: The TA is expected to spend at least 50% of his/ her time in the field in governorates of greater Cairo, Aswan, Alexandria, Minia and Assiut.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Developing Strategy and Thematic Plan

  • Lead the development, periodic review, and implementation of the country health strategy, thematic plans, and emergency preparedness plans, ensuring alignment with the Country Strategic Plan and evolving contextual needs.
  • Provide strategic leadership on the health component of the Country Strategic Plan, ensuring coherence across child health, maternal and newborn health, adolescent health, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and systems‑strengthening priorities.
  • Apply systems‑for‑health thinking to inform strategic priorities, programme adaptation, and advocacy, particularly in fragile and emergency‑affected contexts.
  • Monitor changes in national and humanitarian contexts and guide timely strategic adjustments that maintain quality, relevance, and impact for children and adolescents.

Program Planning, Support and Quality

  • Provide technical leadership and advisory support to ensure the quality, integration, and effectiveness of health programming across development and humanitarian responses, with a focus on child health, MNRH, ASRH, MHPSS, and health systems strengthening.
  • Lead or support health and multi‑sectoral assessments, ensuring robust analysis of children’s and adolescents’ needs and effective use of findings in programme design and adaptation.
  • Guide the design and integration of evidence‑based interventions, including high‑impact, low‑cost child and maternal health interventions and safe, quality MHPSS approaches.
  • Provide technical review and quality assurance of programme designs, proposals, monitoring reports, evaluations, and learning products prior to submission.
  • Ensure integration across the continuum of care and across sectors.
  • Ensure health programmes adhere to international, national, and organisational standards, including Sphere and safeguarding requirements.
  • Lead learning, innovation, and lesson‑learning processes, working with MEAL teams to ensure evidence is systematically captured, disseminated, and applied to improve programme quality and outcomes.

Providing Strategic and Technical Guidance and Oversight

  • Provide technical oversight to PMs and field teams to ensure timely, high quality program implementation, including monitoring against log frames, analysing performance, and advising corrective actions.
  • Coordinate closely with HR and procurement to ensure adequate staffing and timely availability of the health supplies to support effective program delivery.
  • In collaboration with the MEAL team, put in place a health sector MEAL plan, ensuring this links to reporting requirements, and capacity building of technical field staff in conducting the work.
  • Working closely with the accountability lead to put in place sector accountability mechanisms, ensuring that the feedback is incorporated into programme design and learning disseminated to the wider health sector.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor programme quality and compliance with sphere and other minimum standards, provide technical support, strengthen staff, and partner capacity through mentoring and training, while identifying emerging needs to inform program needs and adaptation.

Monitoring, Assessment, Program Design and Fundraising

  • Lead on health or multi-sectoral technical assessments, ensuring assessment findings are documented and that all assessments include a specific analysis of children’s needs.
  • Provide technical quality assurance of health strategies, assessments, and programs as necessary, and proactively promote high quality health technical approaches within country programs.
  • Play a leadership role in shaping health communications, advocacy, and external representation in line with thematic priorities.
  • Lead on program design and proposal development and fundraising, including writing high quality concept notes and position paper, engagement with donors and technical advisors.
  • Drive the health innovation, learning and evidence agenda including documentation and application of lesson learned with MEAL support.

Human Resources and Performance Management

  • Identify health sector staffing needs in collaboration with Human Resources and contribute to workforce planning that supports programme quality and sustainability.
  • Coach, mentor, and provide technical supervision to Project Managers, technical staff, and partners, strengthening their capacity to deliver integrated, high‑quality health programming.
  • Lead learning needs assessments and develop capacity strengthening plans for Save the Children and partner staff, including training on child health, MNRH, ASRH, MHPSS, and systems‑oriented approaches.
  • Oversee the development and delivery of technical guidance and training materials that improve programme quality and technical consistency.
  • Coach and mentor PMs and field staff and link into wider organizational talent development mechanisms.
  • Oversee development and delivery of technical training material that will improve aspects of health work within Save the Children.
  • Develop learning needs assessment and capacity building plans for both SC and partner staff, linking capacity building initiatives to wider opportunities identified via coordination and networks.

Networking, Coordination and External Communication

  • Represent Save the Children in inter‑agency coordination mechanisms, technical working groups, and sector forums, contributing to harmonisation of approaches and standards.
  • Provide technical leadership within coordination platforms to promote integrated health programming, including child health, MNRH, ASRH, MHPSS, and systems strengthening.
  • Ensure Save the Children’s programme results, learning, and evidence are effectively shared to inform sector practice and collective decision‑making.
  • Support the development of external communications and media products related to health programming, acting as a technical spokesperson when appropriate.
  • Actively participate in inter-agency meeting and forums, harmonize approaches or tools, ensure that SC’s program achievements and learnings are represented, and seek assistance in case of challenges.
  • Help shape broader sector strategies through influence of and leadership within inter-agency coordination forums, ensuring the specific needs of children are being addressed. This may involve taking on a co-chairing role where needs demand.
  • Take the initiative in documenting lessons learnt, best practice and case studies to shape in-country strategies and programme approaches and contribute to broader sector learning.
  • Pro-actively identify advocacy opportunities, case studies and research opportunities which link with wider organisational strategic objectives and turn these into action.

Advocacy and Fundraising

  • Identify health sector priorities and funding gaps and support fundraising and proposal development, collaborating closely with members and donors.
  • Ensure advocacy initiatives are informed by programme evidence, learning, and assessments, with a focus on improving equitable access, quality of care, and health system resilience.
  • Proactively identify advocacy opportunities, case studies, and research themes aligned with organisational objectives, including child health, adolescent health, and rights, MHPSS, and systems strengthening.

General Roles

  • Contribute to country office risk management, including identification, mitigation, and communication of programme and safeguarding risks.
  • Ensure safeguarding, accountability, inclusion, and meaningful participation principles are embedded across all health programming, including MHPSS and adolescent‑focused interventions.
  • Collaborate with programme operations teams to ensure programmes are safe, inclusive, and compliant with safeguarding, health and safety, equal opportunities, and anti‑harassment policies.
  • Comply with all Save the Children policies, values, and standards, and contribute to a culture of learning, accountability, and technical excellence.
  • Contribute to the CO risk management process and matrix development, communicate mitigation measures with the team, and ensure that they are in place.
  • Contribute to the development of communications products, in collaboration with the Country Office Communications Manager
  • Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to safeguarding, code of conduct, safety and security, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.

Safeguarding Policy:

  • Support in the mainstreaming of Save the Children’s safeguarding policy within livelihoods and social protection programs design and implementation; including identifying and addressing risks to children that are caused/exacerbated by programme design and intervention.
  • Collaborate with the Program Operations teams to ensure that activities are safe for children and adults, and that all steps are taken to ensure their meaningful and safe participation.

BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice) Accountability:

  • holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values.
  • holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved. Ambition:
  • sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same.
  • widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others.
  • future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

Collaboration:

  • builds and maintains effective relationships with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters.
  • values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength.
  • approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

Creativity:

  • develops and encourages new and innovative solutions.
  • willing to take disciplined risks.

Integrity:

· • honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor of Medicine Bachelor of (MBBCH) specialized in medicine, public health or a related subject.
  • MA in Public Health is a strong asset.

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

  • Minimum 10 years’ experience of working in health programmes in a development and /or Humanitarian context.
  • At least 3-5 years providing technical support to reproductive, maternal, newborn, child health, and nutrition programs.
  • Previous experience of managing a large health team in both development and humanitarian contexts.
  • Proven capacity for mentoring, coaching, and training on health-related topics.
  • Experience in senior level representation
  • Ability to write clear and well-argued assessment and project reports.
  • Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
  • Proven ability to influence change at an operational and strategic level.
  • Proficient level of written and spoken English.

Additional job responsibilities

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.

Equal Opportunities

The role holder is required to perform the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

Child Safeguarding:

We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.

Safeguarding our Staff:

The post holder is required to perform the duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy

Health and Safety

The role holder is required to perform the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

About the job:

We are seeking a highly skilled DevOps Specialist to architect, implement, and maintain end‑to‑end CI/CD pipelines using GitHub, with a strong focus on test‑driven deployment, automated release management, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) practices. The role also includes automating build, tagging, and publication processes across web, desktop, and mobile platforms to ensure consistent and traceable releases. Deep expertise in Linux system administration, networking, and IaC tools is essential to deliver scalable, secure, and highly available deployments.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, architecture, and management of CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions (and similar tools), ensuring fast, reliable, and reproducible software delivery.
  • Implement and enforce test‑driven deployment systems, integrating automated testing, validation, and monitoring to maintain code quality and accelerate feedback cycles.
  • Containerize applications and microservices with Docker, optimize image builds, and manage deployment pipelines for distributed environments.
  • Develop and maintain cross‑platform build pipelines using CMake or equivalent tools, ensuring consistent compilation and release workflows across web, desktop, and mobile.
  • Automate end‑to‑end release processes, including tagging, building, signing, and distributing mobile, web, and desktop applications.
  • Define and manage Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to provision and maintain reliable, scalable, and secure infrastructure environments.
  • Collaborate closely with development, QA, and operations teams to troubleshoot deployment issues, optimize performance, and improve release reliability.
  • Continuously improve observability and feedback loops, leveraging monitoring and alerting systems to maintain operational excellence.

Mandatory

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 3+ years of hands‑on experience architecting and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions or equivalent tools at scale in a production environment.
  • Strong proficiency in test‑driven deployment methodologies, including writing and maintaining automated test suites for integration and end‑to‑end validation.
  • Expertise in containerization technologies such as Docker, including image creation, registry management, and basic orchestration patterns.
  • In‑depth knowledge of C++ build systems, specifically CMake, with proven experience optimizing native build and deployment pipelines.
  • Advanced Linux system administration and networking skills, including shell scripting, package management, performance troubleshooting, firewalls, and VPN configuration.
  • Excellent communication, problem‑solving, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in globally distributed teams.
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform, Ansible, AWS CDK or AWS CloudFormation.
  • Experience with mobile CI/CD automation, including build, tagging, and publication for iOS and Android applications.
  • Advanced knowledge of release management practices, including automated versioning, signing, and artifact distribution.

Preferred

  • Exposure to observability and monitoring systems, leveraging tools like Prometheus, Grafana, or ELK for deployment health tracking.
  • Experience working in high‑availability, security‑sensitive environments, especially in fintech, blockchain, or distributed systems contexts.
  • Experience deploying and managing blockchain‑based applications.
  • Exposure to AI/ML pipelines, including automated model training, evaluation, and deployment using frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow.

title: 01899 - Supervisor Maintenance

Apply specialized knowledge of equipment operation and maintenance techniques. Perform maintenance repair, replacement and preventive maintenance. Complete pre-trips inspections for vehicles and equipment operated.

  • Knowledge of safety policies, procedures, and programs related to roadway construction and maintenance.

  • Skill in the operation and maintenance of hand held and power tools.

Minimum Qualifications:

We are looking for a DevOps Engineer to build and run cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and observability for Data and AI teams in a PCI‑compliant environment.

  • Solid understanding of cloud security and compliance practices, particularly in PCI‑compliant or regulated environments .

title: Lähihoitaja  Psykiatriakeskukseen Geropsykiatrian osastolle P1
description:
Keskitettyjen palveluiden linjalla Psykiatriakeskuksessa osastolla P1 on haettavissa kaksi lähihoitajan toimea. P1 on iäkkäiden potilaiden psykiatristen sairauksien hoito-osasto. Erikoisalaamme ovat muistisairauksien tutkimus ja -hoito sekä vaativien käytösoireiden hoitohaasteet. Osastoille potilaat tulevat lääkärin lähetteellä ja osa potilasta saa avun etäosaston kautta. Potilaat ovat iältään yleensä vähintään 65-vuotiaita. Psykiatriakeskuksessa tehdään yhteistyötä muiden osastojen kanssa.

Geropsykiatrian erikoisalalla pääset hyödyntämään sekä psykiatrista että somaattista hoitotyön osaamista. Perusajatuksemme on potilaslähtöinen hoitotyö. Osastolla toteutetaan yksilövastuista hoitotyötä osana moniammatillista tiimiä ja osallistut aktiivisesti potilashoidon kehittämiseen hoitotyön asiantuntijaryhmissä. Henkilökohtaiset vahvuudet ja kiinnostus huomioiden sinulla voi olla lisäksi muita osastokohtaisia vastuutehtäviä. Hoitajilta toivomme kokemusta psykiatrisesta- ja muistisairaiden hoitotyöstä sekä halua kohdata ikääntyvä potilas ja hänen läheisensä yhdenvertaisesti, sekä kehitysmyönteistä asennetta työhön.

Laaja koulutustarjontamme antaa hyvät mahdollisuudet osaamisen ylläpitämiseen ja täydentämiseen. Työssä viihtymistä tukee avoin työyhteisö. Tarvittaessa työaikajoustoin mahdollistamme työ- ja yksityiselämän yhteensovittamisen. HUSin monipuoliset henkilöstöetuudet, kuten suosittu liikunta- ja kulttuurietu, ovat myös käytettävissäsi. Toimessa on mahdollisuus myös työnkiertoon.

Palkkaus on SOTE-sopimuksen mukainen.

Hae meille hakuajan loppuun mennessä. HUSissa olet osa vaikuttavinta hoitoa.

Mikäli kiinnostuit, tartu rohkeasti tilaisuuteen ja jätä työhakemuksesi hakuajan loppuun mennessä! Vastaamme mielellämme mahdollisiin lisäkysymyksiin.

Tehtävän kelpoisuusehdot

Lähihoitajan tutkinto

Edellytämme asiakas- ja potilastiloissa työskentelevältä tartuntatautilain pykälien 48 ja 48 a mukaista rokotussuojaa, ja terveydenhuollon toimintayksiköissä työskentelevältä terveydentilan selvitystä keuhkotuberkuloosista.

Tehtävään valitun tulee esittää sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon valvonnasta annetuin lain 28 §:ssä edellytetty rikosrekisteriote.

Yhteystiedot

Osastonhoitaja Leena Oila (P1), leena.oila@hus.fi, p. 050 428 7942

Yh Katja Tenhovirta, p. 040 833 2429

Tietoja meistä

HUS Helsingin yliopistollinen sairaala on Suomen suurin erikoissairaanhoidon toimija. Osaamisemme on kansainvälisesti tunnettua ja tunnustettua. Yliopistollisena sairaalana tutkimme ja kehitämme jatkuvasti hoitomenetelmiämme sekä toimintaamme. HUSissa saa vuosittain hoitoa lähes 700 000 potilasta. Meillä työskentelee yli 27 000 ammattilaista potilaiden parhaaksi. Vastaamme erikoissairaanhoidon järjestämisestä Uudellamaalla. Lisäksi meille on keskitetty koko Suomen ja Etelä-Suomen yhteistyöalueen monien harvinaisten ja vaikeiden sairauksien hoito.

HUS – Vaikuttavinta hoitoa

Yhdenvertaisuus on yksi arvoistamme. Edistämme aktiivisesti monimuotoisuutta työyhteisössämme. Haluamme, että meillä HUSissa työskentelee eri-ikäisiä, eri sukupuoliin sekä eri kieli-, kulttuuri- ja vähemmistöryhmiin kuuluvia ammattilaisia. Meille olet tervetullut omana ainutlaatuisena itsenäsi.

  • Engineering Rigor:Proven track record of owning production systems end-to-end, including monitoring, automated testing, CI/CD, and debugging complex distributed bottlenecks.

title: Specialist, Diabetes Care and Education
description:
Diabetes Care and Education Specialist

Lakeview Hospital is looking to hire a Diabetes Care and Education Specialist to join our team! Come join us as a Partner for Good and help us make an impact on the care and experience that our patients and their families receive every day.

Position Summary:

All team members support the mission, vision, and values of HealthPartners and follow all organizational policies and procedures.

The Diabetes Care and Education Specialist (DCES) is a Registered Nurse or Registered Dietitian with advanced knowledge in diabetes care, including nutrition interventions. The DCES provides direct care, education, and support across the lifespan, helping individuals with diabetes reach personalized goals related to nutrition, behavior, and treatment.

Using evidence-based strategies and collaborative care planning, the DCES promotes self-management, reduces risks, and improves health outcomes. As a key member of the care team, the DCES demonstrates professionalism, flexibility, and strong interpersonal skills, while maintaining patient confidentiality and rights. The DCES works closely with managing clinicians to deliver integrated, person-centered care and serves as a resource for the broader care team.

The DCES follows a structured approach to care—assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating—in alignment with the RN scope of practice or the Scope and Standards of Practice for Credentialed Dietetic Professionals, as well as HealthPartners protocols. Diabetes education programs in ambulatory settings must also meet standards set by our accrediting organization.

Work Schedule:

Mon 8:30am - 5:00pm
Tues 8:30am - 5:00pm
Friday 8:30am - 5:00pm

Required Qualifications:

  • Education, Experience or Equivalent Combination:

    • Bachelor's degree in Nursing, Nutrition, and/or Dietetics with 2 years of experience providing care, education, or support to patients with diabetes,

      or

    • Associate's degree in Nursing with 4 years of experience providing care, education, or support to patients with diabetes.
    • Demonstrated leaderships skills

  • Licensure/ Registration/ Certification:
    • Current Registered Nurse license in either the state of Minnesota or Wisconsin upon hire. Must provide proof of application for alternate state license prior to start and obtain the second license within 30 days of hire. Both Minnesota and Wisconsin RN license must be maintained.

OR

  • Dietetic registration (RDN) through Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR).
    • Current Dietetic License for either the state of Minnesota or Wisconsin upon hire. Must provide proof of license application in alternate state prior to start and obtain the second license within 90 days of hire. Both Minnesota and Wisconsin license must be maintained.

  • Current national certification as a Certified Diabetes Care & Education Specialist (CDCES) or ability to become certified within 24 months of hire.
    • Current BLS certification for health professionals through the American Heart Association or Red Cross required and maintained. On-line BLS certification is not acceptable.

  • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

    • Effective Communication: Strong verbal and written skills; able to uphold clinical standards and professional ethics per the Nurse Practice Act or Scope and Standards for Credentialed Dietetic Professionals.

    • Clinical Judgment: Demonstrates critical thinking, sound decision-making, and the ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team environment.

    • Patient-Centered Service: Provides compassionate, professional care with tact and diplomacy in interactions with patients, families, and clinic staff.

    • Education & Engagement: Assesses patient education needs and communicates relevant information clearly to patients, families, and care teams.

    • Organization & Resilience: Skilled in planning, prioritizing, and completing tasks efficiently while remaining calm and focused under pressure.

    • Technology Proficiency: Proficient in electronic medical records and Microsoft Office (Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel); strong keyboarding skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Education, Experience or Equivalent Combination:
    • 4 years of prior experience in diabetes care and education is preferred.
  • Licensure/ Registration/ Certification:
    • Professional association membership in American Diabetes Association (ADA) and/or Association of Diabetes Care and Education Specialists (ADCES).
  • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
    • Familiar with Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES), The ADCES7 Self Care Behaviors, and the ADA Standards of Care.

title: Battery Algorithm and Model Calibration Engineer
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather together, committing to the values that lead to great work. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other's ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It's the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you'll do more than join something — you'll add something.

Are you interested in working at the forefront of Battery Systems? In this role, you will own the development of algorithm and model calibration methodologies supporting battery New Product Introduction (NPI) and advanced technology projects. You will utilize your expertise in both electrochemical characterization and electrical bench testing to calibrate battery algorithms and models for next-generation consumer electronic products. You will be part of a multi-functional team developing a new class of battery systems — spanning algorithms, architectures, and products — as we improve the utility and performance of batteries across the Apple product line.

We are looking for an individual with a deep understanding of battery behavior and characterization techniques from both design and application perspectives. In this position, you will combine electrochemical and electrical engineering expertise for the following responsibilities below.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field, with relevant industry experience.
  • Experience with battery cycling equipment such as Maccor, Arbin, or Bio-Logic.

Preferred Qualifications

  • MS or higher in a technical discipline with at least 3 years of relevant industry experience.
  • Strong background in electrochemistry with understanding of Li-battery performance characterization and analysis, including fast-charge protocol development, longevity/degradation mechanism identification and prediction, and impedance modeling.
  • Knowledge of battery characteristics and diagnostic techniques including OCV, hysteresis, thermodynamic and kinetic diagnosis, EIS, and P2D model development.
  • Experience with cell R&D techniques such as 3-electrode and symmetric cell methods.
  • Experience with Matlab or Python for large-scale data mining and processing.
  • Familiarity with AI tools to develop processes for efficiency improvement, such as automated test scripting, automated review, and data processing.
  • Experience with and understanding of battery algorithm design, battery gauging, and system power management.

title: Senior Camera Imaging Software Engineer - Camera & Photos
description:
iPhone is the most popular camera in the world, with billions of photos taken every year. The seamless integration of software and hardware has led to camera features like the Photonic Engine, Portrait mode, and Super-high-resolution photos which deliver magical experiences that surprise and delight our customers.

The Camera Technologies & Systems team in the Camera & Photos org delivers amazing quality photos and videos by combining state of the art computer vision, image processing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. As an engineer on our team you'll develop and extend those software pipelines, working side-by-side with the world-class engineers who made iPhone’s camera what it is today, and build new great camera capabilities spanning the universe of Apple devices. Whenever you see a “Shot on iPhone” billboard, you see our work; it could be your work too.

Be the First to Touch the Pixels Every great photo starts with a signal straight off the sensor, and sensors are never perfect. Our team gets the first look at that signal. We find hardware flaws and fix them right away, so that everything downstream starts from the best possible image. Our work sets the quality bar for the camera experience that millions of people use every day.

The Role: You will invent the algorithms and calibration schemes that turn imperfect silicon into stunning images. You will write high-performance code for the GPU and the Apple Neural Engine (ANE). You will also work side by side with Camera Hardware engineers to track down root causes and build solutions that ship at manufacturing scale. Your work will have a direct, visible effect on the final product.

What You Bring: Our team works with a large cross-functional group, so engineer soft skills are to the fore. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and a talent for working across disciplines. Strong time management, and the ability to keep several high-impact efforts moving at once. Deep experience with GPU programming and optimization, including designing algorithms for parallel architectures. Hands-on experience developing or working with calibration schemes. Familiarity with machine learning acceleration on the ANE or comparable hardware.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Thrive in a collaborative team, building software together
  • Excellent verbal and written communication
  • Strong programming skills, especially in Objective-C or C++
  • Experience with Unix/Linux, preferably macOS or iOS
  • Proficient with debugging techniques, preferably on embedded mobile platforms
  • Familiar with image processing concepts and algorithms
  • Skilled with performance and memory optimization
  • Masters or PhD in relitive field

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with GPU programming in Metal, OpenGL(ES), OpenCL, or CUDA

Day to day, the intern will participate in Global Travel Sourcing team meetings, support recurring and ad hoc analyses, maintain organized research and project documentation, and collaborate with stakeholders to understand requirements and validate findings. description:
About the Role

As a Staff Software Engineer on Uber’s Code Hosting & Merge team, you will set technical direction across the systems that host, find, and safely merge code for thousands of engineers. You’ll help define how this infrastructure evolves as AI agents become a core part of software development, and turn that vision into reliable platforms that keep engineering at Uber moving.

About the Team

Uber’s Code Hosting & Merge team, part of Developer Platform, builds and operates the infrastructure behind code hosting, code search, and SubmitQueue. Our goal: help engineers and AI agents ship code at scale with more speed, confidence, and less waiting. You’ll help build the infrastructure that keeps pace with that growth as AI agents expand what engineers can deliver.

What we own today:

  • Code hosting: the source control infrastructure that supports repository access and Git workflows across Uber’s engineering ecosystem.
  • Code search: the systems that help engineers and agents find and understand code across large codebases.
  • SubmitQueue and merge integrations: the system that merges thousands of changes daily into Uber’s Go monorepo while keeping the main branch green, together with automated checks and code review integrations.

We work closely with Developer Platform partners in CI, build systems, code review, and AI developer tooling, as well as engineering teams across Uber. Our infrastructure is a foundation for both everyday development and the next generation of autonomous coding workflows.

Explore some of our work

We’ve built systems that tackle some of the hardest problems in developer infrastructure. Here are a few examples:

  • GitFarm: Git as a Service — running Git operations in secure, pre-warmed environments so services can work with large monorepos without maintaining their own clones.
  • Open-source SubmitQueue — using speculative validation to safely merge concurrent changes at scale.
  • Slashing CI Costs at Uber — improving SubmitQueue’s scheduling to reduce CI resource usage by 53% and waiting times by 37% in the reported rollout.
  • AI Writes Code Faster Than Uber Can Merge It — our engineers explain how we’re evolving merge and validation systems for the demands of AI-driven development.

What the Candidate Will Do

  • Set technical direction for code hosting and merge infrastructure: define the long-term architecture and roadmap for systems serving both engineers and AI agents, and align Developer Platform and engineering leadership behind it.
  • Build for the scale of agentic development: evolve source control and merge systems to handle greater concurrency, sustained automation, and growing change volume. Improve throughput and land times while preserving merge correctness and main-branch health.
  • Shape how agents interact with developer infrastructure: partner with AI tooling, CI, and code review teams to build dependable integrations, clear status and failure signals, and workflows that can recover safely from retries and partial failures.
  • Lead the hardest problems hands-on: design and ship critical Go-based distributed services, guide complex migrations, and set the bar for testing, observability, reliability, and cost. Own outcomes from design through rollout and operations, including incident response and preventive improvements.
  • Grow technical leaders: mentor senior engineers and tech leads, lead design reviews, and help teams make sound architectural tradeoffs. Use developer feedback and measures such as availability, land time, and merge throughput to focus investment where it matters most.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including building and operating large-scale backend services or developer platforms in production.
  • Proficiency in at least one major programming language, such as Go, Java, or Python, and strong computer science and distributed systems fundamentals.
  • Experience setting technical direction for multi-team or organization-wide projects through all stages: inception, stakeholder alignment, implementation, and operations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • AI fluency in day-to-day engineering: experience using coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode to drive large, complex projects end to end, from codebase exploration and planning through implementation, testing, review, and rollout. Ability to decompose work, orchestrate parallel agent workflows, and verify results while retaining ownership of architecture and production quality.
  • Experience extending agent workflows through harnesses, skills, or MCP integrations, and making them effective in large codebases and production engineering environments.
  • Deep experience with Go, Git internals, code hosting, code search, merge queues, or large-scale monorepo infrastructure, including integrations with build systems such as Bazel or Buck and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience defining multi-year technical strategy for developer infrastructure and earning buy-in across teams and leadership, including evolving critical systems without disrupting developers.
  • A data-driven approach to engineering: experience using production metrics, experiments, and developer feedback to identify bottlenecks, prioritize investments, and measure improvements in reliability, performance, cost, and developer productivity.
  • Recognized technical leadership beyond your team: mentoring senior engineers, improving reliability and operational practices, and sharing expertise through technical talks, open source, or the broader engineering community.

title: Exercise Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The Exercise Specialist supports safe, individualized exercise conditioning and patient education in outpatient cardiac rehabilitation. The position reports to the Cardiopulmonary Director and works under the clinical direction of the Cardiac Rehabilitation RN and applicable Medical Director-approved protocols. The role may support pulmonary rehabilitation after program implementation and completion of applicable competencies.

Primary Responsibilities

• Exercise prescription: Assist with developing and implementing the exercise component of the individualized treatment plan (ITP), using approved patient-specific parameters. Progress or regress exercise within established protocols and communicate changes to the RN.

• Exercise supervision: Guide patients through warm-up, aerobic conditioning, resistance training and cool-down; demonstrate proper technique and safe use of treadmills, NuStep, SciFit and other equipment.

• Patient monitoring: Obtain and record HR, BP, SpO2, RPE, symptoms and exercise workload as assigned. Observe tolerance and promptly report abnormal findings to the RN.

• Safety: Follow exercise initiation, modification and termination criteria. Stop exercise when safety concerns arise and immediately notify the RN; do not independently clear patients to resume exercise after a concerning event.

• Education: Provide exercise-related education, including safe activity, perceived exertion, home exercise and cardiac risk reduction; conduct assigned monthly education sessions.

• Maintenance program: Support Phase IV/maintenance exercise activities according to department policy.

Clinical Duties in a Critical Access Hospital Setting

• Document exercise progression/regression, workload, patient response, abnormal findings and education in approved LSI/Epic workflows. The RN completes the daily clinical note.

• Maintain a safe exercise environment; disinfect equipment after each patient and at the end of shift per department policy. Report equipment defects and remove unsafe equipment from use.

• Respond to emergencies within training and hospital policy, including BLS, AED use and activation of emergency response.

• Communicate patient progress, safety concerns and operational needs to the RN and Cardiopulmonary Director.

Scope of Practice and Clinical Oversight

• The RN is the clinical lead and is responsible for clinical intake assessment, readiness for exercise, telemetry interpretation, clinical decisions, provider communication and daily clinical documentation. The Exercise Specialist may assist with obtaining data and preparing exercise-related information.

• The Exercise Specialist may view HR and workload data in LSI and assist with transmitter placement and technical troubleshooting after competency validation. Rhythm interpretation, advanced telemetry analysis and clinical response decisions remain with the RN or other authorized clinician.

• Exercise prescription changes must remain within the approved ITP, physician orders and department protocols. Refer changes outside those limits to the RN for clinical review.

• This position does not provide physical therapy services, establish a physical therapy plan of care, independently diagnose or treat medical conditions, or initiate/change medication or oxygen orders.

• Pulmonary rehabilitation duties, when implemented, may include exercise supervision, monitoring dyspnea and SpO2, patient education and assistance with functional exercise testing such as the six-minute walk test, after training and competency validation and under applicable clinical protocols.

The Lift Truck Operator I follows established warehouse, food-safety, equipment-operation, and safety procedures while supporting daily warehouse and shipping activities.

  • Safely unload incoming materials and products and transport them to designated storage or staging locations.

title: Material Modeling and Simulation Engineer
description:
Imagine being part of the team that ensures every Apple product performs exactly as designed — before a single prototype is built. Apple’s Hardware Engineering organization is home to some of the most advanced simulation and signal integrity work in the industry, developing the foundational methodologies that connect virtual models to physical reality. Our work spans every product line — from iPhone to Mac to Vision Pro — empowering engineers across Apple to make confident design decisions faster and with greater precision, all in service of creating products that enrich people’s lives.

You’ll join the Material Modeling Team, a group whose mission is to elevate simulation confidence to the point where it reliably supports critical design decisions. We deliver on this through two foundational pillars: methodology development in close partnership with product teams, and material model generation and validation across the environmental conditions that matter to real products. As a Material Modeling and Simulation Engineer, you’ll develop and validate machine learning and simulation methodologies that drive strong correlation between modeled results and physical measurements — partnering with hardware engineering teams across multiple product divisions to accelerate development and reduce reliance on physical builds.

You’ll focus on applying machine learning and data-driven methods to improve PCB material modeling quality, accelerate simulation cycles, and enhance simulation-to-measurement correlation to inform design decisions for new technologies and designs. You thrive on bridging the gap between modeled and measured results, enjoy cross-functional collaboration with hardware engineering teams, and are motivated to drive adoption of proven methodologies across a diverse set of products.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or a relevant field of study.
  • 1+ years of related work and relevant academic experience.
  • Expertise in AI/ML methodologies — such as DNN, PINN, surrogate modeling, or gradient boosting.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and standard ML frameworks.
  • Exposure to PCB or Package Design — Best Signal/Power Integrity Design Practices
  • Experience with Workflow Development and Optimization

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a relevant field.
  • Good foundational understanding of Electromagnetics and high-speed simulation principles.
  • Hands-on experience with EM simulation vendor tools — such as HFSS, CST, ADS, or Clarity.
  • A deep understanding of PCB material characterization methods and material property modeling across environmental conditions is part of your expertise.
  • Experience with VNA-based S-parameter measurement, TRL/TDR calibration, and de-embedding workflows.
  • Strong understanding of simulation-to-measurement correlation workflows, including de-embedding techniques.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and organizational skills to collaborate effectively across teams.

title: Sr. Swift Standard Libraries Engineer
description:
Are you eager to learn, grow, and make an impact? Join the Swift Standard Libraries team and enjoy the rare opportunity to work at the intersection of:

  • Programming language and library design
  • Apple’s frameworks and the open-source community
  • Applications, servers, scripting, AI, and more The future is being defined right now, and the Swift Standard Libraries team is at the center of it. The work we do will shape the developer experience on Apple's platforms and beyond for decades to come.

The Swift Standard Libraries team is responsible for much of the user-facing experience of the Swift programming language via the Standard Library and Foundation, which reaches from basic types and data structures like Date and String to complex algorithms like sorting and calendrical calculation. The team also develops a growing roster of open-source Swift packages including Algorithms, Argument Parser, Async Algorithms, Atomics, Numerics, Collections, System and Subprocess. You will join a small team of thoughtful, versatile engineers in meeting the challenge of designing correct and expressive high-level APIs with carefully tuned low-level implementations. You'll work mostly in the open as an active contributor to the swift.org open-source project, collaborating with the Swift compiler team, engineers from across every part of Apple, and the Swift open-source community.

Our team strives to build a diverse, inclusive team and healthy, balanced work environment. We believe that every engineer brings unique skills and perspective. Far more than any specific experience or skill, we are looking for engineers who want to enable others to build great software, while learning and developing their skills.

  • Interest in programming language and library design, and engage with the open-source community
  • The ability to simplify complex ideas and explain them clearly

Preferred Qualifications

title: AI Applied Scientist, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function, it is a foundational science. Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building that scientific foundation: rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology for LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship.

What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will work alongside measurement scientists (psychometrics, validity theory), ML researchers, and platform engineers, bringing together ML research, statistical rigor, and production engineering.

We are looking for an Applied Scientist who works across the full arc of evaluation science: turning research into tools engineers can use on their own, and turning what those engineers run into new research. You care whether a method holds up on real data, at real scale, for a real decision, and you are curious enough to go after the open question underneath when it doesn't.

Our team is building self-service evaluation: tools, SDKs, and AI-powered capabilities that let engineers across Apple evaluate their AI features on their own, quickly and correctly, so they can build and ship those features faster. You will develop the methods that make this possible: raising the quality of the evaluations engineers run, and helping them understand what their results mean and what to do next. Often the method a problem needs doesn't exist yet. When that happens, you will figure it out, whether that means extending a recent paper or developing something new, and share what you learn through publications and internal research reports. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.

With research and measurement scientists, you will co-develop new methods, make sure the tools give engineers valid, trustworthy signals, and bring back the hard problems that should shape the team's research agenda. With platform and research engineers, you will define what each method needs to work reliably without an expert in the loop, including its assumptions, failure modes, and validation tests, so it can ship in the evaluation SDKs and APIs used across Apple.

The successful candidate combines scientific depth with practical judgment: you know which methods fit a problem and why, can design experiments that show whether they actually work, can diagnose why they break down on messy real-world data, and can explain clearly what an evaluation result does and does not support.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 3+ years of applied research experience.
  • Deep expertise in evaluating AI systems, gained through research on evaluation methods, substantial hands-on experience evaluating LLMs or agentic systems in real products, or both.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and the modern ML ecosystem, with demonstrated ability to implement complex methods from recent papers and run large-scale experiments.
  • Hands-on experience with large language models, whether fine-tuning, inference, prompting pipelines, or building LLM-powered applications.
  • Demonstrated research ability through publications at peer-reviewed venues, preprints, or equivalent research output.
  • Track record of applying research to practical problems: methods, prototypes, or tools adopted by other teams or used to inform real product decisions.
  • Solid software engineering fundamentals for research code: version control, testing, reproducibility, and code others can build on.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex results, and their limitations, to diverse audiences.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and new problem spaces; you thrive when building something that doesn't yet have a playbook.

Preferred Qualifications

  • First-author publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP), especially on evaluation methodology: papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation to demonstrate model improvements.
  • Specific experience in one or more of: LLM-as-judge approaches (calibration, rubric design, bias mitigation); benchmark design and validation (IRT, contamination detection); human evaluation methodology (protocol design, quality control); experimentation and comparisons between system versions (A/B testing, uncertainty quantification); or agentic and multi-agent system evaluation, including failure diagnosis and automated red-teaming.
  • Familiarity with theoretical foundations of evaluation: measurement theory and validity frameworks, statistical learning theory (calibration, reliability, decision theory), causal inference, or preference aggregation.
  • Experience with the practical challenges of evaluating generative AI and agentic systems: non-deterministic outputs, token economics, multi-turn agent trajectories, and tool use.
  • Experience building methods or tools used directly by non-experts, such as developer-facing ML tooling or self-service analytics.
  • Familiarity with modern evaluation tools and frameworks (e.g., DeepEval, Ragas, TruLens, LangSmith, or agent tracing and observability tools).
  • Experience working with distributed computing or cloud-native tooling (e.g., Ray, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes) to run evaluations at scale.
  • Experience with cross-disciplinary work, such as collaboration with social scientists, psychometricians, or domain experts.
  • Experience in fast-moving, early-stage teams where you helped define technical direction from the ground up.
