  • Apply Design for Lean Six Sigma, Kaizen and project-management methods to eliminate bottlenecks, improve flow, prevent recurrence and sustain measurable results.

Customer, Supplier and Cross-Functional Communication

  • Lead technical interactions with internal and external customers, suppliers, quality authorities and other stakeholders, present project status, technical evidence, risks and recovery plans.
  • Defend technical positions using requirements, objective evidence, analysis and test results while working constructively toward agreement and customer acceptance.
  • Communicate noncompliance, audit findings, technical risks and decision needs promptly to management. Follow escalation paths to protect safety, quality, schedule and compliance.
  • Mentor early-career engineers and share systems-engineering, quality, supplier-development, program-execution and problem-solving practices across the organization.

Test Systems Definitions, Requirements and Estimates

  • Collaborate with Test Leads and Test Project Engineering to analyze baseline test system and subsystem requirements; ensuring requirements are clear, testable, traceable, feasible and aligned with customer and regulatory expectations.
  • Develop and maintain test system context, functional and logical architectures, interface definitions, operational concepts, assumptions and constraints for assigned products or programs.
  • Provide test system cost estimates, schedules, design assumptions and risk assessment.
  • Lead technical test system reviews, identify gaps, conflicts, ambiguity, derived requirements and verification implications before design commitment.

System Design, Integration and Technical Leadership

  • Lead test system and subsystem design activities, including technical trade studies, design decisions, interface management and integration planning across hardware, software, test, manufacturing and supplier boundaries.
  • Assess interactions among electronic assemblies, wiring/interconnect, mechanical elements, sensing, controls, test equipment, production processes and supporting data systems.
  • Present or contribute to formal technical reviews such as Preliminary Design

Verification, Validation and Qualification

  • Develop verification and validation strategies, plans, procedures, acceptance criteria, compliance matrices and reports using analysis, inspection, demonstration and test methods.
  • Lead test readiness, execution, anomaly resolution and results assessment; confirm that evidence objectively demonstrates compliance with allocated requirements.
  • Plan and support test system engineering qualifications, process validations and production-readiness activities.
  • Coordinate test system integration with customer platforms and external interfaces; communicate status, limitations, risks and acceptance evidence to internal and external stakeholders.

Reliability, Safety, Quality and Technical Risk

  • Integrate technical risk management into system decisions using tools such as FMEA, fault-oriented analysis, control plans, statistical process control, reliability assessment, root-cause analysis and corrective action.
  • Lead containment, investigation and permanent corrective action for complex product, process, supplier or integration issues using RCCA, 8D and data-driven problem solving.
  • Ensure all engineering activities are compliant to the Aerospace Engineering Process (AEP) including Configuration Management and Cyber Security.
  • Evaluate nonconformances, deviations and change impacts, support material review and change-control decisions with technically defensible risk assessments.
  • Proactively identify business-continuity, obsolescence, supply, migration and transition risks, and define measurable mitigation and validation plans.

Product, Supplier and Manufacturing Integration

  • Partner with Supplier Quality, Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Procurement and Program Management to translate test system needs into supplier, product and process requirements.
  • Assess supplier capability, qualification evidence, process controls, test coverage and production-ramp readiness for complex test systems and sub-systems.
  • Apply design-for-test and producibility principles to reduce escape risk, rework, troubleshooting cycle time, yield loss and delivery disruption.
  • Support new-product introduction, technology transfer, outsourcing/repatriation, and site transitions for test systems.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical, aerospace engineering or science.
  • Minimum five years of relevant engineering experience in systems/test engineering, equipment qualification, reliability, manufacturing integration or related technical quality engineering within a regulated or high-reliability environment
  • Advanced systems-engineering knowledge and demonstrated requirements validation, verification, system/subsystem logic, interface control, integration and traceable acceptance evidence.
  • Ability to execute engineering work packages, coordinate multidisciplinary contributors and manage technical risks and changes against customer specifications, schedules and applicable standards.

WE VALUE

  • Strong knowledge of testing standards such as MIL-STD and protocols.
  • High competency in data analysis and statistical methods to interpret testing results accurately.
  • PMP, PMI-RMP, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or related project, risk or supplier-quality training: applied FMEA, statistical process control, analytics and root-cause corrective action/8D.
  • Aerospace/defense, semiconductor assembly and test, or electronics experience
  • Test operations, burn-in reliability, equipment/process qualification, proficiency in subcontracted work and transfer readiness; cross-site qualification, configuration/change control and production acceptance.
  • Digital-record transformation, enterprise upgrades, UAT, data migration, reporting or legacy retirement; familiarity with SAP.
  • Electronic assemblies, wire harnesses, electromechanical equipment or metrology; familiarity with LabVIEW or LabWindows/CVI is an asset.
  • Multi-site operational transitions, business-continuity planning and change management, with effective mentoring and cross-functional influence.

Get to Know Darwoft

At Darwoft, we build custom software solutions and partner with international companies to create high-impact digital products.

We are a Latin American technology company with a people-first culture, strong professional standards, and a long-term partnership mindset. We work with distributed teams, complex technical challenges, and clients whose technology has a direct impact on their businesses and users.

About the Project

We are partnering with an innovative cybersecurity company building a next-generation Identity Security and Identity Observability platform .

The product helps enterprise security teams understand how human users, service accounts, workloads, applications, and AI-driven identities access systems across cloud, SaaS, network, endpoint, and on-premise environments .

At the core of the platform is a highly data-intensive architecture that collects and analyzes large volumes of events, logs, network telemetry, identity activity, and security signals . This information is processed to identify unusual access patterns, security risks, identity blind spots, infrastructure misconfigurations, and potential threats.

The platform integrates with complex enterprise ecosystems including identity providers, cloud platforms, SASE solutions, SIEMs, endpoint security tools, network infrastructure, and security services.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer focused on Data Ingestion, Integrations, and Collectors to become a key technical bridge between enterprise customers and the engineering organization.

This is not a traditional backend or internal data engineering position.

You'll work directly with customers to understand their infrastructure, data sources, security architecture, network topology, APIs, and workflows, then design and implement scalable mechanisms to ingest that information into the platform.

You'll combine data engineering, software engineering, solution architecture, cloud infrastructure, and technical consulting .

A major part of your mission will be building and evolving connectors and ingestion pipelines capable of integrating data from complex enterprise environments while maintaining reliability, scalability, security, and fast time-to-production.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design, develop, and maintain production-grade data collectors, connectors, and ingestion services .
  • Integrate enterprise data sources including identity providers, cloud platforms, SASE solutions, network infrastructure, endpoints, applications, security platforms, and SIEM systems .
  • Work directly with enterprise customers to understand their environments, data flows, APIs, security requirements, and integration constraints.
  • Participate in technical onboarding processes, from initial discovery and architecture design through production deployment.
  • Design scalable ingestion architectures for processing security events, logs, identity activity, network telemetry, and other high-volume data sources .
  • Build integrations using REST APIs, cloud-native services, event-driven architectures, and modern software engineering practices .
  • Develop backend services primarily using Python and/or Go .
  • Work with SQL and NoSQL databases to store, transform, query, and analyze high-volume data.
  • Build and operate containerized services using Docker and Kubernetes .
  • Deploy and integrate solutions across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments .
  • Troubleshoot complex customer deployment and integration issues across application, infrastructure, networking, API, and data layers.
  • Optimize ingestion performance, reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency.
  • Collaborate with Solution Architects, Sales Engineering, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering teams.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor around customer data architecture, collection strategies, security integrations, and implementation best practices.
  • Identify recurring customer requirements and transform them into reusable connectors, platform capabilities, or improvements to the core product.
  • Contribute technical insights from real-world implementations to the product roadmap.
  • Support production adoption and continuously improve time-to-value for enterprise customers.
  • Participate in occasional customer-facing technical sessions and, when necessary, onsite engagements.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of professional Software Engineering, Data Engineering, Platform Engineering, or related experience.
  • Strong software development experience with:
    • Python
    • Go
  • Strong experience designing and consuming REST APIs .
  • Hands-on experience building data ingestion pipelines, connector frameworks, integration platforms, or similar systems .
  • Experience integrating complex enterprise systems and third-party platforms.
  • Solid understanding of both SQL and NoSQL databases .
  • Production experience with at least one major cloud platform:
    • AWS
    • Azure
    • GCP
  • Experience working with Docker and Kubernetes .
  • Strong understanding of Git-based development workflows and CI/CD practices .
  • Experience designing reliable, scalable, and production-ready distributed systems.
  • Strong debugging skills across APIs, infrastructure, networking, application services, and data pipelines.
  • Experience working directly with customers, stakeholders, or technical partners.
  • Ability to translate complex customer requirements into pragmatic technical solutions.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to operate effectively in customer-facing technical conversations.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership when solving ambiguous technical problems.

Highly Relevant Experience

Experience with any of the following will be especially valuable:

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM )
  • Identity Providers (IdPs )
  • Identity Security
  • Cybersecurity platforms
  • SIEM systems
  • Security telemetry
  • Network security
  • Endpoint security
  • SASE / Zero Trust environments
  • Cloud security
  • Large-scale event processing
  • Streaming architectures

Integration Experience

Previous experience integrating APIs or data from platforms such as the following is highly valuable:

  • AWS
  • Microsoft Azure
  • Google Cloud
  • Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory
  • Okta
  • Google Workspace
  • Duo
  • CrowdStrike
  • Zscaler
  • Palo Alto
  • Microsoft Defender
  • SIEM and security analytics platforms

Direct experience with every platform is not required. What matters is a strong track record of learning complex APIs and transforming heterogeneous enterprise data sources into reliable integrations.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with large-scale data processing or streaming platforms.
  • Experience designing reusable connector SDKs or integration frameworks .
  • Understanding of identity-related security concepts such as authentication, authorization, credentials, service accounts, privileged access, and non-human identities.
  • Experience with security events, audit logs, network telemetry, or cloud activity data.
  • Familiarity with event-driven and distributed system architectures.
  • Experience deploying AI/ML-enabled applications.
  • Exposure to LLMs, AI agents, or AI-powered security applications .
  • Solution Architecture or Forward Deployed Engineering experience.
  • Previous experience in cybersecurity startups or high-growth SaaS environments.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role will be measured by your ability to:

  • Deliver successful enterprise integrations and deployments.
  • Reduce customer time-to-production.
  • Build reliable and scalable ingestion solutions.
  • Improve customer adoption and technical satisfaction.
  • Resolve complex integration challenges efficiently.
  • Turn customer-specific requirements into reusable platform capabilities.
  • Contribute improvements that strengthen the scalability and flexibility of the core product.

This role works closely with the team to assign new claims, review coverage, evaluate facts, assess liability, manage subrogation and recovery activities, and support claim resolution in accordance with established best practices and client instructions. The Claims Team Leader also provides coaching, guidance, and development support to help strengthen team performance and consistency.

Duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Supervise a team of claims professionals.
  • Assign new claims and provide direction on reviewing policy information, conducting thorough investigations, and determining coverage obligations, as applicable to the line of business.
  • Maintain the diary system to ensure each file is reviewed at least every 90 days.
  • Provide coaching, feedback, and support to direct reports.
  • Develop, monitor, and communicate performance and productivity goals.
  • Review and share performance results, productivity metrics, and audit or quality review findings.
  • Work with claims professionals to ensure detailed 90-day claim summary reports are prepared and client updates are provided regarding investigations, potential settlement opportunities, claim denials, reservation of rights, and recommendations for claims review meetings.

  • Review claim progress and status with claims leadership and discuss issues, opportunities, next steps, and corrective actions as needed.
  • Prepare and submit unusual or potentially adverse exposures to claims leadership, including allegations of bad faith or unfair claim practices.
  • Support Claims Leadership in identifying and implementing improvements to claims handling procedures.
  • Partner with Partnership Leaders to support results, attend meetings, and participate in claim reviews.
  • Review and confirm that claims professionals have obtained appropriate releases, proofs of loss, or settlement agreements and issue company drafts for claim payments.
  • Maintain complete and accurate claim files, including notes, reports, photos, and supporting documentation.
  • Follow all company and regulatory compliance requirements.
  • 5 or more years of experience as a claims professional and/or in claims management, with specialized technical expertise in handling Accident and Health, Travel, or Business Interruption claims.

In this highly collaborative role, you will be at the center of multiple efforts that utilize hardware acceleration for machine learning and high-performance computing workloads hosted on Apple’s Private Cloud Compute Infrastructure and powering pivotal end-user experiences such as Apple Intelligence. You will be part of a team whose work spans across the stack, from firmware to the full stack of software and application services. You will work in a collaborative, fast-paced team, delving into areas across the software and services stack, with the goal of maximizing the operational capacity and efficiency for the platform.

title: Corrective Actions/Regulatory Engineer
description:
Job Summary

Join a team where your expertise directly supports the safe, secure, and compliant operation of a highly regulated nuclear facility. As a Regulatory Compliance Specialist, you will play a critical role in maintaining compliance with NRC, DOE, and TDEC requirements while partnering with leaders across the organization to drive continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence.

In this position, you will lead and support regulatory programs, corrective action initiatives, licensing activities, inspections, and compliance efforts that help ensure the site's continued success. This role offers the opportunity to work on complex regulatory challenges, collaborate with technical and operational teams, and make meaningful contributions to nuclear safety and regulatory performance.

What You Will Do

The Regulatory Compliance Specialist manages the site's Corrective Action Program by reviewing identified issues, assigning actions to appropriate personnel, and partnering with management teams to review and approve corrective actions prior to closure. The position also supports Nuclear Material Control and Accountability activities, including program maintenance, inventory assistance, and regulatory reporting to NMMSS. Root cause investigations are conducted to identify underlying issues and develop effective corrective actions that prevent recurrence.

This role independently plans, schedules, coordinates, and completes moderately complex regulatory assignments, including License Amendment Requests, responses to Notices of Violation (NOVs), and Event Reports. The specialist coordinates revisions to licensing basis documents, develops and manages regulatory schedules, monitors milestone progress, and tracks commitments, actions, and related tasks through the site's corrective action tracking system.

The successful candidate maintains regulatory records and correspondence within electronic document management systems and serves as a key point of contact during NRC, TDEC, and DOE inspections and site visits. Responsibilities include coordinating inspection activities, responding to requests for information, reviewing inspection results, and supporting timely resolution of regulatory matters.

This position maintains the site's controlled licensing documents and associated licensing basis materials, researches and interprets regulatory requirements, gathers and analyzes information related to regulatory initiatives, and assists in developing guidance to address licensing and compliance issues. The specialist works closely with the Regulatory Manager and cross-functional teams to ensure regulatory expectations are clearly understood and effectively implemented.

The role requires frequent collaboration with company personnel, contractors, and representatives from other company locations to support licensing and compliance activities with multi-site applicability. The Regulatory Compliance Specialist ensures technical reviews and organizational inputs meet policy, procedure, regulatory, safety, and quality requirements while maintaining appropriate levels of technical rigor and conservatism.

Additional responsibilities include preparing regulatory presentations and communications for NRC, TDEC, and DOE interactions, conducting regulatory reviews of site procedures, evaluating proposed site changes for licensing impacts, serving as a Site Technical Representative for contract support activities, and participating on teams, committees, and special projects. The position may assume managerial responsibilities during the absence of the Regulatory Manager and is expected to keep management informed of significant scope, schedule, or cost impacts affecting regulatory services. Occasional travel of up to 5% may be required.

We'd Love to Hear from Candidates With

  • Associate degree in Engineering, Applied Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent combination of education and technical experience.
  • Five (5) years of experience working in an NRC, DOE, TDEC, Military, or similarly regulated environment.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of regulatory requirements, policies, procedures, and practices associated with NRC, DOE, TDEC, or comparable regulatory agencies.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DOE "Q" Security Clearance.

A Successful Candidate Also Brings

  • Experience supporting NRC licensing activities under 10 CFR Part 70 or 10 CFR Part 76.
  • Previous experience working with TDEC licensing or regulatory programs.
  • Experience performing root cause investigations, corrective action management, or regulatory compliance oversight in a nuclear or highly regulated industry.
Pay
Estimated Starting Base Salary Range: $80,310- $113,123. This position is incentive eligible. Centrus considers several factors when extending job offers, including but not limited to candidates’ key skills, relevant work experience, and education/training/certifications. While the posted range reflects the anticipated hiring range for this position, compensation above the range may be considered for candidates with exceptional qualifications and directly relevant experience.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

This position will require a pre­-employment background check and a pre-employment drug test.

Centrus Energy and all subsidiaries shall abide by the applicable legal requirements. We prohibit discrimination against qualified individuals based on their status as protected veterans or individuals with disabilities and prohibit discrimination against all individuals based on their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or national origin.

This position requires the successful candidate to obtain and maintain a Q security clearance. Candidates for positions requiring a security clearance are required to be tested for the absence of any illegal drug as defined in 10 CFR 707.4 prior to an offer of employment being made. In addition, once employed, employees will become part of a random drug testing program and may also be tested in the event of any incident causing injury or causing damage to property, or if it is determined that there is a reasonable suspicion the employee is under the influence of drugs or alcohol. This position will require preemployment background check on the part of the Company and in order to receive a Q security clearance, a background investigation by the Federal government. title: Computational Geoscience Postdoctoral Research Associate
description:
Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a well-qualified Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Geoscience for the Department of Critical Minerals & Geothermal Energy in the Energy and Environment Science and Technology (EES&T) directorate. The researcher will develop reactive transport and fully coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical (THMC) reservoir models to forecast the long-term performance, sustainability, and power-generation potential of geothermal systems under alternative development and operating scenarios. The work will use FALCON/MOOSE or similar multiphysics tools and will integrate geologic, geochemical, geomechanical, well-log, field-monitoring, and laboratory datasets into calibrated reservoir models. Our team works a 9x80 schedule in Idaho Falls with every other Friday off.

The successful candidate will work within an interdisciplinary team of computational geoscientists, geochemists, geologists, reservoir engineers, and experimental researchers. The researcher will independently lead model development and analysis while coordinating closely with technical mentors, data providers, and experimental teams to ensure that simulations are physically defensible and useful for geothermal development decisions.

The candidate is expected to be a strong asset to our interdisciplinary R&D team and work effectively both independently and as a team member. The candidate must be self-motivated while also taking direction from mentors, project leads, and peers. The position entails writing scientific manuscripts for journal publication and presenting research results at national and international conferences and meetings.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop reactive-transport models that represent aqueous speciation, advection, diffusion, dispersion, mineral dissolution and precipitation, scaling risk, chemical evolution, and alteration of reservoir rocks.
  • Develop and apply fully coupled THMC reservoir models using FALCON/MOOSE or similar tools to represent fluid flow, heat transfer, geomechanical response, geochemical reactions, and evolving porosity, permeability, and fracture properties.
  • Integrate well logs, temperature and pressure measurements, lithologic descriptions, structural interpretations, field-monitoring data, fluid chemistry, mineralogy, and high-temperature fluid-rock experimental results into conceptual and numerical models.
  • Calibrate natural-state and operational models against laboratory and field observations; perform verification, validation, convergence testing, sensitivity analysis, uncertainty quantification, and parameter estimation.
  • Simulate reservoir response to injection, production, circulation, and stimulation strategies; compare development scenarios and assess thermal drawdown, injectivity, pressure evolution, chemical compatibility, scaling or precipitation, and long-term sustainability.
  • Estimate heat extraction and power-generation capacity across development scenarios, clearly documenting assumptions, limitations, and uncertainty.
  • Create reproducible computational workflows, manage model configuration and data provenance, use high-performance computing resources, and improve parallel performance where needed.
  • Communicate findings through technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, model documentation, and collaboration with internal and external research teams.

Required:

  • Ph.D. in computational geoscience, geoscience, geochemistry, geological engineering, petroleum engineering, mechanical engineering, applied mathematics, computational science, or a related discipline. Ph.D. requirements must be completed by the appointment start date and within the preceding three years.
  • Demonstrated experience developing numerical models of geothermal, subsurface, porous-media, or coupled multiphysics systems.
  • Working knowledge of thermal and multiphase or single-phase fluid flow in porous and fractured media, heat transfer, and reservoir-scale transport processes.
  • Experience with reactive transport and geochemistry, including aqueous speciation, thermodynamic data, kinetic rate laws, mineral dissolution and precipitation, and fluid-rock interaction.
  • Foundation in finite-element or finite-volume methods, nonlinear numerical solution techniques, and model verification, calibration, and validation.
  • Scientific programming experience in C++, Fortran, Python, MATLAB, or comparable languages, including development or adaptation of numerical modeling components and automated workflows.
  • Ability to analyze heterogeneous geologic and engineering datasets, quantify uncertainty, and translate simulation results into defensible conclusions about reservoir performance.
  • Demonstrated oral and published written communication skills in English and ability to conduct independent research within an interdisciplinary team.

The ideal candidate will possess:

  • Experience with FALCON and MOOSE modules such as PorousFlow, Geochemistry, Solid Mechanics, or related multiphysics capabilities.
  • Experience building calibrated geothermal reservoir models and forecasting long-term thermal, hydraulic, mechanical, chemical, or power-production performance.
  • Experience integrating well logs, pressure-transient or injectivity data, temperature surveys, structural models, laboratory measurements, and time-series monitoring data.
  • Experience with fracture and fracture-matrix representations, stress-dependent permeability, stimulation, or constitutive models for brittle geomaterials.
  • Experience evaluating scaling, precipitation, mineral alteration, fluid compatibility, or geochemical feedbacks on reservoir properties and well performance.
  • Experience with uncertainty quantification, inverse modeling, optimization, surrogate modeling, or probabilistic assessment of development scenarios.

description:
Full Time Pacemaker Clinic CV Tech is responsible for the technical management and monitoring of patients with implanted cardiac rhythm management devices, including pacemakers, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs), cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) devices, implantable loop recorders (ILRs), and remote monitoring systems. The technician performs device interrogations, assists with device programming under physician supervision, reviews remote transmissions, identifies clinical and technical issues, and collaborates with physicians, advanced practice providers, and nursing staff to ensure safe, high-quality patient care.

Essential Responsibilities

Device Management

  • Perform in-person and remote interrogations of implanted cardiac devices.
  • Collect, analyze, and document device data including battery status, lead integrity, sensing thresholds, pacing thresholds, and arrhythmia detection.
  • Assist electrophysiologists and advanced practice providers with device programming and optimization according to established protocols.
  • Troubleshoot device-related issues and communicate findings to providers.
  • Monitor and manage remote monitoring systems and patient transmissions.

Patient Care

  • Prepare patients for device evaluations and clinic visits.
  • Educate patients regarding device function, remote monitoring equipment, and follow-up requirements.
  • Respond appropriately to device alerts and notify providers of urgent findings.
  • Assist in coordinating patient follow-up appointments and diagnostic testing.

Documentation & Regulatory Compliance

  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation within the electronic medical record (EMR).
  • Ensure compliance with hospital, departmental, manufacturer, and regulatory requirements.
  • Enter and maintain device information within applicable databases and registries.
  • Support billing and coding documentation requirements for device interrogations and remote monitoring services.

Team Collaboration

  • Collaborate with electrophysiologists, cardiologists, APPs, nurses, and administrative staff.
  • Communicate critical findings and patient concerns promptly.
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives and department meetings.
  • Assist with training and orientation of staff as requested.

Education

  • High School Diploma and Graduate of CardioVascular Training program
  • Associate degree in Cardiovascular Technology, Allied Health, Electronics Technology, or related healthcare field required; Bachelor's degree preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in cardiac rhythm management, electrophysiology, cardiac device clinic, or related cardiovascular setting preferred.
  • Experience with remote monitoring platforms and device manufacturers preferred.

Certifications

Required or obtained within established timeframe:

  • Certified Cardiac Device Specialist (CCDS) through IBHRE preferred.
  • Cardiac Rhythm Device credentialing or equivalent certification preferred.
  • BLS certification required.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of cardiac anatomy, physiology, and electrophysiology.
  • Understanding of pacemaker, ICD, CRT, and implantable monitoring technologies.
  • Ability to interpret device diagnostics and cardiac rhythms.
  • Knowledge of remote patient monitoring systems.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and customer service skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and work independently.
  • Proficiency with EMR systems and Microsoft Office applications

title: Software Engineering Manager, AIML — LLM Inference Quality
description:
Apple is building the next generation of AI data center infrastructure to power large language model (LLM) services at scale. We are looking for a hands-on engineering manager to lead the team that owns the Quality, correctness, consistency, and stability of LLM inference in production.

Your team builds the automation frameworks, evaluation methodology, and qualification strategy that give Apple confidence in every model, prompt, serving stack, and infrastructure change before it reaches users. This is the safety net that lets Apple ship frontier AI quickly — without sacrificing quality, safety, or trust. We are seeking a deeply experienced manager who stays close to the technology to drive both the technical roadmap and the delivery of a high-performing team.

As a technical manager, you will lead a team of engineers spanning quality engineering, distributed systems, and applied ML evaluation. Your team qualifies LLM inference and output-correctness automation frameworks for large-scale AI data center deployment and platform validation — validating that outputs remain correct, consistent, and stable as models, weights, prompts, serving runtimes, quantization schemes, and accelerator hardware change underneath them.

You will stay close to architecture, design reviews, and trade-offs, and partner with ML engineers, inference/performance engineers, distributed systems teams, and platform teams across Cupertino, Seattle, and other sites. You will hire and grow engineers, shape the team's roadmap, define quality bars where none exist yet, and represent the team to senior leadership and partners. This role requires strong technical depth, exceptional people-management skills, and the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-paced environment — including the inherently non-deterministic, probabilistic nature of generative output.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in software and/or ML systems development, or equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years of engineering management experience, with a proven track record of delivering complex, large-scale projects across multiple teams or organizations.
  • Experience architecting test, qualification, or evaluation strategy for large-scale distributed systems — ideally ML serving or inference platforms.
  • Hands-on background in one or more compiled languages (C, C++, Objective-C, or Swift) and proficiency in a scripting language (e.g., Python).
  • Self-directed: the ability to drive a strategy or project from a simple idea to production, setting clear priorities and consistently delivering on schedule with measurable outcomes.
  • B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with machine learning and LLMs — common practical applications and frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, or comparable inference/serving stacks).
  • Familiarity with LLM serving and inference optimization (batching, KV-cache, quantization, speculative decoding, distributed/multi-accelerator serving) and GPU-accelerated software.
  • Experience using AI/LLMs to improve testing itself — test-case generation, defect detection, or reducing manual QA effort.
  • Experience with CI/CD, Kubernetes, containers, and cloud-native systems, and integrating automated evals into release pipelines.
  • Experience with observability and distributed tracing for ML systems (e.g., Splunk, Prometheus, Grafana, LangSmith, or similar) and monitoring for model drift.
  • Experience validating agentic workflows — tool-use, function-calling, and multi-turn coherence.
  • Track record of hiring, developing, and retaining strong engineers, and leading change across multiple sites.

title: Team Lead - Power System Analysis
description:
Introduction

The Northern Europe Power Grids service area within Energy Systems supports a wide range of stakeholders, including Electricity Transmission & Distribution utilities, industrial asset owners, OEMs, developers, investors, and regulators worldwide. As a key partner in the energy transition, we assist with advisory services in expanding and reinforcing grids while leveraging digital transformation.

Our service portfolio spans the entire value chain of onshore and offshore electric grids—from power system planning and transmission & distribution technology to asset management and digital system operations.

The Power System Analysis Team

The Power System Analysis team is part of the PSP-TDT department and consists of approximately 20 DNV employees, supported by contingent workers. The team brings together specialists across electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), high-voltage interference, earthing and electrical safety, power system studies, and grid code compliance. We work collaboratively across disciplines to help utilities, developers and industrial clients address complex challenges related to grid expansion, electrification and the energy transition.

Our strength lies in combining deep specialist expertise with a broader power-system perspective, creating an environment where colleagues can learn from each other, develop their expertise and deliver high-quality solutions for our clients.

Role: Team Lead – Power System Analysis

  • Lead, coach and develop the team, creating a culture of collaboration, accountability, technical excellence and high performance.
  • Foster a strong digital mindset and encourage innovation, digitalisation, automation and knowledge sharing within the team.
  • Take an active role in the professional development of team members, including competence development, career discussions, mentoring and succession planning.
  • Ensure effective resource and capacity management, balancing project delivery, competence development and business development activities.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of the team's technical disciplines and ensure that capabilities evolve in line with market developments, client needs and the energy transition.
  • Promote collaboration between specialists working in areas such as EMC, high-voltage interference, earthing, system studies and grid code compliance.
  • Support technical quality and consistency of the team's services and deliverables.
  • Work closely with Project Managers, Sales Managers and other technical teams to ensure the right expertise is deployed on projects and opportunities.
  • Support recruitment and onboarding of new colleagues and proactively identify future competence needs.
  • Contribute to the development of new and existing services and help translate technical capabilities into client value.
  • Support business development activities and contribute technical expertise to proposals and client discussions where appropriate
  • Contribute to the team's business performance by driving effective utilisation, resource deployment and alignment between market demand and team capabilities.

A career in DNV offers the opportunity to work with leading organisations on complex energy-transition challenges, alongside colleagues from a wide range of technical disciplines. You will be part of a purpose-driven organisation where technical expertise, collaboration and professional development are central to how we work.

  • Be Challenged: Work with leading utilities, OEMs, and industrial clients on complex projects.
  • Learn and Grow: Access to training, coaching, and global networks. We invest 5% of our revenue in R&D and strongly support competence development.
  • Make an Impact: Contribute to a safer, more sustainable energy future.
  • Be Inspired: Join a culture built on our values—caring, daring, and sharing.

DNV is an Equal Opportunity Employer and gives consideration for employment to qualified applicants without regard to gender, religion, race, national or ethnic origin, cultural background, social group, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, age or political opinion. Diversity is fundamental to our culture and we invite you to be part of this diversity.

To qualify for this position, we would like to see that you have:

  • A Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, Energy Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Strong professional experience within power systems engineering and consultancy.
  • Solid domain understanding in several areas relevant to the team's portfolio, such as power system studies, grid connection and grid code compliance, EMC, high-voltage interference, earthing, electrical safety or power quality.
  • Demonstrated people management and leadership experience, with a track record of coaching, developing and motivating technical professionals.
  • The ability to provide direction to highly experienced technical experts without needing to be the deepest specialist in every technical discipline.
  • A strong understanding of how technical consulting services translate into client value and business opportunities.
  • Experience working with clients and stakeholders in the electricity transmission, distribution, generation, industrial or energy-infrastructure sectors.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills and the ability to collaborate across technical and organisational boundaries.
  • A proactive and pragmatic mindset, with the ability to provide clarity and direction in a changing environment.

Security and compliance with statutory requirements in the countries in which we operate is essential for DNV. Background checks will be conducted on all final candidates as part of the offer process, in accordance with applicable country-specific laws and practices.

title: Senior Engineer Pipe Stress
description:
About Us

At Technip Energies, we are more than just a leading engineering and technology company — we are pioneers committed to shaping a sustainable future. With thousands of talented professionals worldwide, we deliver innovative solutions to real-world energy challenges while fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment.
Join us on a one-of-a-kind journey where you can take pride in being part of the solution for the benefit of our planet, people, and communities.

Position Summary

The Principal Engineer – Pipe Stress is responsible for performing and overseeing piping stress analysis to ensure designs meet applicable codes, standards, and operational requirements. This role supports project execution by developing stress analysis guidelines, reviewing technical deliverables, and ensuring safe and efficient piping system performance.

The position provides technical leadership across projects, including coordination with global teams, mentoring engineers, and supporting complex engineering studies. The Principal Engineer plays a key role in maintaining design integrity, resolving technical issues, and delivering compliant and high-quality engineering outputs.

Key Responsibilities

Functional Responsibilities

  • Perform stress analysis to ensure piping designs meet applicable codes, standards, and manufacturer requirements
  • Perform and review stress analysis of piping systems connected to rotating equipment such as pumps, compressors, heat exchangers, turbines, tanks, filters, and air coolers
  • Use Caesar II software for piping qualification in accordance with ASME codes, project standards, and specifications
  • Evaluate stress results including displacement stress range and pipe support loads
  • Perform finite element analysis (FEA) for special piping fittings to evaluate stress intensification factors (SIF) and fatigue
  • Perform dynamic modal analysis to assess natural frequencies and prevent vibration-related failures
  • Update and review existing stress analyses as required
  • Develop standards and guidelines for stress analysis on both general and project-specific levels
  • Coordinate piping documentation and resolve technical design issues with project teams
  • Review, approve, and seal engineering calculations and technical deliverables

Leadership / Management Responsibilities

  • Develop work-hour estimates, plans, and budgets for bids and project execution
  • Track and report project progress
  • Supervise and review work of piping engineers and designers, including global workshare teams (HVECs)
  • Mentor and guide team members on pipe stress analysis requirements and methodologies
  • Interface with project managers, engineering disciplines, and global offices
  • Provide technical leadership and direction for stress analysis activities

Compliance / Operational Responsibilities

  • Ensure compliance with applicable engineering codes, standards, and regulatory requirements
  • Ensure proper sealing of engineering documents in accordance with governing bodies
  • Support coordination with overseas offices and ensure consistency in engineering practices
  • Maintain quality, accuracy, and integrity of stress analysis deliverables

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Engineering
  • Minimum 5+ years of industry experience
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license in Texas and/or Louisiana, or with willingness to obtain, along with willingness to obtain additional registrations as required
  • Proficiency in Caesar II software
  • Experience with finite element analysis tools including FE Pipe, Nozzle Pro, FE Bend, FE SIF, and flange leakage analysis
  • Experience with SmartPlant Review (SPR) and/or Navisworks
  • Strong communication and presentation skills
  • Willingness to travel internationally to support workshare offices and project needs

Role Specific Knowledge & Skills

  • Expertise in piping stress analysis and code compliance (ASME)
  • Strong understanding of rotating equipment interface and piping system behavior
  • Knowledge of vibration analysis and fatigue considerations in piping systems
  • Ability to develop engineering standards and guidelines
  • Strong leadership, mentoring, and technical oversight capabilities

Work Conditions

  • May require travel to international workshare offices and project locations
  • Coordination with global engineering teams

Additional Information

  • No sponsorship or relocation assistance available.
  • Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

What’s next?

At Technip Energies, we prioritize internal applications and provide timely feedback to internal applicants. Our Recruiting Team screens and matches your skills, experience, and potential team fit against the role requirements. We ask for your patience as the team completes the volume of applications with a reasonable timeframe. You can check your application progress directly in PeopleConnect Recruiting.

Together, let’s be part of the solution!

title: Bluetooth/Thread Embedded Software Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
description:

We're looking for a highly motivated embedded software engineer to help turn new ideas into wireless features that make Apple products work better together.

  • Strong proficiency in C programming
  • Experience designing and developing embedded software for real-time operation on ARM processors
  • Working knowledge of Bluetooth/Thread protocols and standard

Preferred Qualifications

  • Excellent analytical and debugging skills, including experience with debuggers and protocol analyzers
  • Experience with chip/platform bring-up
  • Proven track record of shipping consumer products
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills in cross-functional team environments
  • Passion for solving complex engineering challenges and delivering exceptional user experience

title: VP, Corporate Development
description:
About the role

Riot is hiring a Vice President of Corporate Development to lead corporate M&A and structure the external capital that funds our data center development pipeline. You will originate, evaluate, and execute strategic transactions, and design the joint venture and equity structures that allow Riot to scale its powered land and data center portfolio efficiently.


This is a hands-on role for a dealmaker who can build the model, lead the negotiation, and present the recommendation to internal committees. Working closely with the executive team, finance, legal, and our site acquisition and development teams, you will turn strategy into signed transactions.


We have a strong preference for candidates based in or near our Irvine / Orange County, California or Denver, Colorado offices, but remote is possible for an exceptional candidate, with travel as transactions require.


What you'll do

  • Lead M&A execution. Source, evaluate, and execute acquisitions, divestitures, and strategic investments, managing each process from initial screening through diligence, negotiation, signing, and close.
  • Structure development capital. Design and negotiate joint ventures and project-level and preferred equity for Riot's data center developments, balancing cost of capital, control, and returns.
  • Engage capital partners. Build and manage relationships with infrastructure funds, private equity, institutional and sovereign investors, and investment banks, and run capital raising processes for individual projects and portfolios.
  • Own the analysis. Build and oversee valuation, returns, and scenario models, including DCF, comparables, and project-level waterfall analysis, to support every investment decision.
  • Run diligence. Coordinate financial, legal, tax, technical, and commercial diligence across internal teams and external advisors, surfacing the risks and value drivers that shape deal terms.
  • Present to leadership and the board. Prepare investment committee and board materials that deliver clear, defensible recommendations.
  • Partner cross-functionally. Work with finance, financing, accounting, tax, legal, site acquisition, development, and leasing to align transaction structures with Riot's development plans, financial reporting, and public company obligations.
  • Support integration. Help plan and execute post-close integration of acquired businesses and assets so deals deliver the value they were underwritten to create.
  • Track the market. Monitor digital infrastructure, power, and capital markets to identify strategic opportunities and capital partners.


What you'll bring

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field required.
  • 7+ years of experience in investment banking, private equity, infrastructure investing, or corporate development, with a track record leading M&A transactions from origination to close.
  • Hands-on experience structuring and negotiating joint ventures and third-party equity for real assets or infrastructure development.
  • Expert financial modeling and valuation skills, including DCF, returns, and JV waterfall analysis.
  • Strong command of transaction documents, including purchase agreements, JV and LLC agreements, and term sheets.
  • Proven ability to lead negotiations and manage outside counsel, bankers, and advisors.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including board-level materials, with the ability to operate independently in a fast-moving environment.

Bonus Points

  • Transaction experience in data centers, digital infrastructure, power, or energy.
  • Experience raising capital for development-stage projects or powered land.
  • MBA or CFA designation.


Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: $225,000 - $275,000 (commensurate with experience) + bonus + sign-on equity grant.
  • Long-Term Growth: Eligible to participate in Riot’s equity incentive programs and share in the success you help build.
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans.
  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.


Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

SRS Real Estate Partners is seeking a motivated and experienced Commercial Real Estate Broker – Debt & Equity to join our growing Capital Markets team. This individual will focus on originating, structuring, and executing debt and equity financing solutions for commercial real estate owners, developers, and investors.

The ideal candidate brings strong commercial real estate finance knowledge, established industry relationships, an entrepreneurial mindset, and a proven ability to generate new business. This role offers the opportunity to leverage SRS's national platform, collaborative culture, and extensive client relationships to grow a successful capital markets brokerage business. SRS offers competitive commission splits, unlimited upside potential, the industry's best marketing, research, and transaction tools and support, and optional health insurance benefits.

title: Psychology Fellow - Intervention Track
description:
Children's Nebraska is offering a Post-Doctoral Psychology Fellowship position!

The Behavioral Health & Wellness Center (BHWC) at Children’s Nebraska offers the full
spectrum of behavioral and mental health services to meet the growing needs of children and
adolescents in Nebraska and the Midwest. The outpatient department at BHWC is offering two
fellowship positions starting in August 2027.

Clinical Child Therapy & Intervention Track
The clinical child therapy and intervention fellow will have a primary focus on providing
intervention to youth and families. The fellow will have the opportunity to provide
services to youth and families in multiple settings, including: BHWC (outpatient, group,
PCIT), integrated primary care (Children’s Physicians’ offices), and school settings
(Westside Community Schools). Opportunities in assessment will be available to the
interested fellow. Fellows may also engage in shadowing opportunities in medical clinics
(consultation-liaison, cardiology, diabetes, asthma, developmental pediatrics, feeding &
growth) and the mental health partial hospitalization programs if desired.

Benefits:
The fellowship is a 12-month full-time position. Fellows work between the hours of 8:00AM to
5:00PM. Fellows will receive a competitive salary starting at $63,480 subject to the withholding
of taxes. A relocation stipend will be available. Fellows are also eligible for employee benefits,
including paid time-off, medical, dental, and vision insurance options and paid holidays. There
may be options to be hired on following completion of the fellowship.

Requirements:
Applicants must have completed their training in an APA or CPA accredited PhD or PsyD
program. Applicants must have completed a one-year APA accredited internship in
child/pediatric psychology. Applicants should have significant experience working with children,
adolescents, and their families in a clinical setting. Hiring is contingent upon official verification
of completion of all doctoral degree requirements through the graduate school conferring the
degree prior to starting the fellowship. Eligibility for licensure as a PLP in Nebraska is required,
and eligibility for licensure as an LMHP in the state of Nebraska is preferred.

How to Apply: Applications are due on February 1, 2027. You will need to provide
a cover letter, updated CV, and three letters of reference.

At Children’s, the region’s only full-service pediatric healthcare center, our people make us the very best for kids. Come cultivate your passion, purpose and professional development in an environment of excellence and inclusion, where team members are supported and deeply valued. Opportunities for career growth abound as we grow our services and spaces, including the cutting-edge Hubbard Center for Children. Join our highly engaged, caring team—and join us in providing brighter, healthier tomorrows for the children we serve.

A Brief Overview
Provides quality psychological evaluations, therapy, education and consultation to children, families in Behavioral Health at Children's Hospital, and in clinics, agencies, and the community as assigned. Establishes and maintains professional working relationships with hospital staff, physicians, community agencies, and professionals.

Education Qualifications

  • PhD or Psy.D., from an accredited school of psychology required, candidates that have completed their dissertation and all required course work will be considered. Required and

  • Completion of one year pre -doctoral clinical internship Required

Experience Qualifications

  • Previous experience utilizing psychotherapy techniques in a pediatric or medical environment Preferred

Skills and Abilities

  • Knowledge of psychological principles, child and adolescent development, inter-relational dynamics, individual and group behavior, and behavior modification techniques
  • Interpersonal skills necessary to communicate effectively with patients and families, physicians, and other clinical professionals to gather and exchange patient information.
  • Ability to concentrate and pay close attention to detail
  • Demonstrates knowledge and skill in providing age-appropriate care to children, adolescents, adults and families.


Licenses and Certifications

  • Provisional Mental Health Practitioner Current and valid Nebraska licensure (or eligibility) IA Upon Hire Required or
  • Provisional Mental Health Practitioner Current and valid Nebraska licensure (or eligibility) NE Upon Hire Required or
  • Mental Health Practitioner Licensed Mental Health Provider (LMHP) IA Upon Hire Required or
  • Mental Health Practitioner Licensed Mental Health Provider (LMHP) MO Upon Hire Required or

  • Provisional Licensed Psychologist NE Upon Hire Required

title: Nuclear Fuel Performance Postdoctoral Research Associate
description:
Idaho National Laboratory is seeking a well-qualified Postdoctoral Research Associate in nuclear, mechanical, civil, or a related engineering field for the Computational Mechanics and Materials Department. This postdoctoral researcher will focus on the analysis of nuclear fuels (TRISO, metallic fuels, oxide fuels, and/or advanced reactor fuels) and materials using the BISON finite element fuel performance code (https://mooseframework.inl.gov/bison/).

Our team works a 9x80 schedule located out of our Collaborative Computing Center facility with every other Friday off.

This postdoctoral researcher will be responsible for developing simulations and analysis capabilities that help push the boundaries of nuclear fuel research at and beyond INL. Research in this department includes a diverse set of projects ranging from development of multi-scale methods for constitutive properties to coupled thermo-mechanical analysis of experiments and reactor systems to uncertainty quantification of modeling tools using machine learning analysis.

The researcher is expected to contribute to some of these core research areas and demonstrate the impact of their work through peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations. This innovative researcher will participate in engineering projects that impact scientific challenges, tackling complex technological issues facing the nation.

Responsibilities Include:

  • Possess knowledge and/or completed coursework relevant to nuclear fuels and materials performance under irradiation
  • Perform engineering and scientific analyses for advanced fuel types using the BISON code.
  • Build good judgement in the application of finite-element analysis.
  • Write and contribute to scientific manuscripts for peer-reviewed journal publication and present research results at national (and international) conferences and meetings.
  • Participate in the development of plans for new research areas and proposals.
  • Provide peer review of related research internal and external to INL.
  • Possess an interest in developing new skills to apply to complex nuclear and material science-based models.
  • Become a strong asset to our interdisciplinary R&D team and work effectively both alone and as a team member.
  • Develop proficiency with scientific computing languages: C++, Python, git, MacOS/Linux, and LaTeX


Required:

  • PhD in Nuclear, Mechanical, Civil or comparable engineering disciplines.
  • PhD requirements must be completed by commencement of appointment and within the previous 5 years.

The ideal candidate will possess:

  • Demonstrated knowledge of fuel performance modeling techniques such as: numerical methods, constitutive modeling (ex. plasticity, creep, and fracture), and/or code/model-coupling strategies.
  • A strong background in material performance in nuclear environments.
  • A basic understanding of utilizing experimental measurements or code results to develop input conditions for finite-element analysis.
  • Experience in software development and code stewardship.
  • Excellent skills in communicating scientific results.
  • Advanced proficiency with scientific computing languages and object-oriented programming.


Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, bend, use hands to handle materials, manipulate tools, keyboard and type, reach with hands and arms, and operate job-related equipment. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Sufficient visual acuity and hearing capacity to perform the essential functions and interact with people is required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Job Information:

title: Head of Partnerships & Alliances
description:
Your Role at Nutrient…

We’re looking for a commercially minded builder to own every indirect route to market at Nutrient: resellers and distributors, referral and implementation partners, the Salesforce ISV relationship, and cloud marketplaces. You’ll report to our Chief Revenue Officer and sit inside the Sales team.

We’re moving hard towards AI, agentic document processing and consumption-based pricing, and that changes what a good partner looks like. This job is less about signing resellers to move license seats and more about getting Nutrient into the marketplaces, platforms and service partners where buyers already spend their money.

You’ll inherit a working foundation: about 30 signed partners across North America, EMEA and APAC, a live AppExchange listing and an AWS Marketplace listing about to go public. You’ll also inherit honest questions about which of those motions are worth keeping.

What You’ll Work On…

  • Set partner strategy each quarter: decide which motions Nutrient invests in, which it stops and which partners get real support, backed by partner-sourced revenue and pipeline
  • Build AWS Marketplace into a revenue channel through private offers and co-sell with AWS field teams, then lead the decision on our next listing
  • Own the Salesforce ISV relationship and AppExchange listing, and recruit Salesforce consultancies that resell or refer our Salesforce product
  • Recruit, contract, enable and manage resellers, distributors and referral partners across North America, EMEA and APAC
  • Negotiate partner agreements with Legal, set margins and tiers, and build a consumption-based commercial structure for OEM and embedded partners
  • Run the partner program end to end, from portal, onboarding and events to accurate partner reporting in Salesforce for the CRO and CFO

What You’ll Bring…

  • 7+ years in B2B software, with at least 4 building or running partner, channel or alliance programs
  • A record of partner-sourced revenue you can point to, not only partners signed
  • Hands-on experience with at least one cloud marketplace (AWS, Azure or Google Cloud), including private offers and co-sell with the provider’s field teams
  • Experience negotiating reseller, referral, distributor or OEM agreements alongside Legal
  • Fluency in Salesforce CRM, and comfort working across time zones with partners in EMEA and APAC
  • Nice to have: Salesforce ISV and AppExchange experience, a background selling developer tools, APIs or data-extraction products, consumption-based partner economics, or public sector sales

Who Thrives Here…

At Nutrient, we’re not just hiring for skills. We’re hiring for mindset. The people who thrive here are:

  • Collaborators: You work openly, listen actively, and put team success first.
  • Hungry Learners: Rapid learning fuels your progress and career growth.
  • Curious Thinkers: You dig into the “why,” valuing understanding over simply being right.
  • Self-Starters: You take action without waiting for direction, turning obstacles into opportunities.
  • Owners: You take responsibility for outcomes and always look for ways to improve what’s in your control.
  • Doers: You’re energized by progress and motivated to create meaningful impact.

Why You’ll Love Working Here…

At Nutrient, we build tools that reshape how businesses and developers work with documents. Our culture is centered on continuous growth and collaboration. Every team member has room to learn, innovate, and drive meaningful impact.

  • Own the whole channel: every indirect route to market sits with you, with a direct line to the CRO.
  • A market in motion: AI and consumption-based pricing are changing what a good partner looks like, and you’ll shape our answer.
  • Hybrid in Raleigh, NC: three days a week in our Raleigh office alongside the Sales team, with flexibility on the rest.
  • Mission-critical product: Nutrient’s platform is trusted by 15%+ of the Global 500 across 80+ countries.
  • Strong growth trajectory: having more than doubled revenue over the past three years, backed by Insight Partners.

Nutrient believes in equal opportunity. We employ people from many cultures and countries, celebrate diversity, and are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, skill sets, and perspectives. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, age, marital status, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other non-merit factor.

description:
The intern will lead a primary summer project on eCommerce Digital Experience & Product, combining competitive benchmarking, guest-journey research and available product data to identify prioritized opportunities across Browse, Search, Book, Manage Booking, eCommerce/SFCC and App. Working alongside Product Managers and cross-functional partners, the intern will help evaluate competitor capabilities, guest pain points, digital self-service opportunities, feature-adoption signals and emerging eCommerce or AI practices relevant to Princess.

description:
AgileEngine is an Inc. 5000 company that creates award-winning software for Fortune 500 brands and trailblazing startups across 17+ industries. We rank among the leaders in areas like application development and AI/ML, and our people-first culture has earned us multiple Best Place to Work awards.

WHY JOIN US

If you're looking for a place to grow, make an impact, and work with people who care, we'd love to meet you!

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to operate and improve a Snowflake-based enterprise data platform in a regulated healthcare environment.

MUST HAVES

  • 5+ years of professional experience in Data Engineering or Data Platform Engineering.
  • Strong hands‑on experience operating and developing solutions on Snowflake , including data-layer design, warehouse performance, access patterns, and production troubleshooting.
  • Advanced SQL skills and strong experience with dbt for transformation, testing, documentation, lineage, and controlled deployment.

  • Experience orchestrating and troubleshooting data workloads with Argo Workflows on Kubernetes , or comparable workflow‑orchestration technologies.
  • Proficiency in Python or a comparable language for data engineering, automation, and operational tooling.
  • Strong understanding of data modeling, pipeline dependencies, schema evolution, backfills, data validation, and production data quality.
  • Experience with observability, logging, alerting, and incident‑management practices for production data platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex incident resolution, perform root‑cause analysis, and convert findings into preventive improvements.

  • Experience with service‑management and change‑control tools such as Freshservice and Jira.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA, GDPR, FDA‑related controls, least‑privilege access, separation of duties, and audit‑ready operational practices.

  • Execute work through controlled incident, request, access, change, and release processes using established service‑management workflows.

title: Customer Communications Officer
description:
This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.

Job Title - Customer Communications Officer

Business Area/Directorate - Cladding Remediation Directorate

Location - Victoria Quay

Working Arrangement – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should aim to spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within Hybrid Working Policy

Grade - B1

Advert type - Level Transfer

Duration - Permanent

Eligibility - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from core SG only.

Sponsorship: Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

The Cladding Remediation Directorate is a new Directorate that has been established to lead the Scottish Government’s commitment to act decisively to protect lives by assessing and remediating medium and high rise multi-residential buildings with unsafe cladding and by holding developers to account for their commitments to residents and homeowners.

The ideal candidate will be someone who can demonstrate experience of working within a communications environment which was complex and fast paced and underwent significant public and parliamentary scrutiny.

For this key role we are looking for a person who is flexible, versatile, and can make sound decisions.

The Cladding Remediation Directorate is a new Directorate that has been established to lead the Scottish Government’s commitment to act decisively to protect lives by assessing and remediating medium and high rise multi-residential buildings with unsafe cladding and by holding developers to account for their commitments to residents and homeowners.

The ideal candidate will be someone who can demonstrate experience of working within a communications environment which was complex and fast paced and underwent significant public and parliamentary scrutiny.

For this key role we are looking for a person who is flexible, versatile, and can make sound decisions.

The post holder will support the Team Lead Customer Communications – B3 in providing daily oversight of the existing and future communications activity with stakeholders who receive funding from the Cladding Remediation Programme.

The post holder will need to be resilient and capable of operating autonomously and with other teams, but with the expectation of proactive information sharing to build and maintain trust with individuals and both internal and external financial processes.

Support and supervision will be provided by the C1 Team Lead for Operations and the B3 Team lead for Customer Communications.

This role sits within the overall cladding remediation programme with responsibilities for delivering high quality customer communications, support and building communications in terms of Single Building Assessment (SBA) commissioning, Delivery and design and remediation stages.

The postholder will input across several functions interfacing directly with developers, residents and homeowners primarily who live in buildings affected by problematic cladding.

The team consists of this post, and two more B1 Communications assistants, and one A4 Administration support officer. The team is line managed by a B3 team lead.

Responsibilities

  • Undertaking extensive stakeholder engagement with public sector, external organisations, communications representatives, and departments, ensuring activity is joined up via collaborative working. (20%)
  • Ensuring partnership activity is delivered inclusively and communications are accessible. (20%)
  • Lead the client/communication work stream for inflight buildings. Tasks will include monitoring and managing, the team Inbox; triaging emails to colleagues, responding to various types of correspondence, and providing contributions to FMQs and PQs. (25%)
  • Ensure there is accurate, quality/consistent messaging with internal and external stakeholders that support the wider programmes vision and values. (20%)
  • Provide overall support to the wider team by attending meetings with internal and external stakeholders including taking the secretariat roles as required. (10%)

  • Any add-hoc duties commensurate to your grade and role. (5%)

Success Profile

Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of behaviours, experience and technical criteria (if applicable) that candidates will be assessed on.

Technical / Professional Skills:

  • Insight

  • Ideas

  • Implementation

  • Impact

You can find out more about the skills required, here: Communications_competencies_framework.docx

Experience:

  • You may enter these roles with experience from within or outside of the civil service in a customer service or support role.

  • Communication skills and the ability to understand complex information and give clear explanations to customers are important.

  • Remaining calm in difficult situations and maintaining a professional manner.

Working pattern

This role is a permanent level transfer position.

This post is a full-time role, but we welcome applications from staff with different working patterns, proposed working patterns will be assessed against the business requirements for this post.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should aim to work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location. If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

Further Information

Further information about this opportunity is available from nicki.evans@gov.scot

How to Apply

Please submit an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 23:59pm on Monday 23 November.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service observing the Civil Service Code and working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.
